News.title: Blackpool Air Show 2026 schedule: Dates, display times and why the Red Arrows aren’t appearing
News.content:
THE Blackpool Air Show returns to the Lancashire coast for two action-packed days of aviation history and aerobatic stunt flying.

Hundreds of thousands of spectators are expected to line the famous promenade on Saturday, August 8, and Sunday, August 9, for the free annual event.



If you are planning a trip to the seafront, here is everything you need to know about the 2026 flying schedule, and why the Red Arrows won’t be appearing this year.

Why are the Red Arrows not at Blackpool Air Show 2026?

For the first time in several years, the RAF Red Arrows will be absent from the Blackpool lineup.



The iconic aerobatic display team was forced to pull out of the 2026 show following an extended international tour in North America, where the squadron performed across the United States to mark America’s 250th anniversary.

Although the team has returned to the UK, military guidelines mandate a compulsory crew stand-down period and extensive jet maintenance following long-distance trans-Atlantic deployments.



Post-tour crew rest and scheduled maintenance checks mean the team cannot fly at Blackpool this August.

Officials expect the Red Arrows to return to the Lancashire event in 2027.

Blackpool Air Show 2026 schedule and flying lineup

Despite the Red Arrows’ absence, organisers have put together a packed two-day schedule featuring high-speed military jets, historic warbirds, and civilian stunt pilots.

Flying displays are scheduled to take place during the afternoon on both the Saturday and Sunday, running from approximately 2pm until 5pm.



Taking top billing for the RAF is the Eurofighter Typhoon, which will deliver high-speed solo passes and tactical manoeuvres over the Irish Sea.

Aviation fans can also look forward to historic aerial passes from the Battle of Britain Memorial Flight (BBMF), featuring iconic WWII heritage aircraft including the Supermarine Spitfire, Hawker Hurricane, and Douglas C-47 Dakota.

The action in the sky continues with the British Army’s official parachute team, the Red Devils, who will execute precision formation drops down onto the beach.

Thrill-seekers will also witness daring aerobatics from the Aerosuperbatics Wingwalkers atop vintage biplanes, alongside Team Raven’s popular six-aircraft civilian formation display.

Rounding out the weekend are rare classic aircraft appearances, including a Cold War-era MiG-17 jet, a Republic P-47 Thunderbolt, and a North American P-51D Mustang.



For the full aircraft lineup and flying display timings, head to the official VisitBlackpool schedule.

Exact flight times remain subject to changes and weather conditions on the day.

Blackpool Air Show 2026 – key visitor information

The action takes place across the weekend of Saturday, August 8, and Sunday, August 9, 2026.

While aerial displays run throughout the afternoon until around 5pm, the Air Show Village on the promenade opens earlier at 10am.

Best of all, the event is 100% free to attend, with no advance tickets or bookings required.



Spectators looking for the ultimate vantage point should head to the main stretch of the Promenade between Central Pier and North Pier, with the central display point positioned directly off the Tower Festival Headland.

Getting to the seafront is straightforward by train, with Blackpool North station situated just a 10-minute walk from the display area.

Drivers can set their sat-nav to postcode FY1 4BJ, though car parks are expected to fill up very quickly on display days.

Visitors are strongly advised to arrive early in the morning or rely on local public transport.

News.title: Mystery as terrifying giant venomous lizard on the loose in Italy sparking hunt for aggressive beast with powerful bite
News.content:
THE BEAST OF BRESCIA Mystery as terrifying giant venomous lizard on the loose in Italy sparking hunt for aggressive beast with powerful bite

A MASSIVE lizard is on the loose in Italy sparking a major search operation for the aggressive beast.

The Papuan monitor – native to Indonesia and Papua New Guinea – was spotted over 7,000 miles away from home in Montichiari, a town near Brescia in Northern Italy.



A local farmhand took a photograph of the 5ft lizard on July 17, prompting a major search operation that has kept locals fearful for a month.

It is one of the longest lizards in the world growing up to 8ft in length and can weigh up to 90kg.



These “aggressive eaters” will devour anything, and even need a “full room” of space when they become adult-sized if they are kept in captivity, according to Chicago’s Exotic Animals Hospital.

Tracking the lizard involves the flying of drones kitted out with thermal cameras and night vision.

Authorities have also set up two cage traps filled with chicken to lure the beast into capture.

There were three reported sightings in the span of a fortnight.

Marco Togni, the mayor of Montichiari, told The Times: “I didn’t initially believe it could be true.

“But we have now verified the image and we can say that it’s absolutely real.”



The town’s council has also banned residents from walking and cycling in the area where it was seen, even telling farm hands to shut their cabin doors.

Papuan monitors, a relative of the Komodo dragon, have powerful razor-sharp claws making them extremely adept at climbing trees.

They can become aggressive when they are frightened or cornered, and even inflict venomous bites.



Their diet consists of feeding on things as small as eggs, rats, to bigger meals such as pigs, deer, and hunting dogs.

In New Guinea, local tribes believe that these lizards are evil spirits that “climb trees, walk upright, breathe fire, and kill men.”

However, it is not known to prey on humans despite the beast being carnivorous.

Social media has made the Mayor into a star with users posting AI-generated videos of a wildlife ranger chasing the lizard along a swimming pool.

Another spoof can see the ranger controlling a DJ set with the beast belting a dedicated song to the Mayor’s campaign, Beware of the Lizard.



He even posted these memes on his own social media page.

Togni said: “It’s a lot of fun and I showed support with a bit of humour, but it’s important to also maintain an official tone.

“The situation afflicting this town is serious.”

How the lizard travelled to the Italian countryside from that part of the world has left Mayor Togni scratching his head.

A suggestion could be that a resident must have been harbouring the monster illegally.



He said: “We don’t know how it got here.”

“It either escaped or was abandoned.”

Keeping and taming the Papuan monitor in Italy is illegal and it is also protected, which means you cannot kill it.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The hunt so far has remained unsuccessful with the venomous lizard still at large in the wild.

News.title: Women who nicked £5k of clothes & sunglasses in ‘staggering’ shoplifting spree at UK’s biggest designer outlet face jail
News.content:
FASHION CRIME Women who nicked £5k of clothes & sunglasses in ‘staggering’ shoplifting spree at UK’s biggest designer outlet face jail

THREE women nicked £5,500 worth of swag on a shoplifting spree while on a day out at the UK’s largest designer retail outlet.

Dollaresa Pauce, 27, Estera Stepane, 30, and Raksana Kleina, 24, stole sunglasses clothing, handbags and footwear on their “eye-watering” spree.



They drove 75 miles from their homes in the same town to Cheshire Oaks in Ellesmere Port, Cheshire.

They targeted Sunglasses Hut, Hugo Boss, Levis, Nike and Paul Costello which sell their brands at the 145 store complex on June 6.



Other shops looted by them included Dr Martens, Calvin Klein, French Connection and Coach Store.

The women were arrested after security staff at Cheshire Oaks called police when they spotted them attempting to escape with their stash of retail goodies into a waiting BMW 3-series.

The gang initially dropped some of the stolen items as they tried to run away from officers but were tracked down nearby.

Cops discovered a further stash of stolen items in the getaway BMW in a nearby Sainsbury’s car park.



Pauce, Stepane and Kleina stole £5,457 worth of items, including £1,936 worth of Sunglasses from Sunglasses Hut and £1,395 worth of clothing from Hugo Boss.

Some of the goods were recovered but a jacket belonging to Hugo Boss and jeans belonging to Levi’s were unable to be resold.

They had been damaged when the gang tried to remove the tags.

Kleina, who was driving the BMW, had no driving licence and was uninsured to drive the 155mph six-speed automatic.

At Chester Magistrates’ Court, Pauce, who came to the UK with her parents when she was 10 years old, pleaded guilty to nine offences of theft involving goods totalling £2,620.



Stepane admitted eight offences of theft relating to goods worth £1,999.

Getaway driver Kleina, 24, admitted five charges of theft relating to items worth £838 and to driving a BMW 3 series without a licence or insurance.

All were bailed but face up to 26 weeks jail under sentencing guidelines.



They were banned from entering Cheshire pending a further hearing at Sheffield next month.

Earlier Derryn Gibney, prosecuting, said: “On June 6, officers were called to Cheshire Oaks to reports of three females who had made off from Cheshire Oaks having stolen a large quantity of goods.

“The females ran away from the police. The women dropped a large amount of items which were later recovered by security and officers located the three females.

”One of the officers found a key to a BMW which was left in the car park of a nearby Sainsbury’s.

“‘A search was conducted and a large quantity of stolen goods was found from various shops in the Cheshire Oaks as outlined in the charges.



“There was some degree of planning and group activity on the part of the defendants.

“For Hugo Boss, there was a jacket which was recovered but no longer able to be resold. For Levi’s a pair of jeans had a tag removed and could not be resold.”

Pauce had a previous conviction for shoplifting from 2021.

Her solicitor Richard Sibeon said: “She is a single lady, a mother of two children, aged two and seven.

”She lives in Barnsley and has been in the UK for 18 years. She came with her parents who still live Barnsley and she was about 10 when she came to the UK.



“Clearly she has put herself in an awful amount of trouble coming together to Cheshire with two other young women.

“I always find the values of the items eye watering and staggering – £1,300 for instance for four pairs of sunglasses.

“‘Most of the items were recovered but some Hugo Boss goods were damaged because of the attempts to remove the security tag.”

Stepane did not attend the hearing as she was in Scotland preparing to fly back to Latvia for a family funeral.

Her lawyer Ava Seymour said: ”Her grandmother has passed away and she cares for her mother full time. She is struggling with her mental health.”



The court heard Kleina was due to be interviewed for a pre-sentence report but because of a lack of time the report had not been done. District Judge Ian Barnes ordered the background report in her case.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Located off Junction 10 of the M53, Cheshire Oaks is the largest outlet centre in the United Kingdom, with 145 stores.

It was hailed as the first designer outlet village in Europe when it opened in March 1995.

News.title: Schoolgirl, 11, dies at Scots river as emergency crews race to scene
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

RIVER HORROR Schoolgirl, 11, dies at Scots river as emergency crews race to scene

A SCHOOLGIRL has died after being found in the water near a Scots village.

Emergency crews were scrambled to Gore Glen Woodland Park in Midlothian yesterday afternoon.



They were called out to concerns for an 11-year-old girl in the area around 12.40pm.

A major search and rescue operation was launched to find the child.



Tragically, she was pronounced dead at the scene after her body was found in Gore Water near the village or Gorebridge around 4.25pm.

The discovery was made close to Shank Bridge near the village.

Police say the girl’s death is currently being treated as “unexplained”.

An investigation is currently underway to find out the full circumstances surrounding the tragedy.

A Police Scotland spokesperson said: “We were made aware of concern for an 11-year-old girl in the Gore Glen area, near Gorebridge around 12.40pm on Thursday, 6 August, 2026.

“The body of the girl was found in the Gore Water near to Shank Bridge around 4.25pm.



“She was pronounced dead at the scene and her family are aware.

“Her death is being treated as unexplained and enquiries are ongoing to establish the full circumstances.”

The Scottish Fire and Rescue Service and Scottish Ambulance Service have both been approached for comment.

News.title: Moment flip flop-wearing ‘dine & dasher’ sprints out city centre Chinese restaurant without paying as waiters chase him
News.content:
THIS is the moment a man in flip flops flees a family run Chinese restaurant without paying his bill, as waiters chase him down the street.

Noodle Alley in Manchester released CCTV footage of the brazen diner after he ditched his table on Tuesday.



Clad in black shorts, a black button up shirt and flip flops the customer can be seen standing up from his table and making his way to the door.

He confidently waves at a waitress before making his way out of the restaurant.



Noticing that he hasn’t paid, a member of staff drops a tray of dishes in her hands and gives chase.

The man notices he is being followed and bolts up a flight of stairs towards the street.

Video from outside the shop shows him charging off down the street, desperate to shake off his pursuers.

Seconds later the waitress emerges from the restaurant but gives up the chase as the man makes his way across the road.



The restaurant, on Faulkner Street, shared the footage with the caption: “Today, someone ran away from our restaurant without paying.

“This isn’t just about the money.

“Small independent businesses are already struggling with rising costs, and dealing with people who deliberately run away without paying makes it even harder.

“Every meal, every member of staff, and every genuine customer matters.

“Our team reacted immediately and tried to catch him, but he disappeared within seconds.



“We have a very clear CCTV image of the individual, and all the evidence has been passed to the relevant authorities.

“To everyone who chooses to support small independent businesses like ours, thank you.

“Your kindness and support help keep businesses like ours going.”

A member of staff told the Manchester Evening News: “I went to get some chicken legs for the restaurant and when I came back the staff told me one guy got up and ran out.

“So I went to look at the CCTV. He stayed a very short time. He came in, only had noodles and he sat in a booth, actually looking around the bar, waiting for a moment that he could run.



“He saw a family go up to pay and he probably thought it was the best moment.

“A member of staff got up after him to clean the table and then realised he hadn’t paid, so they chased him, but as soon as he got up the stairs he was running so fast, he was already off down the road.”

They added: “I know it’s not a lot of money, but it is hurtful. The effort we put in hoping for everybody to enjoy their meal and then we are being let down.

“This is not the first time it’s happened to us. We opened about three years ago and we’ve had other guests leave without paying.

“We are not like a fast food restaurant, we work very hard and it’s very competitive. I sacrifice my evenings to be at home with my daughter just to make sure we can do our business.



“It makes me sad, because Manchester is such a special place and most people here are very nice.

“I’ve lived in Manchester 26 years now. I came when I was doing university so I decided this was the perfect city. You don’t want things like this to ruin that, or the reputation of Manchester.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We could chase them, but it’s not worth the risk. You don’t know what’s going to happen next time, it could be dangerous. [Staff] did make the effort but he was really fast.”

Noodle Alley reported the incident to the Greater Manchester Police who have since confirmed they are investigating reports of a theft.

News.title: German airport worker KICKED ‘military-grade bomb carried by Russian drone to blow up jet loaded with ammo for Ukraine’
News.content:
A GERMAN airport worker stopped a potential disaster by booting a suspected Russian drone carrying a military-grade bomb out of the air.

The explosive-laden UAV was spotted over Leipzig airport and flew worryingly close to a fleet of Ukrainian aircraft loaded up with ammo.



Investigators have now revealed the drone was first seen by the south runway at the Leipzig/Halle Airport on August 4 at around 11.42pm.

It was hovering between two Ukrainian An-124 cargo planes which led to the workers rushing to try and bring it down.



One employee managed to get close enough so he could bravely kick the drone as it was flying near him, according to DPA, Germany‘s largest news agency.

Police deployed a bomb disposal robot to inspect the stricken drone and found it had been equipped with professional explosives and a detonator.



Germany’s Interior Minister, Alexander Dobrindt, praised the airport worker but said the drone crashing down to the ground could have had serious consequences.

He said a “ripped” detonator on the explosive package was the only thing that prevented the device from going off as it hit the tarmac.



If it had exploded then the blast could have not only injured those nearby but also set light to the aircraft, its fuel and the ammo inside.

Dobrindt said the drone’s explosive cargo points towards it being a failed hybrid attack potentially from “foreign powers”.

The close call came just before a landing plane struck a mystery flying object at the same airport in another major security alert.

Germany’s federal prosecutor has taken on the investigation, along with Nato representatives, into the suspected drone attack.

The Office of the Federal Prosecutor said the “serious attack likely targeted Germany’s transport and logistics infrastructure.”



The airport in Leipzig is the main base for Nato’s Strategic Airlift International Solution.

Putin ‘is prepared to take down a passenger jet in Europe’ THE explosive-laden drone found at a German airport shows Vladimir Putin is prepared to take down a European passenger jet, an expert has warned. Security expert Will Geddes said the terrifying breaches had “shaken fear across not only militaries and across the world, but also commercial airports”. And he warned the chilling ordeal proved that Putin is more than capable of using a drone to blow up a passenger plane in Europe. Geddes told The Sun: “It’s a disaster waiting to happen.” He added that the device could have been adapted to carry radioactive material or even a biological weapon. Geddes said: “The visible demonstration of the ability to get close to a cargo plane in an airport in Leipzig shows that if that had detonated… that would have had a drastic impact.” He also warned the West was lacking in the necessary countermeasures to defend against drones – a weakpoint which could leave Britain vulnerable. Read more here…

It is one of the main European hubs for delivering equipment to strengthen Nato’s eastern flank using a small fleet of Antonov cargo planes.

As opposition Green Party spokesman Konstantin von Notz said: “Should it transpire that a state is behind this action, this would constitute state terrorism directed against Germany and its citizens.”

German officials are yet to identify any suspects but several security experts and European ambassadors say it bears all the hallmarks of the Kremlin.



Kyiv’s ambassador to Germany Oleksii Makeiev said: “Who else could it be but Russia?“

Security expert Will Geddes told The Sun Putin is more than capable of using a drone to blow up a passenger plane in Europe.

Russia has already proved it is capable of taking down passenger jets in Europe.

In 2014, Malaysia Airlines flight MH17 was shot down with a Russian-made missile over eastern Ukraine, killing all 298 people on board.

Moscow was found responsible for the disaster which took place over the Donbas region while pro-Russian rebels were fighting Ukrainians.



European security agencies have been probing a series of incendiary devices concealed in parcels that caught fire in 2024.

Main suspect Vladimir Putin has been frequently accused of planting a parcel bomb on a flight headed to a depot in the UK.

Russia has denied any involvement in the 2024 incidents and the more recent overflights.

News.title: New hosepipe ban comes into force for 1.8MILLION people tomorrow with more areas affected
News.content:
A NEW hosepipe ban is set to come into force for around 1.8million Brits tomorrow, as vast parts of the country continue to face restrictions.

Half of England and the entirety of Wales are still battling drought conditions as a result of prolonged dry weather.

South West Water has announced a hosepipe ban from the early hours of tomorrow (August 8), with most of the south-West of England set to be impacted.



All customers across Devon, Cornwall, parts of Dorset, Somerset, and the Isles of Scilly will be affected as a result of prolonged dry weather.



Restrictions will come into force from 0.01am tomorrow, but customers have been urged to follow restrictions immediately to reserve water supplies.

There is already an active ban by South West Water across Mid Devon and parts of East Devon, but the new restrictions will impact even more customers.

Sam Bottomley, of South West Water said “exceptionally low rainfall” and “high demand during warmer weather” had provoked the decision to introduce restriction, alongside the ongoing drought status.



He continued: “Introducing a hosepipe ban is never a decision we take lightly, and we fully appreciate the inconvenience it will cause.

Full list of regions affected by South West Water's new hosepipe ban The restrictions will be enforced from 0.01am on Saturday, August 8 Devon

Cornwall

Parts of Dorset

Parts of Somerset

The Isles of Scilly

“However, these temporary restrictions are an important step in helping to protect our rivers and essential water supplies for homes, businesses and critical services across the region.”

South West Water has urged customers to use water resourcefully by taking shorter showers, turning off taps when brushing teeth, and only running washing machines and dishwashers with full loads.



Under a temporary use ban, customers cannot use a hosepipe, sprinkler, or pressure washer for various activities, such as watering plants or filling up hot tubs.

Anyone caught breaking these rules can face a £1,000 fine, unless an approved exemption or loophole is in place.

Drought conditions continue to impact half of England and the entirety of Wales, with nine water companies introducing bans for over 23million customers in recent months.

If your water supplier is affected, it is important to check their website to find out if your postcode has been impacted by temporary use bans.

News.title: Afghan ‘suitcase killer’ suspect ‘had issues’ with authority and would ‘feel sorry for himself’, adoptive family reveals
News.content:
THE Afghan boxer accused of killing a Brit woman in Athens had “issues with authority”, according to his “adoptive” parents.

An American couple who took in Sharif Ahmadzai, 26, a decade ago revealed the murder suspect would often feel “sorry for himself” during his rebellious teen years.



They shared their disbelief at the heinous crime Ahmadzai is accused of and the callous manner in which he stuffed the body of Elisabeth Ross in a suitcase before discarding it in a derelict building.

Ross, 38, a Scottish Christian missionary who was living in Athens volunteering for a charity was found on July 18 – just three days after she first went missing.



The US nationals told the Daily Mail they are heartbroken to learn of the alleged crimes of the teenager who had lived with them for almost two years.

The adoptive father said: “He had issues like everybody else does. There could be some trying times with him, but it was usually more rebellion against authority or just him feeling sorry for himself.”

He said the Ahmadzai he knew is not the same person today.

The couple say the accused murderer never showed any signs that he was capable of such brutal violence however did admit he had issues.



His wife mentioned that he would “act out” – though no more than a typical teenager – and noted that, like many refugees, Ahmadzai experienced “much trauma”.

The couple took in the Afghan boxer while undertaking humanitarian aid work at the Moria refugee camp in 2016 and the trio became so close Ahmadzai called the couple mom and dad.

He lived with the couple for two years until they returned to their home in Atlanta, Georgia, and they last saw him in 2019.



Ahmadzai’s adoptive mother reportedly sobbed upon hearing the charges saying it doesn’t feel real.

She said: “When I heard the news, I couldn’t imagine it to be true. Not in a million years.

“I keep thinking I’m gonna wake up and it was a nightmare, and it’s over.



“It’s a heartbreak that you can’t understand. It’s like I have the heart of a mother for that now adult-sized boy.”

Ahmadzai’s life story was previously told in an autobiographical animated video – and soon in an upcoming memoir – From Hell to Home: How Loss, Exile, and Hope Built the Man I Became.

He shared how his entire family were wiped out in Afghanistan.

He fled Kabul in 2016, embarking on a 45-day trek through Pakistan, Iran, and Turkey.



He survived two failed boat crossings before finally reaching Lesvos, Greece, and entering Moria Camp where he met the American couple.

Ahmadzai met his future wife American Christian missionary Alaina Hall, 28, who was volunteering with a relief charity in the camp.

The couple married in 2023 and set up a refugee charity together – where they are believed to have met another fellow Christian, Elisabeth Ross.

Ahmadzai’s wife allegedly reported her husband to cops after she became suspicious he was involved in Elisabeth’s death.



The brave wife gave a testimony after she became concerned about her husband’s actions.

Alaina last saw Scottish charity worker Elisabeth on July 12, leaving her alone with her husband, Ahmadzai.

Elisabeth was killed three days later, on July 15.

That night, Alaina woke up to find Ahmadzai gone.

Tracking his phone, she located him at Elisabeth’s apartment building.



He claimed he was just using her bathroom while he was out watching football.

When news broke of a body found in a nearby suitcase, Alaina suspected the victim was Elisabeth and her husband was the killer.

Alaina remembers Elisabeth as “a very pleasant and sweet person, kind-hearted, with a good soul”.

Ahmadzai denies murdering Elisabeth.

He exercised his right to silence at a Greek court on Thursday and did not respond ​to the charges, awaiting other evidence, his lawyer said.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The court ordered him to be held in jail pending trial.

The suspect has already admitted to putting Elisabeth’s body into a suitcase and taking her to the abandoned site.

News.title: 'I felt so judged when I used food banks — but I wasn't going to let my kids go hungry'
News.content:
'I felt so judged when I used food banks — but I wasn't going to let my kids go hungry'

Mum-of-two Meg Bonnie said she never thought she'd have to use a food bank as new figures showed families with young children were at higher risk of food poverty

View 3 Images Meg Bonnie, 21, said she had to turn to food banks when her children were younger (Image: Kennedy News/@meg_bxnnie)

A struggling mum has told how she resorted to food banks to feed her kids when they were younger after shocking new figures revealed the scale of child food poverty.

‌



Nearly one quarter (24%) of households with children under five in England experience food poverty, according to a report by the Education Policy Institute (EPI), with pre-schoolers facing higher levels of food insecurity than older children.

‌



Mum-of-two Meg Bonnie, from Nottingham, has been receiving Universal Credit since she turned 18 in 2023. The 21-year-old woman receives around £800 a month in benefits for her children - aged four and one - and has relied on food banks in the past to feed her family.

‌



View 3 Images Meg said the single-parent households like hers find it 'harder to manage a budget' (Image: Kennedy News/@meg_bxnnie)

Alarming stats show children under 5 suffer from food poverty as families forced to skip meals READ MORE :

Reacting to the damning new stats, she said: "It doesn't really surprise me. We've had to use the food bank a few times before or used the app Olio or Too Good To Go bags. There's definitely shame in going to the food bank. I felt quite heavily judged.

"It's a last resort for me. I've done it three times when my son was younger. I never thought I'd have to use a food bank. Food is just too expensive. My son will be on free school meals in September which I'm very grateful about. That will be a huge help."

‌



While it's now been a long time since she last needed help, Meg stressed that single-parent households like hers find it harder to manage a budget, especially during the summer holidays.

She said: "I think it's good during summer holidays that a lot of places kids can eat for free or a £1. We meal prep because I like to know what meals we are having and it helps with keeping a budget. I aim to spend between £50 and £70 a week on food.

"In the summer holidays, it tends to cost a bit more. I'd rather make a picnic than go out and buy food somewhere because I can't afford to be doing that multiple times a week. I've definitely noticed food prices have gone up. I used to spend between £30 and £40 a week when it was just me and my son.

‌



"Everything has gone up. I buy the shop's own version of things, I buy the long-life milk because it's 80p over £1.90."

View 3 Images Meg said she felt 'heavily judged' having to use a food bank (Image: Kennedy News/@meg_bxnnie)

The government has said its moves to lift the two-child benefits cap and provide more funding for nurseries will help reduce child poverty.

Article continues below

A government spokeswoman said: “No child can have the best start in life on an empty stomach. That’s why we are determined to reduce child poverty after years of rising hardship.

“We’ve removed the two-child limit, which will lift 450,000 children out of poverty, raised the national living wage, and put over £1billion into extending free school meals to every family on Universal Credit.

“For the youngest children we want to go further. We are consulting now on getting more funding directly to the nurseries and childminders supporting families on the lowest incomes, including help with the cost of food, and we want to hear from parents and providers before the consultation closes on 14 September.”

News.title: Royal Mail message to anyone posting cards in coloured envelopes
News.content:
Royal Mail message to anyone posting cards in coloured envelopes

Customers sending birthday cards and similar items might not be aware of the guidance

View 3 Images Customers should be careful when sending colourful envelopes (stock photo) (Image: Getty)

Royal Mail customers sending letters or cards in coloured envelopes might need to add an extra label to their post. While many people choose colourful envelopes for special occasions, such as birthdays and anniversaries, they might not realise that doing so could delay their post or cause problems during delivery.

‌



The postal service requires that customers write the send address 'clearly' on the front of their envelope to help ensure everything goes to the right place. The Royal Mail website explains: "It's important that the address shows up against the colour of your envelope."

‌



Customers can still use coloured envelopes, but it is advised to add a white label and write the address in black ink. According to Royal Mail advice, the address should go in the bottom-left corner of the envelope or parcel.

‌



When sending letters and parcels, customers might find the Royal Mail app helpful. Royal Mail says customers can use its app to track parcels, find drop-off points, and book redeliveries. The postal service said: "We’re always adding great new features and improvements to give the best Royal Mail experience on our app.

" Track deliveries: Receive instant push notification updates on progress of your deliveries. Send items: Buy postage in just a few simple steps, we can collect your items and bring the label or you can drop off. Get proof of posting. Tell us when you’ve posted an item and receive a digital certificate.

View 3 Images Birthday cards often come with coloured envelopes (stock photo) (Image: Getty)

‌



"Tell us your delivery preferences: Set a Safeplace for your items when you’re not in. Book a redelivery: We’ll automatically attempt delivery again the next working day, or you can book a redelivery on the app.

"Find your nearest drop off points: Find Postboxes, Lockers, Parcel Postboxes and shops (including Royal Mail Shops and Post Office branches)." More information is available on the Royal Mail website.

Royal Mail has also recently revamped its online experience for customers. In a Facebook update shared earlier this summer, the postal service told customers: "We've made it easier than ever to find and purchase the perfect postage option for your parcels.

Article continues below

View 3 Images Royal Mail shares advice for customers online (stock photo) (Image: Getty)

"Next time you're sending something, you'll now see the most popular options first. So, if you're in a hurry, you're only a few clicks away from getting your parcel ready to send. Simply tell us the size and weight of your parcel, how quickly you need it to be delivered, and if you need any extras such as tracking, guaranteed delivery, a photo on delivery, or a signature.

"We will then recommend the best postage services for you to choose from. Click on the postage option you want, and add a few extra details before adding to your basket. Easy."

News.title: UK trains cancelled: Commuters braced for Friday delays after power outage
News.content:
Travel chaos is expected on trains in northern England and the Midlands today after a major power outage in Manchester ground the network to a halt

Rail passengers are bracing for another day of travel chaos with a power outage bringing trains to a standstill across the Midlands and northwest of England.

Electricity cut out in the main control hub for north-west England’s railways, the Manchester Rail Operating Centre yesterday causing widespread cancellations and delays to services.

Trains are back running but they are "now in the wrong locations for the start of service today", said National Rail.

A statement from National Rail continued: "This means that some trains are still expected to be affected this morning. Trains across the Greater Manchester area and North West of England may still be cancelled in full or revised to only run for part of their normal journey until service is able to fully recover."

News.title: Fleabag's Sian Clifford on the Hollywood star that stopped her quitting 'hardest role of her life'
News.content:
Fleabag star Sian Clifford almost turned down her latest film role playing a fame hungry aristocrat vying to become the next Kim Kardashian - because she is chronically camera shy. Best known for playing Phoebe Waller-Bridge's uptight sister Claire in the hit BBC 3 comedy, her new film, Lady, released in cinemas on August 14, has been described as “Saltburn on magic mushrooms.”

Sian plays deluded Lady Isabella Ravenhyde, a celebrity-obsessed aristocrat, who lives alone in a sprawling 26-bedroom country manor and is searching for instant fame. The polar opposite to her real life personality, Sian, 44, says: "I am not like Lady Isabella at all. I would rather hide from everything. Definitely a camera. I have been told by every director I have ever worked with...that I physically turn away from the camera."

Shania Twain turned into £300m country music legend by very unexpected hit READ MORE :

She was persuaded to take the part by British actor Riz Ahmed, while she was working alongside him on his TV series Bait, which sees him play a young Pakistani actor trying to become the next James Bond.

View 5 Images Sian as Claire in Fleabag, with Pheobe Waller-Bridge (Image: BBC/Two Brothers/Luke Varley)

‌



Explaining how her anxiety kicked in, she says: "It was an immediate yes when I first got the script. I then met the director, Samuel Abrahams, and we went for a walk in Hyde Park, where we talked for hours and swapped ideas. I was so excited.

“But it started to get a bit closer and I got really really scared. I almost pulled out. I did not want to f*** it up. It was like nothing I had done before. My neurosis was getting in the way, telling me I could not do it. I was working with Riz Ahmed at the time and he said ‘you have got to do that film. You have got to roll the dice.’ So I was ‘yeah. Ok.’”

Of the 90 minute movie, made in 15 days, she says: "It was some of the hardest 15 days of my life, but we have made a really beautiful thing. I could not be more proud."

View 5 Images Riz Ahmed, the star of 2026 TV series, Bait (Image: Amazon MGM Studios)

‌



In Lady, Sian’s character rushes around her country estate in outrageous outfits, as she dupes a young film-maker, played by Laurie Kynaston, into thinking he is making a new Netflix documentary about her flamboyant life.

Meanwhile, Sian, who won a BAFTA for Best Female Comedy Performance in 2020 after Fleabag finished, thanks her friend Phoebe Waller-Bridge for her success.

The pair first met on the Tube, travelling home together from the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art (RADA). She says: "Phoebe and I went to drama school together. We have been very dear friends from the very first day. We always had a sort of fantasy to play sisters.”

View 5 Images Sian Clifford looking fabulous in the film Lady (Image: MetFilm)

‌



Despite being firm friends from the offset, Sian was forced to audition for her role in Fleabag and feared she would not land the part of Claire. She says: "I first encountered the script for Fleabag when Phoebe was developing it. She always had me in mind for Claire.

"But, for a long time, it looked like I wouldn’t be able to play her. The BBC were keen to get a profile attached for that part, because it was a new show and obviously with new shows they want there to be sparkly things in there to draw a new audience.

“But Phoebe was adamant. I had a horrible audition. I was just terrified. I remember just coming home that night and I messaged Phoebe and said, ‘listen, I know that was awful and I don’t mind if it doesn’t go my way.’

View 5 Images Andrew Scott, Phoebe Waller-Bridge, Sian Clifford, and Brett Gelman, winners of the Outstanding Comedy Series award for Fleabag at the Emmys in 2019 (Image: WireImage)

‌



“I can’t remember how quickly I found out, but the BBC were wonderful and said, ‘So sorry. We absolutely get it now. Yes, we’d love you to play Claire.’”

Of Fleabag and Phoebe, Sian says: “Phoebe is just magical. She is also a composer. I mean, the script is watertight. That is the one script that for me is the holy grail, and I will honour every single dot and cough, because it is perfect, when you read it.”

Sian also feels proud that Fleabag tackled difficult issues, such as Claire’s miscarriage. She says: "The miscarriage story was based on something that happened to a friend of Phoebe’s. I just think it’s so, so important. Miscarriage is unbelievably common and people don’t know that, because it’s not spoken about.

"So, if we in any way have contributed to the beginning of a conversation that will take down that taboo, then I am honoured to be a part of something that did that.”

‌



*Lady is released in cinemas August 14.

News.title: Met Office names areas facing heavy rain on Saturday – downpours in 20 counties
News.content:
Met Office names areas facing heavy rain on Saturday – downpours in 20 counties

Met Office weather forecasters say temperatures should rise above 30C in some parts of the UK this weekend, but other regions could see 10cm of rainfall

UK weather: Met Office forecasts slightly milder temperatures

The Met Office says some parts of the UK could see as much as 10cm of rainfall over this weekend.

‌



Despite temperatures climbing over the next few days - with the mercury possibly hitting 32C in southern areas on Sunday - outbreaks of rain are expected in northern areas, particularly Scotland and Northern Ireland.

‌



People in Scotland and Northern Ireland can expect “outbreaks of heavy rain through the day” on Saturday, the Met Office says, while it will remain “dry” with “sunny spells” for most of England and Wales.

‌



The north-west of Scotland will see the most rain over the weekend. “Some locations could receive over 75mm, with a few exposed upland areas potentially exceeding 100mm in 48 hours by early Sunday,” the national weather agency says.

The BBC Weather forecast paints a similar picture, with “blustery rain for much of Scotland and Northern Ireland” on the cards tomorrow.

‌



It states: “A dry and sunny day for much of the UK tomorrow with some patchy cloud at times. Staying windier in the far north with spells of blustery rain for much of Scotland and Northern Ireland.

“Staying unsettled and wet across northern and central areas on Sunday, but drier and sunnier in the south with only the odd afternoon shower. Monday looks to see any showers in the north gradually ease. It will then be a dry and settled day with sunshine for most.“

Heatwave to come next week

Yet another heatwave is expected to come next week. The Met Office says temperatures should surpass 30C on Sunday, Monday and Tuesday in southern regions - thus meeting the heatwave threshold.

Article continues below

An official heatwave is declared when temperatures hit the ‘heatwave threshold’ three days in a row. The threshold stands at 28C in the south-east, where conditions tend to be warmer, and drops to 25C the further away from the south-east you go.

News.title: New Lidl six-in-one gadget kit with multiple uses coming to stores on Thursday
News.content:
New Lidl six-in-one gadget kit with multiple uses coming to stores on Thursday

Shoppers will be able to get their hands on the new product in just a few days

View 2 Images Many shoppers look forward to Lidl's Middle Aisle Special Buy updates (Image: Getty)

Lidl fans will be pleased to hear that a brand new batch of products will be landing in stores next week. The budget supermarket is popular with many shoppers for its famous 'Middle Aisle'.

‌



Every Thursday and Sunday, Lidl updates its Middle Aisle Special Buy offerings with new stock. However, once they're gone, they're gone, as Lidl says, so customers will need to act fast to get their hands on any of the new items. Next Thursday, August 13, Lidl will be bringing out a gadget that can be used in multiple ways.

‌



The gadget is Philips' All-in-One Trimmer. It will be available for £19.99. The exact same trimmer is available on the official Philips website for £22.99, making Lidl's option a budget-friendly deal.

‌



Lidl says the trimmer comes with a two-year warranty and various accessories, each with a different use. The six accessories include:

Comfort blades Nose and ear trimmer 1mm stubble comb 3mm beard comb 5mm beard comb 12mm hair comb

In the product description, Lidl says: "This 6-in-1 trimmer from Philips has self-sharpening, skin-friendly blades for smooth, precision grooming." The battery has a run time of 60 minutes, with a battery indicator that'll show when more charge is needed. Lidl also says that the blades are washable.

‌



View 2 Images Philips' All-in-One Trimmer can be used in different ways thanks to its six accessories (Image: Lidl)

What other electronic gadgets is Lidl bringing out?

In addition to the trimmer, Lidl will introduce various other gadgets and tools to its Special Buy range next week. For instance, shoppers will also be able to get the Cien Beauty Ionic Hair Dryer for £11.99.

In the product description, Lidl says: "Long-lasting ionic technology for natural shine, silky smooth hair, faster drying and reduced static build-up. Low-noise DC motor. Three temperature settings and two speed settings for versatile styling.

‌



"Cool shot function to lock your hairstyle in place for a long-lasting look. Slim styling nozzle for precision styling and optimal heat distribution. Diffuser for extra body and volume, plus beautiful natural curls. Overheat protection for safety. Removable and easy-to-clean air filter. Practical hanging loop for easy storage."

Another option is the £9.99 Cien Illuminated Make-Up Mirror. The mirror comes with dimmable LED lights, an on/off switch, and a one-touch dimmer control. The back mirror provides 5x magnification, and the mirror head rotates 360 degrees.

Article continues below

For anyone looking to upgrade their home lighting, Lidl will also start selling the Livarno LED Black Floor Lamp for £14.99. Lidl says: " Pleasant, glare-free lighting for crafting, reading or working. Flexible gooseneck for adjustable positioning. Energy-saving and long-life LED module with warm white light. Four-stage touch dimmer on the lamp head."

News.title: Sports Direct billionaire Mike Ashley claims Harvey Nichols in 'death spiral' and would be 'huge challenge'
News.content:
Sports Direct billionaire Mike Ashley claims Harvey Nichols in 'death spiral' and would be 'huge challenge'

Self-made tycoon Mike Ashley has revealed his interest in snapping-up struggling luxury department store Harvey Nichols after its current owner put it up for sale following head office job cuts

View 4 Images Mike Ashley insists 'I don’t buy things to close them down' amid interest in Harvey Nichols sale (Image: PA Archive/PA Images)

Billionaire Mike Ashley - who has emerged as an unlikely buyer for posh department store Harvey Nichols - claims it is in a “death spiral” and turning around business would be a “huge challenge”.

‌



The Sport Direct tycoon, who has a long history of buying struggling retailers, has indicated his interest in snapping-up Harvey Nichols after its current owner put it up for sale. The luxury department store, heavily mentioned in BBC sitcom Absolutely Fabulous starring Jennifer Saunders and Joanna Lumley, has suffered several years of losses.

‌



As well as its famous flagship branch in London’s Knightsbridge, it also has stores in Leeds, Birmingham, Edinburgh, Manchester, Dublin and Bristol. It announced a major shake-up of its operations two years ago, resulting in dozens of job cuts at its head office.

‌



View 4 Images Famous department store Harvey Nichols has been put up for sale after several years of losses (Image: Getty Images)

Tycoon Mike Ashley buys two entire shopping outlets with 7.8 million visitors READ MORE :

Self-made tycoon Mr Ashley’s Frasers Group is seen as a possible buyer along with, it has been reported, fashion giant Next. The maverick businessmen gave an insight into his thoughts in an interview with the Financial Times, telling the newspaper he expected Harvey Nichols to be sold for less than £40million.

View 4 Images Harvey Nichols shot to wider acclaim in 90s sitcom Absolutely Fabulous (Image: BBC)

‌



“We are more likely to overpay . . . It’s more of a natural fit so we can pay more,” he said, while adding he “wouldn’t be crying a river” if Frasers loses the auction “and I don’t think Next would be either". He added: “I don’t think I’ll be writing a huge cheque, because you’ve got to think about the future losses. If it was a little bit tough before, it is in a death spiral now.”

If Frasers were to succeed, Mr Ashley told the FT he would be inclined to keep the retailer’s flagship store in London’s Knightsbridge and its store in Edinburgh trading under the Harvey Nichols brand. However, he said some of its other stores would be rebranded as either House of Fraser or Flannels, both of which are owned by Frasers.

View 4 Images Mike Ashley is believed to be competing with Next for upmarket department store Harvey Nichols (Image: Getty Images)

Article continues below

There were about 60 House of Fraser stores when Mr Ashley bought House of Fraser for £90million in 2018, where as there are now just 20.

“These department store buildings are so expensive to maintain,” Mr Ashley told the FT. “ If even John Lewis is struggling, it shows how tough it is. I don’t buy things to close them down. I don’t lose money for no reason,” he added.

Another part of his empire is Lillywhites, the historic sports store on London’s Piccadilly Circus, which he bought for £11.5million in 2002.

News.title: 'My son died after rare disease - nobody nows how he got it'
News.content:
'My son died after rare disease - nobody nows how he got it'

Doctors were baffled when super-fit Liam Exley started developing “gunky” fluid on his lungs at 17 years of age

View 4 Images Liam Exley was “as fit as anything” until he started developing fluid on his lungs at age 17 (Image: Cover Images)

A mother who lost her son to a rare disease aged just 20 says years of misdiagnosis meant it was found too late. Liam Exley was “as fit as anything” before he fell ill and died of asbestos-related cancer.

‌



He started developing “gunky” fluid on his lungs at age 17 back in 2021. He had various procedures to drain it and doctors at King's Lynn’s Queen Elizabeth Hospital (QEH) said he had pericarditis, the swelling of the tissue around his heart. They prescribed an anti-inflammatory called Colchicine, and Liam continued to be in and out of hospital having fluid drained, including an eight-day stay in October 2023.

‌



A few months later a lymph nodes on the side of his neck had swollen “like a golf ball” and a biopsy confirmed he had stage four mesothelioma - a rare and aggressive type of cancer caused by asbestos fibres. “When they turned around and told all of us that he had terminal cancer, I rushed out and was sick,” his mother Nicola Anderson said. “I just couldn’t believe it.”

‌



After six months of battling, Liam died at home, aged 20. Nicola said: “He got up, and I said, ‘What are you doing?’ He said he wanted to go to the toilet, and as he sat down his eyes were going.

View 4 Images Liam Exley growing up with his family (Image: Cover Images)

“I just picked him up - it was mother’s instinct. I thought it was his oxygen lead trapped - but his eyes were flickering, and I said, ‘I’ve got you sweetheart’ and he just closed his eyes in my arms.”

‌



Mesothelioma UK says that symptoms of the disease include the accumulation of a sticky recurring fluid in the lungs called pleural effusion. Ms Anderson, from Swaffham, in Norfolk, believes that this is what Liam had been experiencing for the years before his diagnosis, and had doctors realised it sooner, it may not have gotten to stage four so quickly.

While the disease cannot be cured, it can be managed to slow its growth and help patients live longer. Most people who develop the cancer are over 65, as they are individuals who had worked in high-risk trades during their younger years where there was less protection against asbestos exposure. However, how Liam developed it is not known.

It is considered to be extremely rare for young people - and Liam is the second youngest in the UK to have died from it. Ms Anderson believes that this may have contributed to his late diagnosis. The QEH has said it does not comment on individual cases.

‌



While the disease cannot be cured, it can be managed to slow its growth and help patients live longer. Now Liam’s mother is raising funds and awareness of mesothelioma to not only help people recognise the symptoms - but also support treatments for others.

“Liam was the light in the life of everyone lucky enough to know him - happy, kind, loving, intelligent and funny,” she said. “Having finished his schooling, he was completing his carpentry apprenticeship with Flagship Housing - well on his way to qualifying as a kitchen fitter.

“He was an incredibly talented sportsman, football and cricket being two of his main passions. He was still playing cricket the summer before he passed away, scoring 87 runs not out in his last match.

‌



View 4 Images Liam loved football and cricket (Image: Cover Images)

“Constantly looking forward, he was planning his future with friends and family, places he was going to go, and things he was going to do. Full of boundless love and energy, there was never a dull moment when Liam was around.

“Losing a child is something no parent should ever have to experience, and what an incredibly overwhelming time it has been,” Ms Anderson said. "Just like Liam, I won’t give up. I can do brave things, and I am determined to share Liam’s story, to raise awareness, and to help advocate for others.

‌



“I want to continue to make Liam proud. His fight was never in vain, and his story will continue to improve things for everyone who has to fight the same fight after him.”

Over the weekend, Ms Anderson successfully climbed Snowdon, the highest mountain in England and Wales, in memory of her son.

View 4 Images Nicola climbed Snowdon over the weekend in Liam's memory (Image: Cover Images)

‌



“It took me under four hours. It was quite hard at the end - but I got through it,” she said. “It was hard work, and it was freezing cold; I couldn’t even feel my fingers - but you just go with your heart anyway. I just had to do it.”

Liam’s brother Harry and his uncle Wayne will also be holding a charity match at Swaffham Town Football Club on Sunday, August 23. It was a tradition started by Liam himself while he was battling cancer in 2024.

Gates open at 12pm for a 1pm kick-off. Donations can be made to Mesothelioma UK and the Addenbrooke’s Teenage Cancer Trust’s C9 Unit upon entry. There will also be a bouncy castle, an auction, ice cream and food.

News.title: Officer who led PC Harper investigation 'appalled' killers could be released early
News.content:
Speaking to BBC Breakfast on Friday, former Det Sup Blaik, who led the Thames Valley Police investigation, pointed to remarks by the judge who sentenced PC Harper's killers. Mr Justice Edis referred to their case of manslaughter as being "very close to a case of murder in its seriousness".

The former officer called for prisoners who were judged to have had a high level of culpability for a manslaughter offence to be excluded from the scheme.

Allowing them to walk free would "undermine" the judicial process and impact police morale, Blaik said, before urging the government to have a "long, hard think" about the case.

The former Det Sup left Thames Valley Police in 2023. This is the first time he has publicly shared his views on the issue.

In an earlier statement given exclusively to BBC Breakfast, he said "like many people across the country" he was "deeply concerned and appalled" by the prospect of Bowers and Cole being considered for early release.

He said that because the "death of Andrew was such a serious and tragic case", Bowers and Coles should "not be afforded the opportunity" to be released early.

"Neither of them showed any remorse during their time in police custody or during their subsequent trial.

"I hope the Government takes account of the strength of public feeling on this issue, which has been both clear and widespread," he added.

Under revised plans announced by the government on Monday, prisoners who have committed rape, grooming, and serious child sex offences will be excluded from an early release scheme for England and Wales.

But those guilty of manslaughter may still be eligible.

Bowers and Cole were sentenced to 13 years for the manslaughter of PC Harper.

They will become eligible for release from prison after serving half of their sentences under the plans, instead of two-thirds.

The driver of the getaway car, Henry Long, was jailed for 16 years for the same offence. But Long will not be eligible.

News.title: England footballer Toney charged with assault in Soho
News.content:
England footballer Ivan Toney has been charged with assault at a nightclub in central London.

The 30-year-old, who plays for Saudi Pro League club Al-Ahli, was charged on 31 July following an incident on Wardour Street in Soho on 6 December.

The former Brentford striker, who started England's 6-4 win over France in the "bronze final" of the World Cup last month, has been charged with assault causing actual bodily harm and is due to appear at Westminster Magistrates' Court on 24 September.

A spokesperson for Toney said: "Ivan acknowledges the charge and although he is naturally shocked, he looks forward to being given the opportunity to clear his name in court."

After starting his career at Northampton Town, the striker had permanent spells at Newcastle, Peterborough and Brentford before moving to Saudia Arabia in 2024.

He was a surprise selection for England's World Cup squad but apart from the France game, his only other appearance was as a late substitute in the 2-1 semi-final defeat to Argentina.

News.title: Arrests in Norfolk town as disorder continues for third night
News.content:
More arrests have been made over disorder linked to anti-immigration protests that saw crowds attempt to storm the homes of suspected asylum seekers and a police officer "seriously bitten".

On Thursday, asylum seekers were removed from properties in Thetford, Norfolk, for their own safety, Norfolk Police said.

Two men in their 40s were arrested as protests in the market town continued for a third night, bringing the total number held to five.

On Tuesday and Wednesday evenings, protesters attempted to enter homes where they believed asylum seekers were living and on Wednesday officers were also "subjected to significant aggression".

Witnesses reported rocks and eggs being thrown and chants of "we want them out" during protests on Clover Way involving up to 200 people on Wednesday night.

A male officer was struck with a rock and a female officer was seriously bitten, breaking the skin, the force said.

News.title: How a diary entry solved the murder of a missing man
News.content:
When Det Con Tom Ryan came across a diary entry about an old cattle trailer in July 2025, he knew he had finally solved the murder of a man who had disappeared six years earlier.

Richard Dyson vanished without trace in November 2019. He was last seen alive on 17 November that year and was reported missing eight days later when he failed to meet his daughter, Bethany.

"He was by all accounts a very good father, and he was regularly in contact with his daughter Bethany who was, I believe, 19 at the time of his disappearance. It was totally out of character," Ryan recalled.

"It was clear that he had disappeared off the face of the Earth."

Richard, who was 55 at the time, had been living in his car at Parkside Cottage on Christopher Wright's farm on Sheffield Road in Barnsley, helping with small jobs around the farm.

The farm was searched, but other than a collection of illegal weapons belonging to Wright, nothing more unusual was found and there was no sign of Richard.

His phone, however, showed it had never left the farm.

Police believed from the outset that Richard had been killed and that Wright and his childhood friend, Karl Schwalbe, were responsible, according to Ryan.

"We very much suspected their involvement, but without a body it's very difficult to prove murder," he said.

On 28 July, Wright, 73, and Schwalbe, 72, were convicted for their roles in Richard's disappearance and murder, ending a six-year wait for answers for Richard's family.

At a sentencing hearing at Sheffield Crown Court on Thursday, Wright was jailed for 35 years for murder and Schwalbe was given a three-year sentence for perverting the course of justice.

But how did police finally catch them?

News.title: Mexico break ranks to join Argentina in backing Infantino
News.content:
However, Conmebol did "express its concern about the repeated unilateral actions taken without resorting to dialogue or the institutional mechanisms provided for dealing with this type of situation".

Meanwhile, the football association of 2026 World Cup runners-up Argentina praised Infantino for recognising and apologising for his "errors".

It described his decade-long tenure as Fifa president as "centred on the development of soccer worldwide and institutional strength based on a clear, stable, and transparent governance model".

Infantino is unanimously backed by the Confederation of African Football (CAF), but faces opposition from European football's governing Uefa and Concacaf.

European teams could still boycott the World Cup as Uefa said its conditions had not been met, despite Infantino's plan being aborted.

"Assurances have to be made that such attempts to disfigure the game in this way will never be made again," a Uefa statement read.

"These conditions have not been met."

Uefa has already said it has lost confidence in Infantino, calling the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal a "shabby, back room, opaque deal".

The English FA has sent a letter withdrawing its support for Infantino, while Wales, Albania and Croatia are among other individual associations to have turned their back on the 56-year-old.

Concacaf described Infantino's proposal as "a symptom of leadership that has stopped putting football first", and that "this recent unilateral and egregious act of poor governance and leadership follows a pattern of missteps and similar behaviour".

However, unlike Uefa, it did not go as far as to say it had lost confidence in the Fifa president.

Before Infantino withdrew his proposal, the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) said it stood "in solidarity" with Uefa and Concacaf in opposition to the plans.

News.title: Could Russia be involved in German airport drone-bomb?
News.content:
A previous Russian-backed plot involving Leipzig airport could provide clues.

In 2024, a parcel containing a sophisticated incendiary device caught fire at the airport's DHL hub shortly before it was loaded onto a plane. Similar packages then ignited in the UK and Poland, causing extensive damage.

A group of men are currently on trial in both Lithuania and Poland, where prosecutors believe they were part of a substantial network of proxies recruited by Russian military intelligence.

But there was a subplot that has been little discussed before.

Last September, Lithuanian prosecutors said that investigators had also seized RDX explosives meant for "other terrorist attacks". The amount was significant: equivalent to 6kg of TNT.

"Some of the devices were manufactured to intensify the blast," the prosecutor added.

The BBC has since had access to case documents that describe how several of the men on trial were paid to transport those explosives around Europe, concealed in cans of sweetcorn and chopped tomatoes. The detonators were hidden inside headphone sets.

The suspects also handled drone parts and the case talks specifically of attachments, suitable for holding a bomb.

Prosecutors allege that some of the items were brought into the EU from the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad.

Almost two dozen suspects have been charged with terror offences, but with the men's handlers still at large, believed to be in Russia, it is not clear whether the entire network was disbanded or all the hidden material found.

While there is no evidence of a link to the Leipzig drone bomb, the 2024 plot certainly highlights the potential.

News.title: Argos is getting a makeover - but can it attract new shoppers?
News.content:
Do you still shop at Argos? And if so, what do you think of it?

The chain has been a fixture of the British High Street for more than 50 years and is still used by around half of all UK households.

But it has struggled to thrive in recent years amid fierce competition from online giants like Amazon, with sales stagnating.

Its owner Sainsbury's recently announced it was selling the chain for a lot less than it paid for it just 10 years ago.

But the new owners say they see "real opportunities" for growth, including opening new standalone shops. Can they succeed where Sainsbury's did not?

News.title: First OpenAI, now Meta - why do AI hacks keep happening?
News.content:
Over the last fortnight, reports of AI models going beyond their expected bounds - be that technically or morally - have been seemingly unavoidable.

What started with a trickle - ChatGPT-maker OpenAI admitting their AI had hacked the site Hugging Face - has turned into a flood of groups revealing they had discovered instances of AI going out of control.

Claude-maker Anthropic, Meta and the UK's AI Security Institute (AISI) have now each reported incidents which seem to paint a worrying picture of a world in which tech going rogue is the norm.

In reality, each case offers a window into the risks posed by increasingly capable AI agents - and the importance of testing their limits before they are released to the world.

The OpenAI incident has, as Hugging Face's co-founder Thomas Wolf described it, come as a "wake-up call" for the tech industry since it happened at the end of July.

It was a big moment which caused big companies to reflect on their own systems - and, in some cases, check they hadn't missed something similarly shocking.

Anthropic was the first to act. On Friday, the company found three instances out of thousands where its model Claude had managed to gain access to the internet.

Then on Tuesday, the AISI, the UK government agency which evaluates cutting-edge models, then said it had detected a "security incident" during a routine evaluation.

It had been testing models by both OpenAI and Anthropic, and found they too tried to carry out cyber-attacks - calling for "scrutiny, transparency, and action".

Finally followed Meta, which revealed one of its AI models had inadvertently been allowed to access the internet due to a "misconfiguration" during a third-party test.

In disclosing the incident, it is following in the footsteps of those before it.

News.title: Conservatives pledge to ban foreign nationals from social housing
News.content:
The Conservatives have said they would end the provision of social housing for foreign nationals in England if they win power at the next election.

The party said ending new tenancies for all foreign nationals, as well as current tenancies for couples where neither person is a UK, Irish or EU citizen, would free up an estimated 228,144 homes for British families.

The Conservatives said Labour had "lost control of immigration" and British families had been left sitting on housing waiting lists as a result.

But Labour said the policy was an "unserious, unworkable proposal, copied from Reform, that does nothing to tackle the housing crisis the Tories themselves created".

In June, Reform UK leader Nigel Farage said he would make it a requirement for foreign national tenants to find private accommodation within three months or face possible deportation if his party won power.

Under the Tory proposals, ineligible tenants would be expected to move out of their homes within six months.

Any single person currently living in social housing who is not a UK, Irish or EU citizen would lose their social home. This includes those with or without children.

Couples, where neither of them are UK or EU citizens, and they do not have EU settled status, will also lose their entitlement.

Anyone with EU settled status would not be evicted.

For future tenancies, UK nationals and those with EU settled status would be eligible but any new EU citizens without settled status would not be.

Foreign nationals with settled status, refugee status, or specific humanitarian protections can currently qualify for social housing.

Asylum seekers are not eligible for social housing, unless in exceptional circumstances such as domestic abuse cases.

Social housing, usually provided by housing associations or local councils, is typically cheaper and more secure than privately rented homes.

When they were last in government in 2024, the Conservatives were considering plans to make it a requirement for foreign nationals to have to live in the UK for 10 years before qualifying for social housing.

There are 1.34 million households on social housing waiting lists, as of March 2025, the latest government figures.

The vast majority of social housing lettings are given to single people.

In 2024-25, most lead tenants of new social lettings, the person in whose name the social home is rented, were UK nationals - 89% or 233,000 tenants.

In the same period, 2.3% of new lettings were given to refugees - 800 refugees were UK nationals, while the remaining 3,900 were non-UK nationals.

The most common nationality of refugees in a new social letting was Afghanistan with the second most common being Ukraine.

News.title: Firearms officers called to violent disorder that left two men in critical condition
News.content:
Two men are in a critical condition after violence broke out in a village in south Wales.

Firearms officers from Gwent Police were called to the incident that happened near Hospital Road and Mill Road in Pontnewynydd, near Pontypool, on Thursday.

Four men were arrested, and police say while two remain in custody, another is in hospital.

Officers have appealed for anyone with information, CCTV or dashcam footage from the area between 19:00 and 19:30 BST to contact them.

The National Police Air Service also attended the scene, alongside paramedics.

News.title: Police to end review into siblings who died in farmhouse 'bloodbath'
News.content:
A forensic review into the deaths of a brother and sister 50 years ago will end almost four years after it began, despite not delivering any new conclusions.

The bodies of Martha and Griff Thomas were found at a farmhouse in Llangolman, Pembrokeshire in 1976, originally prompting a double murder investigation.

Family member Huw Gibby, 79, said he was left "shell-shocked" that the investigation had failed to find any new answers, and described crime scene photos as a "bloodbath".

Dyfed-Powys Police said a "significant amount of complex work" had been undertaken, and "the family has been updated on the limitations faced in reviewing an incident that took place 50 years ago".

On a chilly Saturday morning in December 1976, postman Nigel Rossiter pulled up outside the isolated Ffynon Samson farmhouse in west Wales.

It was his first week in the job, and he spotted a couple of letters still lying on the floor of the porch where he had delivered them days before.

Smelling burning inside, he raised the alarm. This led to the discovery of two bodies â Griff, 73, who was badly burnt, and Martha, 70, who had severe injuries.

Police were called and found Martha - known as Patti - lying slumped on a magazine rack in the corner of the living room, with severe head injuries.

Chairs had been knocked over, and an overturned television lay at her feet. It was still switched on, with the sound of static filling the room.

News.title: Wildfire damage could take hundreds of years to recover from, experts say
News.content:
It could be hundreds of years before habitats destroyed by wildfires in Wales recover, an environment watchdog has said.

Nick Thomas, from Natural Resources Wales (NRW), said if soil had been incinerated in upland areas rich in peat, which grows at about a millimetre a year, it could take centuries for the vegetation to come back.

He expects 2026 to be the worst year Wales has ever experienced.

As well as damage to natural habitats and animal life, Thomas warned loss of soil could increase flood risks, because it no longer acted as a "sponge" holding water on high ground.

Wales has witnessed huge wildfires this summer, including one major incident and the evacuation of a village in Conwy county.

In the Rhinogydd mountain range in Gwynedd, which is home to a National Nature Reserve and a Special Area of Conservation, a blaze burned for nearly two weeks and affected over 2,000 acres.

Both fires were visible from space.

Meanwhile, a fire in Blaenavon, Torfaen, could be smelt as far away as Cardiff.

Although fewer wildfires were reported in the second half of July in England and Wales compared with 2025, Thomas said: "This year seems to have been worse, I would say, than any of the ones I can remember.

"I would expect this to probably be the worst year for wildfires perhaps we've ever had."

While some areas will recover quite quickly - potentially within a couple of years - he said: "It all depends on how deep the fire goes.

"If a fire burns into the soil and incinerates the soil... then you've lost hundreds of years worth of soil.

"So it's going to take hundreds of years really for that vegetation to come back in a similar way to what it was."

News.title: Veteran camps in woods for months waiting for home
News.content:
An Army veteran has spent the last 15 weeks camping in woods while waiting for his social housing application to be processed.

Blair Murray, 44, served more than a decade in the Royal Logistics Corps up to 2010, but was made homeless by a landlord last year and spent months staying with friends before setting up camp in woodland near Crook in County Durham.

Murray said he had lined up a job and arranged to start counselling sessions, but both were being held up by his lack of a home.

Since the BBC got in touch with Durham County Council, homeless prevention manager Christopher Hepworth said the authority had worked with the Armed Forces Outreach Service and booked him into a Travelodge.

Hepworth said: "We will continue to work with him to secure suitable, stable, long-term accommodation."

In the most recent survey carried out by the Office for Veterans' Affairs, one in 400 ex-service personnel reported they were homeless or sleeping rough.

News.title: Amanda Knox defends Fringe comedy show after claims it will 'trivialise violence'
News.content:
Amanda Knox, who was convicted and later acquitted of murdering British student Meredith Kercher in Italy in 2007, has defended her solo comedy show following calls for it to be cancelled.

The sold-out show called Cartwheel, which Knox will perform at the Edinburgh Festival Fringe, discusses motherhood and how she will explain the case to her daughter.

Knox told the BBC she is not the first person to use comedy to talk about traumatic events and said her material focuses on "how the world is unsafe and unfair towards women".

But Stephanie Kercher, the victim's sister, said she is concerned it will "normalise and trivialise" violence against women, and Meredith, in particular.

Speaking on BBC Breakfast, Stephanie Kercher, said: "What I would say [to Knox] is to think about the family here, think about her friends and to turn the tables if it was your sister that this had happened to, because I know you have a sister as well."

Responding to the comments, Knox said: "The interesting irony of that is that my daughter is a huge motivation for me doing this show.

"It's about how the world is unsafe and unfair towards women and what it means to raise a daughter in that world, knowing how bad it can be.

"If they [Kercher's family] saw my show, they would recognise that."

A petition against the show, set up by a friend of Meredith, has been signed by nearly 5,000 people.

It states the show disrespects her memory and risks making light of such a harrowing event.

News.title: Man wrongly jailed for murdering man wants to restore his 'forgotten' grave
News.content:
A man who was wrongly jailed for 11 years for murder is raising money to restore the grave of the man he was accused of killing.

Michael O'Brien was one of three men wrongly convicted of the 1987 murder of Cardiff newsagent Philip Saunders.

O'Brien, along with Darren Hall and Ellis Sherwood, became known as the Cardiff Newsagent Three. They were eventually cleared in 1999, in what became one of Wales' worst miscarriages of justice.

He said he recently visited Saunders' grave and was "sad" to see there was no longer a headstone there and the area was "unkempt."

"It just sort of hit home that one, the killer was still at large, and two, this man has largely been forgotten about," O'Brien said.

Saunders was killed with a shovel in his backyard. It seemed the ambush and brutal attack was an attempt to steal his day's takings.

In June, nearly 40 years on from the original crime, South Wales Police said they were launching a review of the evidence in the case, "in the hope advances in forensic science will provide the breakthrough needed".

News.title: All schools in England to get pupil attendance targets, government says
News.content:
Every mainstream state school in England will be given their own target to improve pupil attendance, the government has confirmed.

Schools will also be encouraged to offer more clubs and activities on Fridays, to improve attendance at the end of the week.

It comes as official attendance data, published on Thursday, suggested school absence rates in England remained above pre-pandemic levels, with nearly one in five pupils missing at least 10% of school in the 2025/26 academic year.

Education minister Paul Waugh said the new attendance targets would take each school's local challenges into account, but that "every school has a role to play to improve attendance".

Before the Covid pandemic, when many schools closed to pupils for significant periods of time, attendance rates at English mainstream state schools regularly stayed above 95%, but schools have struggled to get back to those rates in the years since.

Thursday's figures, external suggested an overall attendance rate of 93% for 2025/26, a slight decrease on the previous year. That includes both authorised absences, such as illness, and unauthorised absences, which is when pupils miss school without permission or a valid reason.

The rates of persistent absence have doubled since the pandemic. A pupil is described as persistently absent if they miss at least 10% of school sessions.

In 2018/19, persistent absence rates for England state schools were around 10%, while the most recent data showed it was at 19% in 2025/26.

Pupils on free school meals and those with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) were also still more likely to be absent from school than their peers.

News.title: England footballer Ivan Toney charged over assault at Soho nightclub
News.content:
