England footballer Ivan Toney has been charged with assault following an incident at a Soho nightclub in December, police have confirmed.

Toney, 30, of Nothampton, was charged last Thursday with assault causing actual bodily harm in relation to an alleged incident which reportedly took place on 6 December last year at a nightclub on Wardour Street in London.

He will appear at Westminster Magistrates’ Court on 24 September, Metropolitan Police have said.

The Sun newspaper reported on 8 December that Toney had been arrested after an alleged headbutt. A spokesperson for the footballer said: “Ivan acknowledges the charge and although he is naturally shocked, he looks forward to being given the opportunity to clear his name in court.”

The Al-Ahli striker returned just last month from the United States where he was part of Thomas Tuchel’s 26-man Three Lions squad in the World Cup. He replaced Harry Kane as striker in England's 6-4 win over France in the “bronze final” of the tournament.

The force said in a statement: “A man has been charged with assault following a Met investigation.

“Ivan Toney, 30 (16.03.1996), of Northampton, was charged on Thursday, 31 July with assault causing actual bodily harm.

“He will appear at Westminster Magistrates' Court on Thursday, 24 September.

“The charge relates to an assault, which reportedly took place on 6 December 2025 at a nightclub on Wardour Street, W1.”

The Irons are back in the fire. Yet this time, the fire might not actually be the Championship.

The inaptly-named second tier of English football, which is welcoming back West Ham United after a 14-year absence, may simply represent a single flame of the many licking at the east London club.

The other particularly scorching strand to the narrative around the club in 2026, of course, has been the saga involving David Sullivan's exit as chairman after 16 years at the club.

In June it was revealed that West Ham had been “made aware of the impending publication of serious historic allegations”, leading the billionaire to step down but also deny all claims, which were soon shared in a joint-investigation by BBC Panorama and The Times.

The investigation detailed allegations that Sullivan had abused his power as owner of the Daily Sport and Sunday Sport tabloids to prey on women in their late teens and early 20s, with seven women speaking to the BBC and the Times about accusations spanning decades, starting in the 1980s. “All come from women who were [...] young models seeking work at Sullivan's Daily and Sunday Sport newspapers,” the BBC reported. “They accuse Sullivan of sexually exploitative and predatory behaviour.”

Many fans celebrated Sullivan's resignation, having craved his exit for so long. At the time of writing, however, he is not truly gone.

Despite his resignation, a warning that he should stay away from men's first-team games in the coming season, and suggestions that he was previously asked to stay away from the women's and youth teams (which he denies), Sullivan remains West Ham's largest shareholder, possessing a 38.8 per cent stake in the east London club.

open image in gallery David Sullivan resigned as West Ham chairman but retains a stake in the club ( PA )

But here comes Amanda Staveley, bursting through the doors with a consortium in tow, aiming to buy Sullivan's stake.

The former Newcastle United director agreed last week to buy a 25.1 per cent stake from the family of former co-owner David Gold, who passed away in 2023, at a cost of £150m.

Yet there is opposition from club co-owner Daniel Kretinsky, a Czech billionaire with a minority stake in West Ham, who could yet have a say in this power struggle.

It feels as though Staveley's involvement has led to equal parts concern and optimism in recent days, which is testament to the complicated opportunity facing West Ham.

As the flames continue to lick at the club, it's worth remembering that fire can destroy but it can also purge and purify.

It was far too easy at the end of the 2025/26 season for fans of other clubs to shrug, to claim that West Ham would come straight back up; it’s easy to say, if one supports a team that has never endured the stomach churn of the drop. Yet some West Ham fans do feel that relegation can represent a necessary wake-up call, an overdue reset.

open image in gallery Captain and forward Jarrod Bowen has extended his deal with West Ham ( Getty )

Many will remember the joys of the 2011/12 Championship season, the unfamiliar feeling of consistent wins – although a botched, wasted bid to seal automatic promotion led to a nervier climax than was needed. And as West Ham return to the Championship, they do so with a coach in Nuno Espirito Santo who has won that league before.

This curious appetite among the fanbase has been represented by the number 50,000, which relays the approximate number of season tickets sold for the coming campaign, and even the number of tickets sold for Saturday's first-round Carabao Cup clash with Portsmouth.

Optimism has also been augmented by a promising start to the transfer window, which saw West Ham lock down captain Jarrod Bowen and bring in a combined £148m by selling Mateus Fernandes, Crysencio Summerville and Freddie Potts.

A counter-concern, of course, might be a lack of signings since then, with the exception of defender Joel Veltman from Brighton, although staples of last year’s squad have been retained.

At the time of writing, goalkeepers Alphonse Areola and Mads Hermansen remain on the books; Aaron Wan-Bissaka, Konstantinos Mavropanos, Jean-Clair Todibo and Kyle Walker-Peters are still available in defence; Tomas Soucek and Edson Alvarez persist in midfield; and forwards Taty Castellanos and Pablo should be champing at the bit to put a dent in second-tier opposition.

open image in gallery Midfielder Tomas Soucek is injured but could still play a key part in West Ham’s upcoming season ( Getty )

Some of these talents could depart between now and the Championship opener at Burnley on 16 August, but at least they would yield further funds for investment before the 3 September transfer deadline – or in the January window, should West Ham stutter in their bid for an instant return to the top tier. The club has suggested that any uncertainty around its hierarchy will not impact transfer dealings, although that does remain to be seen.

So, the Irons are back in the fire. There, perhaps, they can forge something stronger for the future.

Shoppers may be needlessly overpaying for omega-3 supplements marketed as "high strength" that often contain surprisingly low levels of their crucial active ingredients, a new investigation by consumer watchdog Which? has found.

Which? nutrition experts scrutinised 24 omega-3 supplements, comparing them against guidance from the Scientific Advisory Committee on Nutrition (SACN), which advises a daily intake of 450mg of the omega-3 fatty acids EPA and DHA.

For products claiming "high strength," Which? set a benchmark of 1,000mg of combined EPA and DHA. Their analysis revealed that several of these premium-priced supplements contained less EPA and DHA than the recommended daily intake.

The watchdog highlighted that in some instances, consumers could be paying twice as much for products offering no more active omega-3 than significantly cheaper alternatives on the market.

open image in gallery Which? highlighted that consumers could be paying twice as much for products offering no more active omega-3 than significantly cheaper alternatives on the market.

All of the retailers involved said their product labelling complied with the Nutrition and Health Claims Register.

So, what exactly are EPA and DHA, and why are they important? We spoke to Dr Sarah Schenker, registered nutritionist and dietitian, who explained what omega-3 fatty acids are, the role they play in maintaining health, and the best food sources for increasing your intake naturally.

What are the different types of omega-3 fatty acids, and why are they important?

“Omega-3 is a type of fatty acid that helps support your heart health, maintain normal brain function and eye health, and reduce inflammation,” says Schenker.

“There are lots of different types of fatty acids, and according to their structure, they can be omega-3, omega-6, omega-9, and the number relates to the position of what we call double bonds.”

There are three main types of omega-3 fatty acids: ALA (alpha-linolenic acid) and EPA (eicosapentaenoic acid) and DHA (docosahexaenoic acid).

open image in gallery There are plenty of natural sources of omega-3 (Alamy/PA) ( Alamy/PA )

“Our body cannot make ALA, an essential omega-3 fatty acid, on its own, so we get it from plant sources such as chia seeds, walnuts, hemp seeds, flax seeds, soybeans and rape seed oil,” says the dietitian.

“Whereas, oily fish is the main food source of EPA and DHA, which are important long-chain omega-3 fatty acids.”

Here are some of the best food sources of omega-3 fatty acids to add to your next shopping list…

Salmon

“Keep it simple with smoked salmon,” recommends Schenker.

“If you’re looking for something easy for lunch, smoked salmon in a bagel or a sandwich is a good option. Smoked salmon also goes really nicely with scrambled or poached eggs.”

Mackerel

“Mackerel is also a great source of omega-3 and smoked mackerel just comes in a packet that you can add to a salad,” says the dietitian.

open image in gallery Smoked mackerel is a great source of omega-3 ( Alamy/PA )

Sardines

“A tin of sardines is pretty cheap and there’s lots of things you can do with them,” says Schenker. “Some people like to put them in tomato sauce or to have them on toast.”

You can also make a fast, healthy, and creamy dip using canned sardines.

“If you get sardines in oil, you can mash them together with a little bit of soft cheese and make a nice dip,” suggests Schenker.

Tuna

“Fresh tuna can be expensive, but it can be nice to have once in a while,” says Schenker. “Tuna steaks are pretty easy to cook as you can just pan fry them on one side for two minutes and then turn them over and do the same thing on the other side.”

Edamame beans

“You can buy edamame beans from frozen and just chuck a handful into a stir fry, a salad or a soup,” recommends the dietitian.

open image in gallery Edamame beans can be added to stir-frys, salads or soups. ( Alamy/PA )

Chia seeds

“Chia seeds can be expensive, but if you shop around you should be able to find a big bag of them in an international supermarket for a lower price,” says Schenker.

“You could soak them in yoghurt overnight which makes them swell up and makes a nice filling breakfast.”

Flax seeds

“You could stir flax seeds through your yoghurt or muesli for breakfast,” suggests the dietitian.

Walnuts

“A handful of walnuts are a good thing to have as a snack,” says Schenker.

Using walnuts to make a muhammara dip is also a great summertime snack.

open image in gallery Walnuts are great as a quick snack or used to make dips. ( Getty Images/iStockphoto )

“You can make a delicious dip with a small handful of breadcrumbs, walnuts, roasted red peppers, pomegranate molasses and olive oil,” recommends Schenker.

“That will keep in the fridge for a few days, and you can just have it with crackers or as an accompaniment to whatever you might be eating.”

Fortified products

“There are also foods that are fortified with omega-3, so you could look for some of those,” says Schenker.

“For example, you can buy eggs that have come from hens that have been fed an omega-3 rich diet and you can even get fish fingers and butter that have been fortified with omega-3.”

This month, pound-for-pound No 1 Islam Makhachev defends his welterweight title against Ian Machado Garry in the main event of UFC 330.

The bout marks Makhachev’s first defence of the belt, which he won by dominating and outpointing Jack Della Maddalena in November, after giving up the lightweight belt following a record-breaking four successful defences.

And the Russian, 34, faces an intriguing test against the divisive Machado Garry, 28, who enters the fight with just one professional loss to his name.

open image in gallery UFC welterweight champion Islam Makhachev ( Getty )

The Irishman bounced back from that narrow points defeat by Shavkat Rakhmonov with wins over ex-champ Belal Muhammad and Carlos Prates, and he enters UFC 330 full of confidence.

The co-main event pits women’s strawweight champion Mackenzie Dern against Gillian Robertson, as Dern defends the belt for the first time, having been upgraded from interim-title holder. In October, during Zhilei Zhang’s reign atop the division, Dern outpointed Virna Jandiroba to win the interim strap, before Zhang moved up in weight and gave up her title.

Here’s all you need to know:

When is UFC 330?

UFC 330 will take place on Saturday 15 August at Xfinity Mobile Arena in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The early prelims will begin at 10pm BST (2pm PT / 4pm CT / 5pm ET), followed by the regular prelims at 12am BST on Sunday (4pm PT / 6pm CT / 7pm ET on Saturday); the main card will start at 2am BST on Sunday (6pm PT / 8pm CT / 9pm ET on Saturday).

How can I watch it?

In the UK, the card will air live on TNT Sports and is also accessible via HBO Max, EE TV, Virgin Media, Amazon Prime Video, and Sky Sports. In the US, Paramount+ will stream the action, with CBS showing a segment of the card.

News.title: Luxury holidays worth the journey
News.content:
The most rewarding travels balance downtime and discovery in equal measure. These exceptional places to stay — from hotels to holiday rentals and floating retreats — in diverse destinations are sure to leave a lasting impression.

Head to the Med for a summer stay unlike any other

( Nobu Ibiza )

This summer, Ibiza becomes truly celestial. Inspired by the upcoming total solar eclipse over Spain on 12 August and Perseid meteor showers in 2026, Nobu Hotel Ibiza Bay has created Beyond the Sun, a collection of exclusive experiences that encourage renewal, adventure and celebration of the island’s natural beauty during a once-in-a-lifetime cosmic event. Designed for those who seek more than just a summer escape, guests can rejuvenate with Pilates, breathwork and sound healing sessions, and experience immersive OPO meditation during sunshine-filled daytimes. Then, as the skies darken during the eclipse, join a guided hike to scenic viewpoints to watch in awe. Back down on Earth, the hotel’s position right on the sand means leisurely barefoot days, dips in Talamanca Bay and unmatched seafood dining at the hotel’s namesake restaurant.

Book your celestial stay at nobuhotelibizabay.com

Be spoilt for choice with stays in Llandudno

( Four Saints Hotel )

Known as the ‘Queen of the Welsh watering places’, Llandudno is a charming seaside destination, renowned for its Victorian heritage and elegant 19th-century architecture. Four Saints Hotels is a family-run collection of five hotels in some of the town's most sought-after locations. Offering something to suit every budget, style and desired location, the portfolio of boutique hotels includes the four-star Merrion Hotel, which overlooks the buzzing promenade, with stunning views over the bay and easy access to the beach. Nearby, Lauriston Court sits opposite the Llandudno Pier, making it an ideal spot for family stays. Higher on the hill beside Happy Valley is Headlands Hotel, which gives guests fabulous views from the Great Orme. Down on the front, Brig Y Don enjoys lovely sea views from opposite the bandstand and the White Heather Hotel offers accommodation steps away from Llandudno High Street.

Save 10% with code SAVE10 at 4saintshotels.uk and merrion-hotel.com

Head to a village-like resort in Cyprus

( Columbia Beach Resort )

Set along the sheltered curve of Pissouri Bay, Columbia Beach Resort offers a quiet retreat in Cyprus. Its low-rise stone buildings, terracotta roofs and landscaped gardens create the feel of a traditional Mediterranean village, one built around a lagoon-like pool. The all-suite resort looks out towards Cape Aspro and balances a laid-back coastal living vibe with five-star comforts. Enjoy leisurely tavern-style meze dinners and family-friendly al fresco options, work up a sweat playing tennis, squash or padel, or slow down with a stand-up paddleboard yoga session in the bay. The dedicated kids’ club keeps children busy, while the award-winning spa is a calming space where adults will love to spend restorative afternoons, meaning everyone on your trip is catered for.

Plan your stay at columbiaresort.com

Make memories on a luxury getaway to Rhodes

( Prince Andriana Resort )

At Princess Andriana Resort & Spa, family holidays revolve around keeping every age group entertained without losing the sense of relaxation that makes a summer break feel worthwhile. As part of the H Hotels collection, premium family rooms and suites offer plenty of room to spread out, with options for private pools offering added privacy. Children spend many happy hours at the Aqua Princess Water Park with its slides and splash areas, while adults love the sandy beach, indulgent spa, well-equipped gym and sports including padel and tennis. A kids’ club, open-air entertainment and watersports ensure there’s always something happening, while the ultra-all-inclusive dining programme covers everything from high-end Mediterranean cuisine to barbecue classics, with options for all ages.

Discover more at Hhotels.gr

Try a holiday with a difference on an Arctic summer escape

( Arctic Norway )

This year, discover a different side of Arctic Norway at Snow Resort Kirkenes. Far from being only a winter playground, during the summer, the north transforms into a green and vibrant landscape with dramatic fjords, pretty forest trails and near-endless daylight under the midnight sun. Stay in cosy gamme (wooden wilderness) cabins or experience the unmatched Snowhotel 365, the world’s only real snow and ice hotel, which remains open for overnight stays all year round. Families, couples and adventure-lovers will love the king crab safaris by rigid inflatable boat, husky hikes, wagon rides and reindeer encounters, as well as the peaceful nature that surrounds far above the Arctic Circle. Autumn also brings a new hue of colourful landscapes and excellent conditions for viewing the Northern Lights.

Save 10 % when booking summer and autumn packages with overnight, activities and transfers included at snowresortkirkenes.com

Swap city skylines for the South Tyrolean mountains

( Das Gerstl )

There are hotels with a view, and then there’s Das Gerstl Alpine Retreat. Nadia Sawalha has threatened legal action against ITV after claiming she’s been removed from Loose Women due to her vocal support for Palestine.

The presenter and former EastEnders star, 61, alleged that she was temporarily axed from the daytime show in July 2026 and accused ITV of “forever changing the goalposts” in relation to her return.

She claimed the channel’s decision arose from “escalating campaign of smears, complaints, hostile media coverage and targeted calls to have me removed” from the series.

open image in gallery Nadia Sawalha said she was removed from the programme in July 2026 ( ITV )

In a video shared on Instagram, Sawalha said: “I want to say how sad I am that it’s got to this. Believe me, I have appealed to ITV’s hearts and minds, but to no avail.

“After I began speaking publicly in support of Palestine in December 2023, I became the target of an escalating campaign of smears, complaints, hostile media coverage and targeted calls to have me removed from Loose Women.”

She said that, after her initial removal, ITV “couldn’t guarantee they wouldn’t take me off again, as it would depend on what was said, even though I’m hired for being an opinionated woman on a discussion show and I’ve never brought up or spoken about Palestine directly on the show”.

She called it “the tip of the iceberg of what’s been happening”.

Alongside the lawsuit, Sawalha has launched a petition demanding a public apology from ITV and her reinstatement. The petition has already garnered more than 20,000 signatures.

She said the petition was to show there are “many more people with us than against us”, adding: “It’s not just me that has been targeted like this from my beliefs. There are the teachers, doctors, nurses, charity and supermarket workers, and students who have also spoken according to their conscience and have suffered a similar fate as me. Enough is enough.

“We need to send a clear message to ITV and other groups and corporations that we won’t be scared into silence, and no-one should be bullied out of their job for following their conscience and speaking out against brutal oppression.”

open image in gallery Nadia Sawalha said she was removed from the programme in July 2026 ( Channel 5 )

Swalha has been supported by another of the show’s panellists, former athlete Dame Kelly Holmes, who said she had “no idea” what had been happening.

“This is just not right or just,” she wrote in response. “I am so sorry, Nadia, no one can even begin to comprehend the ‘fight’ you must have been having behind the scenes. Thanks for sharing this. I had no idea. With you.”

The Independent has contacted ITV for comment.

Sawalha joined the ITV show in 1999 as one of the original panellists alongside Kaye Adams, Jane Moore and Karren Brady. She took a maternity break in 2002 and returned to the programme in 2013.

In 2025, she criticised ITV’s “out of the blue” budget cuts, after the channel announced that Loose Women, alongside other popular daytime talk show Lorraine, would be slashed from one hour to 30 minutes.

Speaking alongside her husband Mark Adderly on the couple’s YouTube channel, she said many people behind the scenes were “really suffering”.

Struggling to contain her tears, Sawalha said: “To all my friends and colleagues behind the scenes who have just got a huge shock out of the blue, I'm so sorry.”

Sawalha is also known for playing Annie Palmer on EastEnders in the late 1990s, and has had roles in ITV comedy Second Thoughts, The Bill and Benidorm. She is also a successful cook and won Celebrity MasterChef in 2007.

President Donald Trump has posted an AI meme of himself hosting a party for his supporters using Vincent Van Gogh’s 1889 painting “The Starry Night” as a backdrop on another busy evening on Truth Social.

The president is seen in the image basking in the admiration of representative members of his base, who are clustered around outdoor tables to enjoy a drink in the summer twilight.

“Trump 2028, Make America Great Again,” reads a banner headline.

The post might be interpreted as Trump’s latest hint that he intends to seek an unconstitutional third term in two years’ time, although The Washington Post reported Thursday that he has privately told donors to throw their money behind Vice President JD Vance at the next election.

The tortured Dutch artist’s celebrated painting captures the view, as he saw it, from the window of his asylum room at Saint-Remy-de-Provence, France, and has been in the collection of the Museum of Modern Art in New York City since 1941.

Prior to his being taken into care, Van Gogh famously attempted to sever his left ear following a heated argument with fellow artist Paul Gaugin, requiring it to be heavily bandaged, a distressing detail captured in a subsequent self-portrait.

Trump’s supporters unconsciously echoed that image when they wore cotton bandages in sympathy with the president at the 2024 Republican convention, which came days after his right ear had been clipped by a sniper’s bullet in Butler, Pennsylvania.

Trump again goes after former talk show host and comedian Rosie O'Donnell, once more posing as a doctor claim she is suffering from 'Trump Derangement Syndrome' ( Donald J Trump/Truth Social )

Elsewhere on his social media platform, Trump posted a series of memes celebrating victories for his preferred Republican candidates in Tennessee’s primary elections, as well as others attempting to associate himself with great figures from American history.

In one, he can be seen signing a document by feather quill with George Washington and Abraham Lincoln; in a second, he shares a joke with John F Kennedy at Camp David; and in a third, he marches on the battlefield with Generals George S Patton and Douglas MacArthur.

The last of these, which he first posted earlier this week, is perhaps the most contentious, given that Trump never served in the military, having received several draft deferrals from the Vietnam War during his youth after being signed off with bone spurs.

He has also been quoted in the past making disparaging remarks about fallen American soldiers – although he had denied making the offending comments.

The president also posted a new version of a meme he first showcased a month ago in which he casts himself as a doctor diagnosing former talk show host and comedian Rosie O’Donnell with “Trump Derangement Syndrome.”

O’Donnell, who left the U.S. to live in the Republic of Ireland following the president’s re-election, responded to the original video by saying of him: “He’s quite ill – and getting worse daily. The 25th Amendment exists for exactly this reason. Remove. Impeach. Convict.”

Finally, Trump posted two further attacks on Abdul El-Sayed, who won this week’s Michigan Democratic Senate primary, calling him a “Communist Dumocrat,” and again lashed out at the press for reporting on an alleged rift between himself and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, which he also denies.

News.title: Suspected Ebola case on packed Congo river boat sparks testing rush
News.content:
Congolese health authorities have intercepted and detained a river boat on its way to the capital after a suspected Ebola case onboard.

Authorities have set up a mobile clinic to test more than 200 passengers after one of them disembarked and died earlier on the voyage.

The boat travelling from the northeastern commercial hub of Kisangani was stopped and held in Maluku, some 40 miles from Kinshasa.

Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is dealing with its worst ever outbreak of the viral haemorrhagic fever, which has seen nearly 4,000 cases and killed around 1,801 people according to the latest government figures.

Samuel Roger Kamba, the health minister, said a 32-year-old man had disembarked in Pimu in Mongala province, before developing ‌suspected Ebola symptoms and dying.

“We did not say it was Ebola. We said there was a suspected case for which we are being cautious,” the health minister told a press conference, according to MediaCongo, a local news site.

He said there had been no other reports of deaths among travellers.

The virus has so far spread to five provinces, though more than 90 per cent of cases have been recorded in the north eastern Ituri region.

News.title: El Nino could cause explosion of rabid seals, animal health experts warn
News.content:
This year’s El Nino weather event risks propelling an outbreak of rabid seals around the world, the world’s animal health body has warned.

Countries in South America and Australasia are being urged to look for signs the deadly infectious disease has reached their waters, only two years after it was first confirmed in South Africa.

The 2024 discovery of rabies in South Africa’s Cape fur seals was the first significant outbreak ever found in marine mammals and has been described as a “significant shift in rabies ecology”.

More than 100 cases have been confirmed in South Africa and Namibia since then, raising fears that aggressive rabid seals could infect humans, pets and other wildlife.

Changing patterns in fish stocks caused by the El Nino phenomenon now potentially risk widening the spread, as uninfected seal populations migrate for food and come into contact with rabid colleagues.

Scientists believe warming sea temperatures off Antarctica could send seal populations northwards into Southern African waters, where they could be exposed to rabies.

They could then return to their home waters, taking the virus with them and infecting other seal populations.

News.title: ​Arteta’s ‘dynasty’ dream collides with Arsenal’s harsh reality
News.content:
Arsenal 1 Real Betis 3

Mikel Arteta says he wants to create a “dynasty” at Arsenal as he threw down the gauntlet to his players to retain their Premier League title and reach a “different level”.

Arsenal are on the verge of completing a £75m deal for Brazil midfielder Bruno Guimãraes from Newcastle and have not given up hope of landing Real Madrid winger Vinícius Júnior, who has been offered an improved contract by the Spanish giants.

The Premier League champions slumped to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night, when they paid the price for individual errors and a lethargic, sloppy defensive display.

But that did little to quell Arteta’s ambitions for the new season. “I’m even more excited [about this season], and we’re going to go and attack every possible title because that’s the ambition that we have,” he said.

“We know that we have the ability. We will go from a strength to a strength as well, whether it’s with the players that we have to take them to a different level, and with the market that is still open to recruit as well, so we are very optimistic about it.

“All the work that we’ve done – that I’ve done through the summer – is to understand what we need to do to win again and to create a dynasty in this football club. That’s the aim.”

Despite Arteta’s bullishness, he conceded Arsenal would have to be a lot better than they were against Betis. When asked about the mood in the dressing room, he said: “Very upset, given a hard time. They are fuming, but this is good. That’s what we need.”

Telegraph Sport analyses some of the talking points from a disappointing evening at the Aviva Stadium.

No Saliba a concern

The importance of goalkeeper David Raya and centre-backs William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhães to Arsenal hardly needs overstating. Their title success was built on the foundations provided by that triumvirate at the back.

Raya has yet to report back from holiday after Spain’s World Cup triumph and Saliba is facing an extended spell on the sidelines with a back injury. Gabriel did appear for the second half but, watching this, Arteta is unlikely to have been dissuaded from the belief he needs another top defender to compensate for the loss of Saliba.

It may have been only Arsenal’s second game of pre-season, so a degree of legginess was understandable.

But the ease with which they were cut open and overloaded by the Spanish side, and the volume of individual errors, did not sit comfortably with Arteta with just over a fortnight until they kick off their title defence at home to newly promoted Coventry City.

Only once in 63 matches last season did Arsenal concede three goals in a single game but they were fortunate Betis did not score more. “In the first half there are two different things: to play well and to compete,” said Arteta, who saw his side trail 3-1 at the interval.

News.title: Ebola outbreak outpacing containment effort, WHO chief warns
News.content:
Caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, for which there are no vaccines or treatments, it has been extremely difficult to contain, according to experts on the ground.

“The outbreak is spreading faster than our scale-up of the response, with new cases doubling in some hotspots over the past week alone,” Dr Tedros said on X.

Part of the difficulty is that the virus was circulating undetected for weeks before the outbreak was formally declared in mid-May, leaving health officials even now racing to catch up with the spread.

Prof Placide Mbala, director of research, clinical trials and innovation at Africa CDC, told the Telegraph: “It’s mostly the fact we arrived a bit late. It took us some time before we detected this virus outbreak. And when we detected the outbreak, we already had a total of I can say more than 200 suspected cases. It’s been difficult to catch up. That’s where we are.”

While the DRC has a wealth of experience in tackling haemorrhagic fever outbreaks, the effects of that initial delay are still being felt.

Prof Mbala said: “We have some experience dealing with the cases, the labs, the communication, the infection prevention and control.

“We have some experience... But my observation is that we were very slow, and it’s why we’re in this situation.

“We are slow detecting the people, slow responding, we are slow deploying people, we are slow to recruit the community healthcare workers to improve contact tracing, we are slow to deploy the safe burials.”

DRC’s largest outbreak had previously been from 2018 to 2020, when 3,481 cases were recorded.

The West Africa outbreak recorded 28,616 cases and 11,310 deaths according to the WHO.

Prof Mbala said insecurity was also severely hampering attempts to curb the virus. The outbreak epicentre is in Ituri province, which has been wracked by ethnic strife for decades and is also home to militias competing to control mining.

He said: “There are many, many mining groups controlling most of the mining places. We have a big issue with those places, because they are places where the response team cannot go.”

Medics and aid workers have also been undermined by violent public distrust of their efforts.

Locals in the area have either doubted the existence of the virus, or have accused health teams of deliberately spreading the infection, or somehow benefiting from it.

More than a dozen health facilities have been set alight and several health workers have been killed.

Prof Mbala said: “The local people, they also sometimes are very upset, because they believe that it’s a kind of a business, and people who are coming here, they are getting a lot of money, [so] don’t want this disease to stop.”

He said he hoped that immunity was starting to rise in some areas and this would start to curb transmission.

However there was also a risk that people fleeing the outbreak would spread the virus further afield.

He said: “The second scenario is the fact we are seeing people moving from the affected area to new areas, to run away from the response team because they do not want to go to the treatment centre.

“And in complicity with their family members living in other areas, they are now the ones who are spreading the disease to new areas

“So we’ll see new places affected because people are moving around from the affected zone to the non-affected zone.”

News.title: Mykhailo Mudryk returns as Chelsea slip to Juventus defeat

Mykhailo Mudryk made his first Chelsea appearance since November 2024 as Xabi Alonso’s team succumbed to their second pre-season defeat.

Mudryk replaced Nicolas Jackson in the 82nd minute against Juventus, marking his return to competitive football after a long doping ban that was resolved this week thanks to changes in Wada regulations.

There were a couple of crosses delivered from the left flank by the Ukrainian winger, who could yet leave Chelsea on loan or on a permanent basis before the close of the transfer window.

Juventus were the victors though, thanks to a sumptuous 68th-minute goal by Kosovo winger Edon Zhegrova.

Alonso had 21 players on his bench, and made 12 second-half substitutions.

Levi Colwill and Cole Palmer featured in the defeat by 10-man Spurs on Saturday, but sat this game out as they continue to build fitness. Danny Welbeck did start though, reunited with former Brighton team-mate Joao Pedro up top.

Chelsea scored just one goal against Spurs and Juventus, but the thrust provided by right-back Marco Palestra in tandem with first Geovany Quenda and then Estevao was a bright spot for Alonso.

Chelsea continue their pre-season against AC Milan on Saturday, before they host Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge on August 15.

They begin their Premier League campaign at Fulham in the Monday night slot on the opening weekend.

News.title: The underground lab where ‘princess mosquitoes’ are treated like royalty
News.content:
Beneath the grand Art Deco headquarters of the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine lies a vast labyrinth inhabited by weird and wonderful creatures.

In this maze of subterranean labs, store rooms and corridors live colonies of disease-bearing insects and arachnids from all over the world, from bed bugs, sand flies and microscopic dust mites to the so-called kissing bugs that spread Chagas disease – a sinister condition that can cause its victims to drop dead of heart failure without warning, albeit decades after the first (silent) infection.

Behind a series of doors, contained in stacks of mesh boxes, you can even find the flies that spread trachoma, the Dickensian eye disease that is still a leading cause of blindness around the world. But be warned: entering the room is not for the faint of heart – the flies feed on human excrement and the smell is impossible to forget.

There are also many varieties of mosquito, including several species of the Anopheles genus that spread malaria, Culex and Aedes mosquitoes that are also vectors for human and animal diseases, and even Toxorhynchites, perhaps better known as the elephant mosquito, a friendly giant which doesn’t bite people but preys on other mosquitoes.

These animals have been studied intensely since the insectaries were established in the building’s vaults in the 1960s, underpinning many breakthroughs in the control, surveillance, and understanding of vector-borne diseases in the developing world.

LSHTM researchers are now looking closer to home. They have established the UK’s first laboratory colony of Aedes vexans mosquitoes, a species native to the British isles, to study whether they could harbour diseases like West Nile virus, Rift Valley fever, Zika or Japanese encephalitis.

News.title: What I saw in a week on the front line of Afghanistan’s hunger crisis
News.content:
May 15 and 16, 2026

It is the weekend, a small moment to rest, although there is still a lot of work waiting for me. A week in the field does not mean that work in Kabul stops. I try to catch up on my emails and have a planned online interview for an international staff position – since in Europe, Friday is a normal working day. I also review parts of new proposals for donors and our financial planning.

On Saturday, however, I take a short break. Together with the base management team in Helmand, we visit a historical site called Qala-e-Bost, believed to have been built around 3,000 years ago. It is a rare moment to step away from work, followed by lunch with the team.

May 17, 2026

Sunday morning, the first working day of the week, we visit Basrhan Sub Health Centre, run by one of our local partners. As a nurse and former nurse trainer, I feel very much in my element in these health centres. It allows me to engage easily with the team and discuss their work.

I speak with the outreach officer and the vaccinator. They explain that this facility supports 18 outreach locations, each visited at least once a month. They provide vaccinations, raise awareness, and connect communities to the health centre. These visits often take place in simple settings, like mosques.

Immunisation is now well accepted. In the beginning, there was some resistance, but trust has grown over time. Every child is tracked, and if a child misses a vaccination, community health volunteers follow up at home. For extra polio vaccinations, this is carefully recorded by marking a finger of the child – helping ensure that no child is missed. The goal is clear: a polio-free Afghanistan.

I also speak with a mother. She is wearing a burka, so I cannot see her face. She tells me she is 22 years old and holds her 12-month-old son on her lap. She came because he has a fever, but I see a healthy child – something that stands out after my time in the TFU.

She brings her child regularly for follow-up and growth monitoring and the child has never been in a treatment program for malnutrition. She speaks positively about the services. “We are lucky,” she says. “The staff treat us well, and we have access to care in our community.”

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford set for Man Utd reunion for the first time in 18 months as transfer options run out
Sports.content:
MARCUS RASHFORD is set to reunite with his Manchester United teammates for the first time in 18 months this weekend.

Rashford is scheduled to travel to Dublin for United’s pre-season training camp on Sunday as he will have completed his mandatory three-week post-World Cup break.



Kobbie Mainoo and Lisandro Martinez are also expected to report this weekend following their presence in the United States three weeks ago.

Rashford, 28, has not trained with teammates since January 2025 due to separate loan spells with Aston Villa and Barcelona.



During that last session, Rashford and fellow United stars playfully hit Ruben Amorim while he ran a birthday gauntlet. He joined Villa five days later following his continued omission from Amorim’s matchday squads.

Barcelona passed on the option to buy Rashford for £26million in June, instead moving for fellow England left winger Anthony Gordon in a £69m deal.

Villa also brought in Alejandro Garnacho, Rashford’s former left-wing competitor at United, on a season-long loan with an obligation to buy for £42.5m.

Rashford and Garnacho were part of a five-man ‘bomb squad’ at United’s Carrington training complex last summer, when they were ordered by Amorim to report for separate training times to the main squad.

Although Amorim was sacked in January and head coach Michael Carrick has stabilised United, the imminent reunion is still awkward for all parties.

Rashford publicly declared his wish to join Barcelona permanently in May and doubled down on his desire to leave permanently during the World Cup.



But the England international’s £325,000-a-week salary has effectively blocked a permanent departure.

On the eve of the World Cup, Rashford posted a brief message on his Instagram page thanking Barcelona, Villa, England and their respective coaches, with no mention of United.

United are also conspicuous by their absence on the bios of Rashford’s verified Instagram and Twitter accounts. Rashford’s Facebook page has been dormant since December 2021.

Senior United figures were surprised by Barcelona’s decision not to buy Rashford, which has left them out of options.

That has caused United to park plans to bring in a winger. Their focus has shifted onto a full back to reinforce their left-hand side.



Rashford is not entertaining the prospect of moving to Turkey or Saudi Arabia when he is aiming to be in Tuchel’s squad for the 2028 European Championship.

Carrick was a teammate, captain, coach and caretaker manager to Rashford over a period of nearly six years. Carrick’s non-confrontational style should avoid a repeat of the treatment Rashford copped under Amorim.

But Rashford also crossed former manager Erik ten Hag over a birthday party hours after the October 2023 3-0 home defeat to Manchester City and a midweek jaunt to Belfast in January 2024.

RECOMMENDED STORIES



United sources have repeatedly stressed they will not let Rashford leave on another season-long loan. The academy graduate is under contract until 2028.

Rashford’s first appearance back at United could be in their final pre-season friendly next Saturday against AC Milan, who are managed by Amorim.

Sports.title: Six wingers Arsenal could turn to after Vinicius Jr transfer snub including Rashford and two hijacks of Prem rivals
Sports.content:
ARSENAL have been forced into a rethink after their pursuit of Vinicius Jr ended in failure.

The Gunners audacious pursuit of the Brazilian winger ultimately ended in him snubbing a move to the Emirates to sign a new deal with Real Madrid that will keep him at the club until 2032.



Vinicius, 26, had entered the final year of his contract at the Bernabeu and was open to a move to the Premier League if he did not pen new terms, though an improved contract offer worth £480,000-a-week proved too good to turn down.

That has left Mikel Arteta‘s squad with a gaping hole in their left wing in terms of a lucrative signing, with the club open to selling Gabriel Martinelli and £34m new signing Christos Tzolis’ only experience at this level an underwhelming spell at Norwich.



A number of options remain open to them in the market, including World Cup winners, Champions League winners and Premier League stars.

SunSport have looked at six potential signings Gunners sporting director Andrea Berta could swoop for to bolster the squad’s firepower.

Bradley Barcola

With Vinicius and Yan Diomande both off the table, Paris Saint-Germain‘s Bradley Barcola appears to be the most valuable attacker remaining on the market.

The Frenchman has two years left on his deal with the Ligue 1 and Champions League champions, and is being targeted in a £100m move by Liverpool after informing the club he won’t be signing fresh terms.

Arsenal were willing to break the British transfer record for Vinicius, meaning they would certainly be able to get their elbows out in moving for the 23-year-old – even though PSG reportedly want £145m to sell.

A frighteningly quick and ruthlessly devastating winger, Barcola was also a star at the World Cup and would be the sort of lucrative signing fans demand.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Marcus Rashford

Only three seasons ago, Marcus Rashford was banging in 30 goals in all competitions for Manchester United.

Yet following two loan spells at Aston Villa and Barcelona, which came after he was frozen out at United by then-boss Ruben Amorim, the England World Cup star is available for a cut price transfer.

The 28-year-old could have left for £40m this summer thanks to a release clause – not made available to Liverpool or Manchester City – but could now move for even less after that clause expired on July 15.

Rashford was previously linked with Arsenal, and Arteta and Co would be hard-pressed to find a more explosive Prem proven left winger for such a relatively small fee.



Rafael Leao

Rafael Leao is another player who, a few seasons ago, was one of the most wanted stars in all of Europe.

However, he is now an outcast at AC Milan and the Italian club are looking to sell, with talks for a move to Galatasaray currently ongoing.

But should Arsenal come calling, it’s hard to imagine Leao turning down the chance to sign for the Gunners.

On his day he is an incredibly gifted player, and while there are concerns over his defensive work rate Arteta would surely be able to mastermind a plan to get the best out of the Portuguese.

Pedro Neto

Another star linked with Arsenal in the past, Pedro Neto is the perfect winger for an Arteta team, with graft, versatility and lethality in the final third all ticked off.

The Chelsea star registered 10 goals and 10 assists in all comps last year, an output only bettered by Joao Pedro and Enzo Fernandez – 26 and 22 goal contributions respectively.

Enzo Maresca, his former boss at Stamford Bridge, is eyeing a reunion with Neto at Man City, with the Blues reportedly demanding £70m to sell.

That is the going rate for a good-level winger these days, and strengthening themselves while also weakening a rival can only be a good thing for Arsenal.



Cody Gakpo

That same logic applies with Cody Gakpo, who is edging closer to a Liverpool exit.

Tottenham are the main team linked with the Dutchman, who has hit a half century of goals for the Reds since joining in January 2022.

The Anfield outfit reportedly want around £60m for the 27-year-old, who can play as both a winger and central attacking option.

Also, gazumping north London rivals Spurs on another signing would also be something the Gunners fanbase find hilariously sweet as well.



Nico Williams

Nico Williams endured an injury-hit campaign as he was hampered by a persistent pubalgia issue, yet still managed to become a world champion after featuring in Spain‘s World Cup winning team.

The 24-year-old has a contract at Athletic Bilbao running to 2035, but matching his reported release clause of £77m could naturally tempt him into a move.

Arsenal and Barcelona have been heavily linked with Williams in the last few summers.



If they can get the Spaniard fit and firing again, there are few left wingers in world football who are better.

Sports.title: Legendary Premier League goalkeeper slams Robert Sanchez… and urges Chelsea to make transfer for ex-Liverpool star
Sports.content:
PREMIER LEAGUE icon Shay Given has urged Chelsea to sign a former Liverpool star to replace Robert Sanchez in goal at Stamford Bridge.

Sanchez has been highly criticised since arriving in a £25million transfer from Brighton three years ago.



Many fans have called for him to be replaced as Chelsea‘s No1 – and former Prem star Given believes that Caoimhin Kelleher would be the ideal candidate to step in.

Kelleher impressed last season after joining Brentford from Liverpool and made 37 Premier League appearances.



Given says that Chelsea should make an attempt to sign him before the new season kicks off.

Speaking to BOYLE Sports recently, he explained: “Could Chelsea or Newcastle come in for Kelleher this summer? Possibly.



“It would depend on Liverpool and whether they can activate any sort of clause to sign him themselves to stop another club picking him up.”

Given also expressed frustration with Sanchez and his tendency to make high-profile mistakes.

He continued: “I stuck up for him a lot last season but he does keep going over old ground with some of the mistakes he makes.

“He can pull off some unbelievable saves and you think this guy’s the real deal only for him to have a mad rush of blood to the head at the edge of the box and halve someone in two.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

“I feel that signing a new goalkeeper is something that could happen at Chelsea this summer, and if it’s not Kelleher maybe it’ll be someone else, but that’s a position they need to strengthen in this window, not the next window, but now.

“Xabi Alonso is in place now and he might have seen enough from Robert Sanchez. I’m not sure.

“I definitely think Newcastle and Chelsea want the strength in that position and Kelleher would be a good signing for either of them.”

The former Manchester City and Stoke goalkeeper suggested that Kelleher could one day return to Liverpool – but only when Alisson leaves.



But in the meantime, he says the 27-year-old could also be a great signing for Newcastle – who have struggled in the transfer window so far.

Given added: “A lot will depend on Allison because you wouldn’t bring Kelleher back right now if Alisson’s staying for the next two seasons.

“Chelsea are the club who have surprised me a little bit by not bringing someone in, and I say that as someone who does like Robert Sanchez.”

Sports.title: Mo Salah ‘set to be reunited with Liverpool flop’ as Trabzonspor working on transfer for £400k-a-week striker
Sports.content:
MO SALAH could be joined by a familiar face at Trabzonspor with the Turkish club reportedly working on another ambitious deal.

Salah, 34, penned a two-year contract worth about £360,000 a week to join the side that finished third in the Turkish Super Lig last season.



And the challengers’ spending spree looks set to continue.

According to The i Paper, Trabzonspor are keen to reunite Salah with his ex-Liverpool team-mate, Darwin Nunez.



The Uruguayan earns about £400,000 a week at Al-Hilal but was chucked out of their Saudi Pro League squad when Karim Benzema joined in February.

Nunez, 27, was only eligible to play in the AFC Champions League Elite from then on, and he finished the campaign with a modest nine goals in 24 games.

Reports in Turkey state that Trabzonspor are ‘increasing the pressure’ in their pursuit of the centre-forward.

Al-Hilal, who splashed £46million on Nunez last year, could let him go for as little as £17m.

Tottenham have also been keeping tabs on the cut-price star but have not made a formal offer.

Nunez failed to catch fire at Liverpool, scoring just 40 goals in 143 games after what was then a club-record £85m move from Benfica in 2022.

Manchester United goalkeeper Andre Onana has joined on a second season-long loan, while ex-Manchester City defender Stefan Savic and former Evertonian John Lundstram have both played for the Trabzon side since 2024.

Ex-Southampton giant Paul Onuachu was the joint top scorer in the league last season with 22 goals but risks being frozen out at Trabzonspor if Nunez takes his place up top.

Sports.title: ‘Never heard a bigger load of rubbish’ – Ex-British tennis No1 slams Man Utd legend Paul Scholes in scathing rant
Sports.content:
GREG RUSEDSKI slammed Paul Scholes in a scathing rant – then challenged him to a game of tennis.

The former British No1 even hit out at the ex-Manchester United midfielder’s take as the “biggest load of rubbish in my life”.



Scholes, 51, ruffled his feathers during an episode of The Good, The Bad and The Football podcast with co-hosts Paddy McGuinness and Nicky Butt.

During the show, he claimed football is a more physically demanding sport than tennis.



Scholes – who played 718 times for the Red Devils between 1994 and 2013 – moaned about tennis: “Every two minutes you go and have your nice little glass of orange juice.

“You can play it when you’re 50, tennis. Play it when you’re 70, tennis.”



Then he added: “Football is much more demanding than tennis.”

But Rusedski was having none of it.

The Canada-born tennis star, winner of 15 career titles and former world No4, fired back in a brutal response.

And now he wants Scholes to walk the walk after talking the talk.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Rusedski, 52, told talkSPORT: “You can’t compare football to tennis. There’s no question about it.

“I was watching Paul Scholes saying, ‘Oh, football’s so much harder than tennis.’

“I’ve never heard a bigger load of rubbish in my life.

“Come on, Scholesy, let’s go play some tennis and see how long you can last out there.



“Having to move directions, no substitutions.

“There is no question, physically, tennis is much more demanding.

“With the travel schedule, with competing, with having to support and fund your own team.

“There are so many more things that make tennis a much more difficult sport.”

Sports.content:
Rodri's agent drops transfer bombshell as Man City star decides future

Real Madrid were long considered the favourites to sign Rodri before Barcelona entered the running, with the midfielder having entered the final 12 months of his contract at Manchester City

Sports.title: Argentina at odds with England as statement released on FIFA president Gianni Infantino
Sports.content:
Argentina at odds with England as statement released on FIFA president Gianni Infantino

FIFA president Gianni Infantino has split world football this summer, with football associations sharing statements about his premiership, with Argentina and England again at odds

Gianni Infantino retains FIFA board’s support after crisis meeting

The Argentine Football Association have shared a statement in support of FIFA president Gianni Infantino's premiership over the last decade. That stance is at odds with the Football Association, who are withdrawing support for his re-election to a fourth term, much like the Football Association of Wales (FAW).

‌



The Football Associations of Finland, Serbia and Sweden have also done likewise ahead of the 77th FIFA Congress in mid-March. That is when the next presidential election will take place in Morocco.

‌



Denmark and Norway also oppose his re-election. Argentina, however, have now joined Egypt and several others in publicly supporting Infantino.

‌



View 2 Images Lionel Messi's Argentina have backed FIFA president Gianni Infantino (Image: Getty Images)

The AFA statement, translated into English from Spanish, reads: "Of our highest consideration, on behalf of the Argentine Football Association (AFA), and its Executive Committee, we address you, dear President, and through your worthy intermediary the FIFA board, to express our support for the management carried out during the last 10 years, which had as its main axes the development of football throughout the world and institutional solidity based on a clear governance model. stable and transparent.

"In this sense, in relation to the recent events that are public knowledge, we must recognise the decision of the Administration to withdraw a project that generated, within the football family and from its inception, many more uncertainties than certainties.

‌



"That is why it is worth highlighting the acceptance of the errors made in this process and the apology expressed in the heartfelt message displayed to the 211 member associations of FIFA. Prioritising governance standards is a fundamental pillar for strengthening good relations between FIFA, its member associations and the confederations.

View 2 Images The Confederation of African Football have backed Gianni Infantino, too (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

"In the same way, and as we have already expressed, you are leading a management that led to a profound transformation of FIFA, which opened the doors of the organisation to all member associations and confederations, so that with a frank and direct dialogue, we can, together, continue to promote football at all levels and disciplines.

‌



"From our point of view, this transformation was based on a model of transparent governance, respect for statutory structures and the monitoring of democratic procedures, essential principles for the football family to be united, firm and working to continue generating improvements in sports and institutions, which have an impact on a better quality of life for millions of human beings who practice our beloved sport.

"Accordingly, with the upcoming FIFA Congress approaching, the Association that I proudly preside over firmly believes and reaffirms that the way forward is to continue to work under your leadership, so that we can continue to develop better and even more inclusive football."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



The FA's last public statement was made last weekend regarding the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal being withdrawn by Infantino. They also acknowledged a statement from UEFA welcoming the move.

An FA spokesperson said: "We fully support UEFA's position. It is time for a full and robust review of FIFA's leadership and governance to ensure that the global game is run transparently, for the benefit of all 211 member nations and with the long-term stewardship of football at its heart."

Sports.title: Michael Carrick's telling response after being told to sell eight players by Man Utd hero
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick's telling response after being told to sell eight players by Man Utd hero

Manchester United boss Michael Carrick has not yet followed transfer instructions previously laid out by Paul Scholes

View 4 Images Manchester United boss Michael Carrick was told by a former team-mate to sell some players (Image: Getty)

Michael Carrick has not sanctioned any major sales so far this summer at Manchester United. This is despite United hero Paul Scholes recommending eight stars be sold.

‌



Carrick is currently taking charge of his first pre-season and there are just a few weeks until the Premier League returns. With only three first-team signings made so far in Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Karl Darlow, more additions are expected.

‌



However, there has yet to be a major exit from the club, aside from Casemiro's departure. In April, Scholes was asked for a series of United stars who were surplus to requirements and of the eight players he listed, only one appears set to leave as things stand.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

7 Man Utd players face uncertain futures as part of huge summer overhaul of squad READ MORE :

Jadon Sancho's Man Utd decline and manager trend leaves unwanted star in awkward spot READ MORE :

Joshua Zirkzee was among the players that Scholes believed should be sold and the former Bologna forward is edging closer to a return to Italy. La Gazzetta dello Sport claims that Zirkzee is willing to join Juventus, who are pursuing a loan arrangement with an option to buy.

View 4 Images Zirkzee could be on the move soon (Image: Getty)

‌



Scholes and Carrick spent seven seasons together in United's midfield during their playing days. However, whilst the pundit's suggestion to move on Zirkzee may materialise, the other seven stars Scholes mentioned could all remain part of United's squad next term, with Carrick's response clear.

The 51-year-old stressed the importance of United revamping their defence. Speaking on The Good, The Bad and The Football podcast, Scholes said of Leny Yoro: "I think he's struggled, me. I think there's something in there, I think he needs a bit of time, but if you had to make a choice now, I'd probably sell him."

He also argued that the shift away from ex-boss Ruben Amorim's three-at-the-back system would have implications for Noussair Mazraoui. Mazraoui has been linked with a departure this summer, though he remains part of Carrick's side. Highly-rated defender Yoro has also expressed a desire to make his mark at United next season.

‌



View 4 Images Yoro was a surprise inclusion (Image: Getty)

Turning to midfield, Scholes felt Manuel Ugarte would depart and the Uruguayan was linked with a move before picking up an injury at the World Cup. Mason Mount also featured on Scholes' eight-man list, though the England international has caught the eye during pre-season.

‌



Additionally, Scholes felt the moment had arrived to say goodbye to Harry Maguire, who continues to have a key role at United. He said: "I'm thinking about a Manchester United team you want to win the league and the Champions League and that's where United should be aiming. I'm not sure you'd do that with Maguire."

Elsewhere, United have held an interest in Newcastle United full-back Lewis Hall in the transfer window. Focusing on the left-back position, Scholes previously urged the club to offload long-serving Luke Shaw due to doubts about his reliability, despite him having featured in every Premier League fixture last season. He was equally prepared to let Patrick Dorgu leave.

Scholes said on Dorgu: "They brought him in as a wing-back and he's not really played much there. I'd probably sell. I'm not sure what position he is. Again, if you keep him then he's just a squad player."

Overall, of the eight players Scholes recommended be sold, only Zirkzee appears set for an imminent exit. There has been little speculation regarding the remaining seven of Yoro, Mazraoui, Shaw, Dorgu, Mount, Ugarte and Maguire.

Sports.title: Arsenal's 10 highest Premier League sales – and why it speaks volumes for Andrea Berta
Sports.content:
Arsenal's 10 highest Premier League sales – and why it speaks volumes for Andrea Berta

Arsenal sporting director Andrea Berta has plenty on his plate as the Premier League champions bid to kick on this summer

View 4 Images Andrea Berta has a lot on his plate as Arsenal's sporting director (Image: Getty)

Arsenal's sporting director Andrea Berta has overseen some important signings since joining the club, with more expected to follow. But sales have been a challenge for the Gunners, with the problem persisting long before the Italian took up the role.

‌



The north London side's record sale still sits at just £35million. To put that into context, only three of the other 19 Premier League sides - Sunderland, Hull and Coventry - have lower records. Arsenal simply aren't selling well.

‌



A total of three sales this summer have raised less than £40m combined, with Karl Hein, Jakub Kiwior and Leandro Trossard completing permanent exits. Arsenal have already paid in the region of £34m for both Piero Hincapie and Christos Tzolis, whilst the anticipated move for Bruno Guimaraes will see them more than double their outlay.

‌



When it comes to record sales, it's telling that the top four spots are occupied by transfers from the Arsene Wenger era, and the club simply aren't keeping up with the big-money exits that clubs like Chelsea and Manchester City sanction. Here are their 10 most lucrative offloadings, in reverse order, per Transfermarkt figures.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Two Champions League rule changes announced by UEFA ahead of new season READ MORE :

Ex-Arsenal star makes winning return to English football with League Two club READ MORE :

10. Joe Willock (£25.2m)

Willock's move to Newcastle was a case of striking whilst the iron was hot. The midfielder scored eight goals during a loan spell at St James' Park, driving up his value and convincing Arsenal to cash in.

‌



The England Under-21 international hasn't yet matched that goal tally across more than 100 games as a permanent Newcastle player, though his role became far less attacking under Eddie Howe. He was used sparingly last term, struggling to displace Bruno Guimaraes and Sandro Tonali.

9. Eddie Nketiah (£25.4m)

Another recent sale, Nketiah demonstrated Premier League pedigree in an Arsenal shirt when he scored a hat-trick against Sheffield United in 2023. Months later, Crystal Palace took the plunge with a big-money bid and the striker - battling with the likes of Kai Havertz and Gabriel Jesus for opportunities - decided to try his luck elsewhere.

View 4 Images Nketiah is about to embark on his third season at Crystal Palace (Image: Getty)

‌



Get Arsenal's new 2026/27 home kit This article contains affiliate links, we will receive a commission on any sales we generate from it. Learn more £85 Fanatics Buy Now on Fanatics Product Description Arsenal have launched their new home kit for the 2026/27 season, said to incorporate classic Arsenal design features that tie into the club's heritage.

The Eagles could end up paying even more for the England international if conditions for add-ons are met. However, his second season at Selhurst Park was cut short by injury and he will hope for a fresh start under new boss Pierre Sage.

8. Folarin Balogun (£25.7m)

Balogun, like Nketiah, moved in search of more regular first-team football. Again, Arsenal got good money for a fringe player when he followed up a 21-goal Ligue 1 season at Reims with a move to their rivals Monaco.

‌



The United States international top-scored for his club last term and thrived for his country at the World Cup. There's no guarantee he would have developed at the same speed in North London, though.

7. Alex Iwobi (£26m)

Academy graduate Iwobi grew into his role at Arsenal, scoring in the 2019 Europa League final defeat to Chelsea and playing 100 league games for the Gunners. But the arrival of Nicolas Pepe meant he was considered disposable.

Marco Silva signed the Nigerian international for Everton but was gone within months in a tough first season. Things have gone better for Iwobi after a reunion with Silva at Fulham, where he has thrived in a deeper midfield role than the one he occupied at his boyhood club.

‌



6. Robin van Persie (£26.3m)

View 4 Images Van Persie's United move was one of 2012's most talked-about transfers (Image: Getty)

The £26m paid by Manchester United for Van Persie in 2012 was worth a great deal more then than now. Still, it's telling that a deal from more than a decade ago is one of the top 10 on this list. And it's not the only one.

The Dutch striker's move was hugely dramatic at the time, with plenty of fans turning on a former favourite. United will have considered the move a success after his goals brought an immediate league title but the following two years were less fruitful for player and club and he left for Fenerbahce in 2015.

‌



5. Emile Smith Rowe (£27.2m)

Academy graduate Smith Rowe made a fast start as a teenager but found himself overtaken in the pecking order during Mikel Arteta's tenure. He left for Fulham in 2024, with Mikel Merino brought in by Arteta just weeks later.

The three-cap England international has remained a solid presence in Fulham's midfield, featuring in 71 of 76 available league matches. However, he has not looked close to a Three Lions recall, nearly four years on from his most recent cap.

‌



4. Cesc Fabregas (£29.1m)

Your eyes don't deceive you. That's a 2011 sale in the top five - by way of comparison, Chelsea have sold 20 players for more money since then, give or take the margin of error for conversions between Euros and Pounds.

It was one of two big-money moves for Fabregas in his career, with the Spaniard also joining Chelsea in 2014 for a similar amount to the Barcelona deal after Arsenal opted against bringing him back. He won two Premier League titles with the Blues and has now made an impressive start to his managerial career with Como.

3. Alexis Sanchez (£29.1m)

You might not even want to count this one, given the fact that it came as part of an effective swap deal. We're leaving it in just to emphasise the task facing Berta as he looks to succeed where his predecessors struggled.

‌



Sanchez moved to United in 2018, with Henrikh Mkhitaryan joining Arsenal from the Red Devils. The Londoners came out of the deal a little better but neither club had huge success from the arrangement.

2. Nicolas Anelka (£30m)

Those tricky conversion fees mean reports vary for how much Anelka went for in Pounds. Even so, it says a lot that a sale from 1999 features on this list.

View 4 Images Anelka joined Real Madrid more than a quarter of a century ago (Image: Getty)

‌



Anelka was an example of Arsenal turning a huge profit on a player they signed for less than £1m from Paris Saint-Germain. He would go on to make more than 500 career league appearances across several countries and also played for France at the World Cup and European Championships.

1. Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain (£35m)

Arsenal's record sale remains the £35m they received when Oxlade-Chamberlain joined Liverpool in 2017. The England international became a Premier League and Champions League winner during his time at Anfield but was plagued by injury.

Despite spending six years as a Liverpool player, he made just 103 league appearances. He left for Besiktas on a free transfer in 2023 and is now at Celtic.

Sports.title: Gibbs' Lions deal makes him NFL's highest-paid running back ever
Sports.content:
Jahmyr Gibbs is set to become the highest-paid running back in NFL history having agreed to a new three-year deal worth up to $75.7m (£56.3m) with the Detroit Lions.

Gibbs' agents Athletes First announced the deal Thursday, hours after he took the field for the first time since the Lions' training camp started. His agents also noted the new contract includes $51.5m (£38.3m) guaranteed for the Pro Bowler.

Two days earlier, Atlanta briefly made Bijan Robinson the NFL's highest-paid running back in history.

Gibbs had been participating in meetings at camp, but Thursday was his first appearance on the field, an indication the Lions and his agents were close to a deal. Gibbs held his right arm high and gave a thumbs-up when asked if an agreement was close as he walked off the practice field.

Gibbs changed his jersey number from 26 to 0 ahead of the 2025 season and rushed for 1,223 yards and 13 touchdowns, and had 77 receptions for 616 yards and five scores.

Sports.title: Undrafted King leads Panthers to comeback win vs Cardinals in Hall of Fame game
Sports.content:
Undrafted rookie quarterback Haynes King ran in on the final play to give the Carolina Panthers a 33-30 victory over the Arizona Cardinals in the Hall of Fame game that kicked off the NFL preseason on Thursday night.

King, who was the Atlantic Coast Conference Player of the Year last season at Georgia Tech, was 21 of 34 for 180 yards and two touchdowns. He ran for 39 yards and the winning score.

"Well, that was a lot of fun. Just the back and forth of it. Just a really good game," Panthers coach Dave Canales said.

"The guys were resilient and finish is what we preach as a team. We practice for these situations, end of half, end of game. Haynes did a fantastic job, just keeping the play alive, doing whatever he had to do, run it, throw it. Really proud of the group."

Sports.title: Is red-hot Norrie now favourite to win Montreal? Brit dumps out third seed De Minaur
Sports.content:
Five years on from winning his biggest title in Indian Wells, Britain's Cameron Norrie has found his form to dump out third seed Alex de Minaur and reach the fourth round of the National Bank Open in Montreal.

Down 7-5 5-2 with De Minaur on match point, Norrie turned the tables by winning 11 out of the next 13 games to beat the Australian 5-7 7-6 (7-5) 6-1.

Norrie, who has climbed above Arthur Fery to No 36 in the live rankings will become the new British No 1, but the former Wimbledon semi-finalist has ambitions of collecting the second Masters title of his career with Frenchman Arthur Fils up next.
