World.title: Anambra First Lady, Nonye Soludo wins BudgIT 2026 Active Citizens Award
World.content:
Nonye Soludo

By Vincent Ujumadu

AWKA – Wife of the Anambra State Governor, Dr. Nonye Soludo, has emerged winner of the health activism category at the 2026 BudgIT Active Citizens Awards.

The award, in its third edition, recognises individuals and organisations making outstanding contributions to civic engagement, social development, accountability and sustainable development across Nigeria.

Mrs Soludo was honoured for her efforts in advancing preventive healthcare, community wellness and public health advocacy through her non-governmental organisation, the Healthy Living with Nonye Soludo Initiative.

She emerged winner ahead of Nigerian health and gender rights advocate, Ramatu Ada Ochekliye, and public health and social impact professional, Sidney Sampson, after a rigorous selection process that assessed nominees based on innovation, impact, sustainability, inclusion, leadership and measurable community outcomes.

Receiving the award, Mrs Soludo described the recognition as a humbling honour and a renewed call to serve with greater commitment.

She said the award belonged to members of the Healthy Living with Nonye Soludo Initiative, partners, healthcare workers, volunteers, community leaders and residents of Anambra State who had embraced the vision of wellness and healthy living.

“Like a family driven by one common goal, we have shown that when communities take ownership of their health, lasting transformation becomes very possible,” she said.

Mrs Soludo expressed appreciation to BudgIT, Civic Hive and the Ford Foundation for the recognition, adding that it would motivate the initiative to expand its reach and continue promoting healthier communities.

In a statement, Senior Special Assistant to the wife of the governor, Mr. Daniel Ezeigwe, said the award reflected growing national recognition of the impact of Mrs Soludo’s healthy living campaign, which he described as a model for promoting preventive healthcare and healthy lifestyles.

Ezeigwe said that since becoming Anambra First Lady, Dr. Soludo had championed several people-centred initiatives, including statewide fitness campaigns, maternal and child health advocacy, nutrition education, environmental sanitation, the Healthy Living Pad Bank for schoolgirls, free seed distribution to households and the Nonye’s Healthy Living Pap Initiative aimed at tackling childhood malnutrition.

“These programmes have touched thousands of lives while reinforcing the importance of prevention as the foundation of a healthier society,” he said.

He added that the recognition further highlighted Mrs Soludo’s commitment to improving the health and wellbeing of Anambra residents while contributing to Nigeria’s broader public health development.

World.title: Mental health crisis: Fewer than 300 psychiatrists serve over 200m Nigerians — Sheikh
World.content:
… Demands urgent implementation of Mental Health Act, stronger funding

By Chioma Obinna

A Professor of Psychiatry at Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria, Prof. Taiwo Lateef Sheikh, has said that Nigeria is facing a deepening mental health crisis, with fewer than 300 psychiatrists available to serve a population of over 200 million people.

Sheikh, a member of the Advisory Committee to Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, Africa CDC, said the severe shortage of mental health professionals, inadequate funding and poor access to community-based services were widening the gap between Nigerians who need mental healthcare and those who receive it.

He spoke at the Mental Health Leadership and Advocacy Public Lecture, where he called for urgent implementation of the Mental Health Act and stronger policy, financing and legislative reforms to strengthen Nigeria’s mental health system.

According to him, mental health remains one of the most neglected areas of healthcare, particularly in Africa, despite its enormous impact on individuals, families, communities and national economies.

“Legislation provides the skeleton, policy provides the direction, and financing provides the muscle. Closing the mental health systems gap requires all three to move together,” Sheikh said.

He said Nigeria’s Mental Health Act, signed into law in December 2022, represented a major milestone but warned that the law would have limited impact without adequate funding, trained personnel, functional services and effective implementation.

“Without legislation, policy is just paper. Without policy, legislation has no direction,” he stated.

Sheikh said mental health services in Nigeria remained concentrated largely in federally owned tertiary psychiatric hospitals, most of which are located in state capitals and therefore out of reach of many people requiring care.

He noted that although mental health had been recognised as a component of primary healthcare in Nigeria, mental health services remained largely unavailable at the primary healthcare level.

The psychiatrist said the country’s shortage of specialists was compounded by inadequate numbers of psychologists, psychiatric nurses and other mental health professionals.

He said trained psychiatric nurses were sometimes deployed to other duties because of the absence of functional mental health units and inadequate commitment to mental healthcare.

Sheikh also expressed concern over poor financing, noting that mental health receives less than 3.5 per cent of the health budget, with more than 90 per cent of available mental health resources going to hospitals.

He argued that such an arrangement was unsustainable and inconsistent with the goal of universal health coverage.

“The treatment gap is about demand versus supply. Demand is all over, but barriers restrict access,” he said.

To bridge the gap, Sheikh advocated a decentralised mental health system in which most people receive care at the lowest appropriate level, including self-care, community services and primary healthcare, while patients requiring specialised intervention are referred to higher levels of care.

He called for greater integration of mental healthcare into primary healthcare and the adoption of task-shifting, whereby trained nurses, community health workers and other non-specialist health workers provide mental health services under appropriate supervision.

“Treat at the lowest level. Integrate into primary healthcare. Task-shift. No discharge to nowhere,” he said.

According to him, the “no discharge to nowhere” principle requires patients leaving psychiatric hospitals to be linked to community-based follow-up services rather than being discharged without continuing care.

He said common conditions such as depression could be managed at the primary healthcare level through appropriate training and the World Health Organisation’s Mental Health Gap Action Programme, mhGAP.

“Seventy per cent of mental health problems can be treated by trained doctors, nurses and primary health workers with adequate supervision and support,” Sheikh said.

The professor warned that neglecting mental health could undermine Nigeria’s economic and social development, stressing that untreated mental health conditions impose significant costs on individuals, families, workplaces and governments.

“Africa needs to invest in mental health as mental health is not only a key part of healthcare but also of education and labour. If ignored, the economic development of the countries in Africa will be compromised,” he said.

“The message is clear for policymakers: invest in mental health and get good returns.”

Sheikh also called for mental health to be integrated into education, employment, social protection and other sectors, arguing that mental healthcare cannot be addressed by the health sector alone.

He urged stronger suicide prevention strategies, anti-stigma programmes and measures to protect the rights of people living with mental health conditions.

The psychiatrist said Nigeria’s mental health legislation had historically been rooted in colonial-era laws focused largely on custodial care rather than treatment, recovery and human rights.

He noted that mental health legislation in Nigeria dates back to 1916 and evolved into a law in 1959, retaining its colonial orientation for decades before the country eventually moved towards a modern rights-based framework.

According to him, sustained advocacy by mental health professionals, civil society organisations, lawmakers, development partners and other stakeholders played a critical role in the eventual passage of the Mental Health Act.

He, however, stressed that the passage of the law was only the beginning.

“The Mental Health Act is a major achievement, but the real test is implementation,” he said.

Sheikh called for sustainable domestic financing, stronger governance, reliable mental health data, adequate human resources, essential medicines and technologies, as well as effective monitoring of the implementation of the law and national mental health policy.

He also advocated mental health parity in health insurance, anti-discrimination measures, school and workplace mental health programmes and greater protection of patients’ rights.

The psychiatrist urged policymakers to involve people with lived experience of mental health conditions in the development of policies and legislation, saying their experiences were essential to building humane and effective services.

He warned that stigma and discrimination continue to prevent many Nigerians from seeking help, often forcing people to present at hospitals only when their conditions have become severe.

“Protecting the rights of persons with mental illness is not optional. Modern mental health legislation must be rights-based, promote autonomy and consent, provide the least restrictive care and ensure access to appropriate services,” he said.

He called on the Federal Government and states to move mental healthcare closer to communities by integrating services into primary healthcare facilities and strengthening referral and follow-up systems.

Sheikh also urged government to reduce dependence on donor funding by providing sustainable domestic resources for mental health.

He said Nigeria could no longer afford to treat mental health as a peripheral issue, warning that the country’s development aspirations would remain threatened unless mental health was made a national priority.

“Mental health is a significant part of development,” he said.

Also speaking, Emeritus Professor of Psychiatry at the University of Ibadan and Director of the WHO Collaborating Centre, Ibadan, Prof. Oye Gureje, stressed the importance of strong leadership and sustained advocacy in tackling Nigeria’s mental healthcare challenges and driving reforms across Africa

Gureje explained that the Mental Health Leadership and Advocacy Programme, now in its 13th edition, was established to develop leaders capable of influencing policy, mobilising stakeholders and championing improvements in mental health systems.

He noted that there is growing global recognition that “there is no health without mental health,” stressing that mental disorders remain common, underdiagnosed and inadequately treated despite their impact on individuals, families and national productivity.

According to him, inadequate funding, weak political commitment and poor implementation of policies have contributed significantly to the treatment gap.

He said trained leaders and advocates were needed to keep mental health on the policy agenda, raise public awareness and pressure governments to prioritise quality mental healthcare.

Speaking, the Head of the Division of Disease Control and Prevention at the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, Africa CDC, Dr Mohammed Abdulaziz, also called for stronger leadership, reform of outdated mental health laws and adoption of a public health approach to close Africa’s widening mental healthcare gap.

Abdulaziz said the Africa CDC Mental Health Leadership Programme was established to develop leaders capable of driving policy reforms and strengthening mental health systems across the continent.

He said the programme rests on four pillars: the Kofi Annan Fellowship, the Field Epidemiology Training Programme, FETP, short leadership and advocacy courses, and support for civil society organisations and people with lived experience of mental health conditions.

He disclosed that Africa CDC was supporting countries including The Gambia and Sierra Leone to modernise their mental health laws, while encouraging other countries to adopt rights-based legislation.

Abdulaziz urged African governments to replace archaic laws that stigmatise people living with mental health conditions, strengthen surveillance and research, and generate evidence to guide policymaking.

He called for a whole-of-government and whole-of-society approach to mental health.

“We cannot continue to say mental health is underfunded without making deliberate efforts to change the narrative,” Abdulaziz said, reaffirming Africa CDC’s commitment to supporting mental health reforms across the continent.

World.title: More appalling APC arrogance! By Donu Kogbara
World.content:
Donu Kogbara

Last week, I complained about the arrogance displayed by Dave Umahi, the Minister of Works, who has a lot of questions to answer around the mysterious death in his compound of an attractive young female nurse.

This week, I will focus on another example of APC arrogance.

Following a visit to the presidential villa by the Catholic Bishops Conference of Nigeria (CBCN), His Eminence, Cardinal John Olorunfemi

Onaiyekan, the emeritus archbishop of Abuja, gave an interview in which he described Tinubu’s nonchalant response when the bishops expressed concerns about the widespread suffering in the country.

They told him that the country was bleeding. He disagreed and said the economy is doing fine.

They said they were very worried about the hunger in the land. He said that hunger existed before he was born, displaying a reluctance to take responsibility for the hunger that has increased under his watch.

An uproar ensued as opposition politicians, mainstream journalists, Christians generally, some Muslims, anti-APC social media influencers, professional humanitarians who run charities, etc, and members of the general public accused Mr President of chronic insensitivity

Villa aparatchiks, alarmed by how bad the above remarks made their boss look, flew to his defence and accused Onaiyekan of breaching confidentiality by repeating the contents of a private interaction.

Meanwhile, pro-APC social media influencers insulted Onaiyekan. Some even depicted him wearing demonic horns.

The National Executive Council of the Catholic Laity Council of Nigeria (CLCN) addressed these complaints in a letter thus:

It is the Catholic church’s God-given duty to speak truth to power, defend the vulnerable and hold leadership accountable “with truth and charity”.

The bishops, priests and laity are called to be “salt of the earth and light of the world” (Matthew 5:13-14), even in the corridors of power.

While the church respects the sanctity of private engagements, “matters that touch on the life, welfare and future of over 200 million Nigerians cannot remain forever in closed rooms.” “Cardinal Onaiyekan did not reveal secrets. He shared the moral concerns of the church and response of government, which is in the public interest.”

Onaiyekan spoke out of concern, not malice because he is a man of peace and integrity who believes in dialogue.

Government and church should continue to work together for the common good. We should pray for our leaders and support policies that bring relief to the poor, security to our communities and justice to all.

Now, fair-minded people like me know that Tinubu cannot be blamed for every systemic dysfunction in a country that has been on the wrong path for decades. But, as one of his many detractors has eloquently pointed out (in an anonymous online article), “leadership is judged by results rather than historical context”.

And there is no getting away from the fact that Tinubu is the personification of arrogance, delusion and gaslighting. I’m convinced that there is no humble, intellectually honest or genuinely compassionate bone in that man’s body!!! And his response to the bishops proves his penchant for hubris and callousness.

Meanwhile, there are 38 million Catholics in Nigeria, including me and a whole bunch of very senior APC stalwarts – the Senate President (Godswill Akpabio), the Chairman of the APC Governors Forum (Hope Uzodinma) and others too numerous to mention in this short column.

One of the above, George Akume, the Secretary to Government, has decided to stick his neck out and play peacemaker and placate both his religious and political constituencies.

According to Akume, the Tinubu administration remains fully open to deepening its relationship with and receiving sincere counsel from religious institutions…and regards constructive engagement with the CBCN and other faith-based organizations as essential to navigating Nigeria’s economic and security challenges.

I salute Akume for trying, but it is too late. Tinubu has already soured the milk.

I also, of course, salute Onaiyekan. He has done better than the likes of Adeboye who are always making excuses for Tinubu, probably for reasons linked to ethnic loyalty.

And, by the way, I thank God that Onaiyekan is a Yoruba from Kogi State because he cannot be accused of criticizing Tinubu for anti-Yoruba reasons. Better still, because he is not from the southeast, he cannot be viciously attacked the way the Yoruba wing of the APC constantly attacks Igbos, either subtly or overtly and especially online.

Also, when a man who is notoriously suspicious of other tribes needs to be cautioned, his own brother is more likely than an outsider to persuade him to change direction. And I guess it’s possible that Tinubu will eventually listen to Onaiyekan’s advice.

Finally, let’s hope that the many Catholics who are slavishly follow-following Tinubu have heard our spiritual leaders clearly stating that his government’s performance is morally indefensible. Frankly, they should hide their heads in shame.

World.title: Coastal Highway: We have moved beyond Epe, Umahi replies Duke
World.content:
Minister of Works, Davide Umahi.

By John Alechenu

ABUJA – Minister of Works, Engr. Dave Umahi, has said the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway project has moved beyond Epe in Lagos State and is currently ongoing across five states.

Umahi stated this in response to concerns raised by former Cross River State Governor, Donald Duke, that the project might not progress beyond Epe.

The minister spoke during an inspection of Section 4B of the highway in Ondo State, according to a statement issued on Friday by his Senior Special Assistant on Media, Francis Nwaze.

He said, “The Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway is already on. We have sailed past Lagos that my brother Donald Duke talked about.

“We are on in Ogun — 28 kilometres of dual carriageway. We are on in Ondo — 52 kilometres of dual carriageway. We are also on in Calabar — 27 kilometres. In Akwa Ibom, the first section is about 47 kilometres. Those ones are over 60 per cent done.”

Umahi added that construction had also commenced on the longest stretch of the project, a 180-kilometre dual carriageway section in Akwa Ibom State.

The minister described the coastal highway as one of the flagship infrastructure projects of President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda, saying it would not only connect states but also create employment opportunities and boost economic activities along the corridor.

“Roads mean employment. In this section alone, Hitech has employed over 1,000 people. Direct and indirect jobs are springing up.

“Anywhere we are working, you will see security presence. We also have local vigilantes working with them. It is opening up commerce, agriculture and education,” he said.

Umahi urged residents of the Niger Delta region to support the project, insisting that those criticising the highway were not acting in the interest of the people.

“It is up to Niger Delta people to speak up for this project. They should defend it. They should defend the President. They must vote for the President to complete it,” he said.

On allegations that the highway alignment was altered to favour private estates, the minister explained that the original coastal route was abandoned due to technical challenges, including deep soil deposits of up to 50 metres and the need to construct three bridges of about 3.5 kilometres each across ocean channels.

“That option was not feasible. It would have been too expensive,” he said.

Addressing concerns over funding, Umahi described the project as one of the most transparent infrastructure initiatives undertaken by the Federal Government.

He said Deutsche Bank, which is financing Section 1 of the highway, had described the design and construction as being “in perfection” and had oversubscribed the loan facility by $100 million.

The minister commended Hitech Construction Company for the quality of work and its engagement with host communities, expressing confidence that the project would be completed as promised by President Tinubu.

“Under President Tinubu, this country will be rebuilt. The roads he is building now will last for the next 100 years without reconstruction,” Umahi said.

He urged Nigerians to continue to offer constructive criticism, stressing that the administration remained open to feedback aimed at improving governance.

World.title: Four injured as tanker fire hits Abuja filling station
World.content:
By Omeiza Ajayi

ABUJA – Four persons sustained injuries on Thursday night after a petroleum tanker caught fire while discharging products at AYM Shafa Filling Station, beside the Federal Capital Territory Internal Revenue Service (FCT-IRS) office along Funmilayo Ransome-Kuti Way, Area 3, Garki, Abuja.

The Federal Fire Service (FFS) confirmed that the incident involved a tanker carrying about 60,000 litres of Premium Motor Spirit (PMS).

In a statement issued on Friday, the National Public Relations Officer and Head of Corporate Services, FFS Headquarters, DCF Paul Abraham, said the fire had been successfully extinguished following a coordinated emergency response operation.

He said the inferno affected part of the adjoining three-storey FCT-IRS building before firefighters contained it using multiple firefighting appliances, medium water jets and foam compound.

The Controller-General of the Federal Fire Service, Olumode Samuel Adeyemi, who acted as Incident Commander, personally coordinated the operation and remained at the scene until the early hours of Friday to ensure the fire was completely brought under control.

According to the statement, the four injured adult males were evacuated by a National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) ambulance to a nearby hospital, where they received treatment and were later discharged.

The FFS said a thorough inspection of the scene confirmed that there was no further fire outbreak or casualty, adding that all responding personnel and equipment had returned safely to their stations.

The Service commended residents, motorists and members of the public for their patience, cooperation and compliance with safety directives during the emergency response.

It also acknowledged the support of sister agencies, including the FCT Fire Service, NEMA, the Nigeria Police Force and other emergency responders, for their roles in managing the incident.

The FFS added that investigation had commenced to determine the immediate and remote causes of the fire, with a view to preventing future occurrences.

“The Federal Fire Service remains committed to safeguarding lives, property and critical national assets through prompt, professional and coordinated emergency response,” the statement added.

World.title: I want to be remembered for bringing Nasarawa out of the woods — Gov Sule
World.content:
Nasarawa State Governor, Abdullahi Sule, says he wants to be remembered for transforming the state and bringing it out of what he described as “the woods” before the end of his tenure in May 2027.

Sule stated this on Friday during an interview on Arise Television’s Day Break, while reflecting on his administration’s achievements and what he hopes to leave behind.

The governor described Nasarawa as a “diamond in the rough” when he assumed office, saying his administration had worked to unlock the state’s potential and improve its visibility.

“I want to be remembered for bringing the state out of the woods. It is a diamond in the rough; we have now washed the diamond, and the people can see the diamond clearly,” he said.

According to Sule, his administration had also succeeded in fostering greater unity across the state while reducing the influence of opposition political parties.

“The state is now more seen. The state is now more united. We have reduced the opposition to minimal. Therefore, we have unified the state,” he said.

The governor explained that most of the political disagreements in the state now occurred within the ruling party, rather than between the ruling All Progressives Congress and opposition parties in the state.

“Our opposition now is really within our own party. If we have opposition, it’s maybe some people who feel shortchanged or don’t feel happy that they lost elections; that they are fighting, but no opposition from outside,” Sule said.

He also listed industrialisation and the state’s economic prospects among the achievements he hopes will define his administration.

“So the state is more united, it’s more industrialized, it has more prospect. The prospects are seen. Those are the things that I want to remember for,” the governor added.

World.title: Orutugu is a gift to Nigeria, Soludo hails retiring Anambra police chief
World.content:
By Nwabueze Okonkwo

ONITSHA — Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has described the retiring Commissioner of Police, AIG Ikioye Orutugu, as a gift to Nigeria, while commending his contributions to improving security in the state.

Soludo made the remarks during a special session of the State Executive Council held in honour of the outgoing police chief at the Light House, Awka, on Wednesday.

The governor described the event as a historic milestone, noting that it was the first time an officer would retire from active service in Anambra with a formal state government ceremony.

“This is the first time an officer is retiring in active service from Anambra State. To say goodbye formally, with the full government paraphernalia in full session, is quite emotional and almost impossible to believe that Orutugu is leaving us,” Soludo said.

The governor said the 60-year-old officer, an indigene of Brass Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, was retiring after a distinguished career and only due to the mandatory retirement age.

“He is retired but not tired. You all gave Nigeria the gift of Ikioye. We want to congratulate you on your elevation; you more than deserved it,” Soludo said.

He praised Orutugu for his teamwork and collaboration with other security agencies, saying the collective efforts of the security architecture contributed to the achievements recorded in the state.

The Secretary to the State Government, Mrs. Chiamaka Nnake, described the occasion as an important opportunity to recognise the contributions of the outgoing police chief, wishing him success in retirement.

The Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, Tochukwu Nweke, recalled that Orutugu assumed office at a time the state faced serious security challenges, adding that collaboration among stakeholders helped improve the security situation.

“When he assumed office, the state was wrapped in insecurity, but through collaborative efforts, Anambra is now one of the safest states in the country. He fought with us and we won the battle,” Nweke said.

The State Director of the Department of State Services (DSS), Mr. Chuks Anukposi, described Orutugu as a committed security partner, praising his passion, organisational ability and contribution to joint security operations.

Also speaking on behalf of traditional rulers in the state, the traditional ruler of Uke, Igwe Charles Agbala, thanked God for the retired officer’s successful service, noting that he supported the state’s security policies during his tenure.

Responding, AIG Orutugu expressed appreciation to God, Governor Soludo, the state government, security agencies, community leaders, journalists and residents of Anambra for their support throughout his service.

“Anambra is truly the Light of the Nation, and I am honoured to have served in this state,” he said.

The retired police chief recalled that the command faced significant security challenges when he assumed office, but added that joint efforts with stakeholders led to improved public safety and greater confidence in the police.

He urged the state government to sustain and improve the existing security support, while charging police officers to maintain professionalism and uphold high standards.

During his pulling-out parade at the Anambra State Police Command headquarters, Orutugu specifically appreciated journalists for their support, describing the media as important partners in the fight against crime.

He said the cooperation and professionalism of journalists helped communicate the activities and achievements of the command to the public.

Orutugu disclosed that he was recently honoured with the Crime Fighter and Most Professional Police Officer of the Year 2026 Award by the National Association of Women, as well as another award from the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ), Abuja Council.

He said the recognitions showed that the efforts of the command were being noticed, adding that the media played a significant role in projecting its activities.

Reflecting on his career, the outgoing police chief advised officers to remain professional and avoid undue influence, stressing that integrity remained the greatest asset of any police officer.

“The only thing you owe yourself as a police officer is professionalism. You do not owe any influential person anything. Just be professional,” he said.

Orutugu said he joined the Nigeria Police Force out of passion for service rather than financial gain, adding that a good reputation remained more valuable than material wealth.

He thanked the people and government of Anambra State, security stakeholders and members of the police command for their support, while wishing the state continued peace and security.

World.title: 27 coffins symbolise Nigeria’s failure to end mass killings — Ejiofor
World.content:
Ejiofor

By Nwabueze Okonkwo

ONITSHA — Social critic and legal practitioner, Sir Ifeanyi Ejiofor, Esq., has described the image of 27 coffins from a recent mass burial as a painful reminder of Nigeria’s worsening security challenges and the need for urgent action to protect citizens.

Ejiofor, in a statement titled “The Escalating Tide of Genocidal Atrocities: Mass Burial of 27 Victims of Jihadist Terror as Nigeria’s Conscience Stands Trial,” said the image was more than a photograph, describing it as a reflection of the human cost of recurring violence across the country.

He said the loss of innocent lives should provoke national reflection and collective action rather than temporary emotional reactions.

According to him, repeated attacks and mass killings risk becoming normalised when society fails to sustain attention and demand accountability.

“History teaches that every genocide begins with the normalization of repeated atrocities and the collective silence that follows them. Nigeria must resist travelling that perilous path,” he said.

Ejiofor said the continued loss of lives, whether described as terrorism, insurgency or criminality, points to a serious security crisis requiring sustained national attention.

He expressed concern that security challenges were increasingly being overshadowed by political activities and preparations ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The social critic also condemned reactions trailing the recent visit of Catholic bishops to the Presidency, saying religious leaders should be allowed to express concerns about national issues without being subjected to criticism or intimidation.

He argued that religious institutions have historically played a role in providing moral guidance and speaking on issues affecting society.

“A government genuinely committed to solving national problems should welcome sincere criticism, particularly from respected institutions whose only interest is the preservation of human dignity and national stability,” he said.

Ejiofor called on the Federal Government to make national security its foremost priority, urging the deployment of available resources, intelligence capabilities and constitutional mechanisms to address violent attacks.

He said Nigerians deserved more than condolences after tragedies, stressing the need for effective measures to prevent further loss of lives.

Recalling the recent mass burial conducted by the Catholic Diocese of Kafanchan, Ejiofor said the ceremony represented the human consequences of attacks on communities.

He said reports indicated that the attack occurred at about 11pm on a Sunday night when armed assailants invaded Naridan, a farming community on the border between Kaduna State and Ganawuri in Riyom Local Government Area of Plateau State.

He added that several people were reportedly killed, homes destroyed and residents displaced during the attack.

Ejiofor said the victims were ordinary Nigerians whose lives and aspirations were cut short by violence, urging authorities and citizens to work together towards restoring security and protecting communities.

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs predicted XI vs Golden Arrows including Langelihle Phili
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs have finally completed the signing of Langelihle Phili from Stellenbosch FC after weeks of speculation.

The highly rated 21-year-old joins Amakhosi with plenty of expectations and could make his debut in Sunday’s MTN8 clash against Golden Arrows.

Chiefs have already opened their 2026/27 campaign with a hard-fought 1-0 victory over newcomers Kruger United. Their attention now turns to the MTN8, where coach Fernando Da Cruz faces an early selection dilemma following Phili’s arrival.



Phili is naturally a left winger, meaning either Asanele Velebayi or Pule Mmodi could make way if the new signing is thrown straight into the starting XI.

Luke Baartman, who featured in the season opener, could switch to the right wing, while Flavio Da Silva is expected to lead the attack.

Phili likely to feature for Chiefs this weekend

In defence, Bradley Cross is tipped to return at left-back after missing the opening fixture.

However, Da Cruz may opt for a more cautious approach by introducing Phili from the bench. In that scenario, either Velebayi or Wandile Duba could retain their place in the starting lineup, allowing the former Stellenbosch star to make an impact as a substitute.

Regardless of whether he starts or comes off the bench, all eyes will be on Phili as Chiefs look to book their place in the MTN8 semi-finals. His pace, direct running and creativity could pose a serious threat to the Golden Arrows defence.

Predicted Kaizer Chiefs starting XI: Brandon Petersen; Thabo Monyane, Thabo Moloisane, Miguel Inácio, Bradley Cross; Lebohang Maboe, Adolf Mtasingwa Bitegeko; Mfundo Vilakazi; Luke Baartman, Langelihle Phili, Flávio Silva.

World.title: Durban opens first phase of R29 million market upgrade
World.content:
Durban's R29 million market upgrade aims to create safer spaces for informal traders in the city. Image: canva

The eThekwini Municipality has officially launched the first phase of the R29 million Mansel Road Market Development, while handing over trading permits to 53 newly selected Church Walk traders.

The project marks another step in Durban’s efforts to strengthen the informal economy by providing safer, more modern trading facilities and creating opportunities for small businesses to grow.

Boost for Durban’s informal economy

According to the municipality, the Mansel Road Market Development forms part of a broader programme to modernise informal trading infrastructure and build a more inclusive local economy.



Chairperson of the Economic Development and Planning Committee, Thembo Ntuli, said informal traders play a vital role in supporting households and driving economic activity across eThekwini.

He described traders as business owners, job creators and breadwinners, adding that investing in improved trading spaces helps entrepreneurs expand their businesses while improving their quality of life.

What’s been upgraded?

The first phase of the development includes several improvements designed to create a safer and more business-friendly environment for traders.



These include:

Upgraded trading infrastructure

Improved ablution facilities

Dedicated maintenance and cleaning services

The municipality said the upgrades are intended to improve the overall trading experience while creating a cleaner and more secure marketplace.

As part of the launch, 53 newly selected Church Walk traders have received official trading permits.



The permits allow traders to operate legally while providing greater security and support for the long-term sustainability of their businesses.

The municipality said the project reflects its ongoing commitment to investing in the informal economy, which continues to provide livelihoods for thousands of residents across Durban.

World.title: SuperSport only just secure broadcast rights for Springboks-All Blacks
World.content:
The Springboks are preparing for battle against the All Blacks. Image: SA Rugby website

The so-called Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry tour will kick off on Friday night when the Stormers host the All Blacks, while later this month the Springboks and New Zealand will go into battle in the first of four Tests in the series.

Although it was always presumed and expected that SuperSport would broadcast the matches, it was quite strange to see that CANAL+ – the French media giant that has officially taken full ownership of South Africa’s MultiChoice Group – only confirmed a broadcast rights agreement on Friday.

The agreement will see SuperSport, Africa’s leading sports broadcaster, showcase all four Test matches between the Springboks and All Blacks, as well as the four matches against the United Rugby Championship teams.



SABC will not be able to broadcast any of the games.

SuperSport secures Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry TV rights for Springboks and All Blacks

A statement has highlighted that “SuperSport’s coverage will go further than ever before, capturing all the behind-the-scenes action from both camps during this intriguing tour, with expert analysts and former players breaking down all the key moments and talking points”.

“The South African, New Zealand and global rugby audience is thirsting for this Tour, and we’re delighted to confirm that SuperSport will continue to bring rugby’s biggest matches into homes in Africa,” said Rian Oberholzer, SARU CEO.

“This is a landmark event in the rugby calendar and having a landmark broadcaster in SuperSport to once again bring the passion and drama of the Tour to screens on the continent will be music to the ears of local fans.”

Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry fixtures

World.title: LIVE | Stormers vs All Blacks
World.content:
The long-awaited "Rugby's Greatest Rivalry" tour gets underway in Cape Town on Friday night when the Stormers host the All Blacks at the Cape Town Stadium. Image: Facebook @Allblacks

The long-awaited “Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry” tour gets underway in Cape Town on Friday night when the Stormers host the All Blacks at the Cape Town Stadium in the opening fixture of New Zealand’s historic tour of South Africa.

Kick-off is at 19:00.

The clash marks the first-ever meeting between the Stormers and the All Blacks in the professional era, kicking off an unprecedented eight-match tour that includes fixtures against South Africa’s four United Rugby Championship franchises before a four-Test Freedom Cup series against the Springboks.



Memorable wins

While the All Blacks toured South Africa in 1996, they did not face the Stormers – then known as Western Province – or any of the country’s current URC franchises.

Western Province did, however, enjoy memorable victories over the All Blacks in 1928 (10-3) and 1976 (12-11).

The Western Cape also shares a unique connection with New Zealand rugby.



Current Springbok assistant coach and former All Black flyhalf Tony Brown represented the Stormers in 2008.

Dave Rennie focused on improvement

All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie said his side’s priority is building momentum after their recent Nations Championship campaign.

“We want to build on what we’ve done in the past three games,” Rennie said.



“We’ve had a bit more time together, and that’s been good.

“There’s some combinations we’re testing against a team that’s been competitive in the URC who will be excited about the potential of an international scalp, so that makes them dangerous.”

The New Zealand coach stressed that the fixture is about preparing his squad for the looming Test series against the Springboks.



“This is only about us getting better; we’ve got a Test match around the corner, and we know we’ll need to be better against them than we were in the three Tests.”

Respect for Stormers’ depth

Despite the absence of several Springboks from the Stormers squad, Rennie dismissed suggestions that his side would face a weakened opponent.

“It’s still a pretty strong Stormers side we feel,” he said.



“There’s no shortage of talent and depth in this country.

“The old days of playing a French Barbarians or a South African XV that want to soften you up ahead of a Test series probably changed.

“We have a massive amount of respect for South African rugby, and we’re well aware of the quality of team we are up against, and we’ll give them that respect.”



Strong support expected

The All Blacks are also expecting plenty of backing from South African supporters, with New Zealand teams traditionally enjoying a loyal following in Cape Town.

“It’s been awesome. It’s my eighth time staying in this hotel,” Rennie said.

“We’ve played the Stormers a lot when I was with the Chiefs, and the support we got was always fantastic.



“I know supporters of all New Zealand sides came through here and very much like the All Blacks.

“The crowd we saw last Friday at the welcome event were very passionate, and it will be great to have those voices and numbers behind us this week to start the tour off.”

Friday night’s encounter will be the first chapter of a month-long tour that revives the traditional format of extended visits between rugby’s two greatest rivals for the first time since the professional era began.

World.title: Sundowns in early talks with FC Copenhagen over Bafana star
World.content:
Mamelodi Sundowns are in early talks with Danish giants FC Copenhagen over the possible transfer of Thapelo Maseko.

Maseko is back at Chloorkop following a successful loan stint with Cypriot outfit AEL Limassol.

And while AEL Limassol wanted to make Maseko’s deal permanent upon the expiry of his loan deal, the two clubs could not agree terms.



Also read|REVEALED: Sundowns rejected over R30 million offer for youngster

SUNDOWNS IN TALKS WITH FC COPENHAGEN OVER THAPELO MASEKO

Now, The South African can exclusively reveal that Sundowns have opened talks with FC Copenhagen.

The negotiations, however, are still in their early stages, and it has taken more than two weeks for the Brazilians to even entertain FC Copenhagen.

Sundowns are open to sell the speedy attacker as he is deemed surplus to requirements, but they don’t want to do business with any of the PSL clubs.

And the fact that it has taken weeks for Sundowns to listen to offers, has left the Bafana Bafana star even more frustrated.

Also read: South Africans Abroad: Mbokazi ruled out for the rest of 2026



MASEKO TO BECOME FOURTH SA STAR TO PLAY FOR FC COPENHAGEN?

Maseko could become only a fourth South African-born player to play for FC Copenhagen should the proposed deal go through.

Legendary striker Sibusiso Zuma was the first to don the jersey in 2001 after he signed for the club from Orlando Pirates.

Another former Bafana Bafana international in Elrio van Heerden then followed in his footsteps in 2002.

The last South African player to join and feature for FC Copenhagen was Maseko’s teammate at AEL Limassol, Luther Singh in 2021.

World.title: Phili’s arrival at Kaizer Chiefs is bad news for THIS player
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs have signed arguably one of the league’s most promising operators in Langelihle Phili. What does that mean for Pule Mmodi, though?

Mmodi faces a struggle for game time

With Phili’s arrival, Chiefs have several wide attacking options. There’s the option of right-footed Asanele Velebayi as an inverted left winger, while Phili’s two-footedness makes him a great option on that flank too. Pule Mmodi, often deployed wide on the left, could be falling further down the pecking order. Meanwhile, 21-year-old Phili, known for his low centre of gravity, trickery and accurate shooting, is excited about the move:

“Everyone at home supports Amakhosi, so I thought it would be a good move for me to join the team I grew up supporting and being here feels like my dream has really come true.”



MTN8 action next for Kaizer Chiefs

Against Kruger United on matchday 1 of the new season, some surprise names made starts. Among those were Ethan Chislett in the number 10 position and Luke Baartman wide in attack. World.title: Food security fears mount as UK farmers battle drought
World.content:
LONDON - Giant dust clouds rose from a green-red combine harvester as it crawled across a parched field, a sign that something was awry with UK farmer John Pawsey's land.

"It suddenly, completely dried out," Pawsey said. For weeks the drought "just seems to have gone on forever" on his farm in the eastern county of Suffolk.

English farmers have been contending with the driest July ever recorded by the Met Office weather agency -- unwelcome news for those like Pawsey who have only seen paltry yields of crops such as oats, wheat and vetch.

Concern over food security has gripped Britain's headlines amid a series of heatwaves this year.

"All of our fears were realised when we got our combines into the field and realised that actually the yield was ... between 25 and 30 percent down," Pawsey said.

His family has tilled the Suffolk soil since a Scottish great-grandfather moved there, one of many farm workers who flocked south following the late 19th century agricultural depression.

Like his ancestors, Pawsey, 62, is navigating a turbulent future.

"I am worried about the coming years," he admitted.

The drought is the most recent weather-related challenge to hit the nation's farmers over the past five years.

World.title: UK observatory nervously watches growing space junk threat
World.content:
LONDON - In the sweeping shadow of a satellite dish, staff at the Chilbolton Observatory in southern England track a growing number of objects in Earth's orbit, providing data that underpins Britain's space monitoring efforts.

As the hulking antenna swivels into action, screens inside the control room light up with the names of objects the radar system detects: stars, satellites and abandoned rocket bodies.

Experts at Chilbolton Observatory, operated by the UK's national space laboratory RAL Space, monitor UK-licenced satellites and fast-multiplying fragments of space debris swirling around them.

The space junk includes defunct man-made objects like rocket bodies, dead satellites and fragments from launches, explosions and collisions that threaten to re-enter Earth's atmosphere or crash into functioning satellites.

According to the European Space Agency, there are more than 46,000 pieces of debris weighing a total of 17,000 tonnes currently in orbit.

"Most of those don't collide with anything, most of the time," Matthew Archer, deputy director for launch and space domain awareness at the UK Space Agency told AFP on a visit to the observatory.

"But any of them can cause significant damage or even destroy potential satellites."

On Wednesday, part of a SpaceX rocket about the size of a bus slammed into the Moon, unleashing a stream of debris. Researchers warn the growing density of space junk could trigger the so-called "Kessler syndrome" cascade of collisions.

- 'Look at everything' -

Chilbolton Observatory feeds data to the National Space Operations Centre (NSpOC) -- led by the UK Space Agency and UK Space Command -- that works around the clock to prevent orbital collisions and track debris re-entering Earth's atmosphere.

"Our role is to look at everything that happens and is in space," said Archer.

Space infrastructure underpins some 20 percent of the UK economy, said Archer. The growing "number of objects is making space far more congested, so the need for this capability is growing all the time."

As he speaks, multiple Starlink devices -- part of the constellation of thousands of internet satellites launched by US tycoon Elon Musk's SpaceX -- float by on the control room screens.

There are currently 14,000 satellites orbiting Earth, with some 1.7 million satellites planned in coming years. SpaceX alone has unveiled plans to begin launching more than one million satellites in 2028.

The UK has pledged to invest £85 million ($114 million) in the NSpOC, which issues around 3,000 monthly collision warnings to satellite operators.

The researchers also monitor to ensure satellite operators are complying with their licences and track foreign "adversaries".

"We see examples of countries that have demonstrated the ability to get close or to fly by certain objects," said Archer. "We do have to track ... threats regularly from a military perspective."

And when space debris re-enters the atmosphere, scientists are on stand-by to issue alerts for objects which may not burn up before landfall.

In January, Britain and European countries closely watched the re-entry of a Chinese rocket, amid fears fragments could land in Britain. The rocket eventually splashed down in the Pacific Ocean.

- Asteroids -

"The whole environment is changing," said Chilbolton Observatory's facility leader Sarah Nash. "It really is a multinational environment and there are so many objects that are not controllable."

"The only way that all of this can continue to operate safely is by keeping track of where everything is," Nash told AFP.

Another branch of their work is planetary defence, which involves identifying threats like comets and asteroids.

Last year, the UK Space Agency became a member of the International Asteroid Warning Network (IAWN), which monitors the movement of asteroids including those that could hit Earth.

"We work in partnership with NASA and others in the US to effectively give a percentage chance that (it) might hit the Earth and when that might happen," said Archer.

While smaller space rocks frequently burn up in Earth's atmosphere, large orbiting rocks like asteroids are rarer.

The UK to support the European Space Agency's 2029 mission to study a 375-metre-wide asteroid called Apophis as it flies by Earth.

"Asteroids are a really interesting challenge in many ways. It's unusual for an asteroid to come out of nowhere," explained Nash.

The giant space rocks are generally monitored by optical sensors, as they are too far away for Chilbolton's radar dish to detect.

"If they're close enough for the (radar) antenna to see them, then we have bigger problems," laughed station manager Graham Marshall.

World.title: All Blacks skipper Taylor cautiously recovering from calf strain
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - Playing time could be restricted for New Zealand stand-in captain Codie Taylor before the first Test against South Africa on August 22, head coach Dave Rennie said in Cape Town on Thursday.

The 35-year-old is recovering from a calf strain sustained during the first half of a 40-21 Nations Championship victory over Ireland in Auckland last month.

"We are definitely not looking at him (playing) against the Sharks," said the head coach on the eve of the tour opener against the Stormers franchise in Cape Town.

New Zealand play two other franchises -- the Sharks in Durban on Tuesday and the Bulls in Pretoria next Saturday -- before the first of four Tests in the 'Greatest Rivalry' series.

"Codie will potentially be okay for the Bulls. We are not going to rush him, though. Perhaps a small amount of game time against the Bulls to lead him into the Test match," added Rennie.

New Zealand brought four hookers to South Africa for an eight-match tour that concludes with the fourth Test on September 12 in American city Baltimore.

Rennie also selected Samisoni Taukei'aho and Asafo Aumua, the understudies to Taylor during the Nations Championship matches, and George Bell.

However, Bell suffered a calf strain during training in Cape Town and had to return home. He was replaced by Bradley Slater.

The 'Greatest Rivalry' is the first extended tour by New Zealand to South Africa since 1996, when the tourists won a series in the republic for the first time.

World.title: LIVE | Justice Minister Kubayi testifies before TRC cases inquiry
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Justice Minister Mmamoloko Kubayi is appearing before the TRC cases inquiry on Friday.

Her testimony is expected to include matters relating to her role in dealing with apartheid-era crimes.

This includes the implementation of recommendations by the Truth and Reconciliation Commission.

Government says her participation signifies its commitment to supporting the Commission's work.

The Khampepe Inquiry is probing allegations of political meddling in the prosecution of TRC cases.

It has so far heard evidence from former justice officials, prosecutors and heads of the NPA.

World.title: School violence escalates as learners, teachers face growing safety fears
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - A series of violent incidents at schools across the country has raised fresh concerns about the safety of learners and teachers.

In the latest incident, learners at Iphutheng Primary School in Alexandra, Johannesburg, were left traumatised after two-armed men allegedly entered the school on Tuesday.

It is understood the suspects entered the school during an alleged robbery. Preliminary reports indicate that several warning shots were fired, causing panic among learners and educators.

Learners and staff fled for safety, while laptops were reportedly stolen during the robbery.

The Gauteng Department of Education has confirmed the incident, while police have launched an investigation.

The incident comes just days after Gauteng Education MEC Lebogang Maile and police conducted search-and-seizure operations at several schools as part of a province-wide school safety campaign.

Police confiscated knives, scissors, vapes, a fork and drugs during the operation.

Meanwhile, in KwaZulu-Natal, a 19-year-old learner was allegedly assaulted and killed on school premises on Tuesday.

Siboniso Landela, a learner at Vusumuzi High School in Isithebe, northern KwaZulu-Natal, was allegedly involved in a physical altercation with four other learners.

He was allegedly struck on the head during the fight and was later found unconscious.

KwaZulu-Natal police spokesperson Colonel Robert Netshiunda said four learners, aged between 15 and 20, had been arrested in connection with the incident.

Comment from the provincial education department will be added once received.

In the Western Cape, a Grade 10 learner died in June after he was involved in a fight with another learner at Bellville High School in Cape Town.

The learner was taken to hospital, where he later died. No arrests have been made in connection with the incident.

Last week, learners from the school were allegedly involved in another fight, this time with pupils from a nearby school. No serious injuries were reported.

A community leader said the fights were often linked to gang activity and cultural differences.

World.title: R1.57m cash withdrawals questioned in Mapisa-Nqakula trial
World.content:
PRETORIA - The High Court in Pretoria has heard that former Defence Minister Nosiviwe Mapisa-Nqakula and her family could not have funded renovations to their Johannesburg home through cash withdrawals from their bank accounts.

NPA chief financial investigator Wynand Wessels told the Pretoria High Court that the family withdrew a combined R1.57-million between 2018 and 2020.

That amount falls short of what was allegedly spent on fixing the property.

Mapisa-Nqakula is accused of soliciting bribes from a logistics contractor.

Wessels also told the court his analysis of businesswoman Nombasa Ntsondwa-Ndlovu’s bank statements showed she withdrew nearly R4.3-million between 2016 and 2020.

The state alleges that a portion of those funds was paid to Mapisa-Nqakula, allegations the former Speaker denies.

Under cross-examination, the defence questioned whether Wessels had any direct evidence that the money reached Mapisa-Nqakula. He responded that his findings relied on sworn statements made by Ntsondwa-Ndlovu.

The defence further indicated it would challenge Wessels’ status as an expert witness.

Earlier, the court heard testimony from former Mapisa-Nqakula spokesperson Joy Peter, who said Ntsondwa-Ndlovu felt abandoned by the Defence Department after her business came under scrutiny.

Peter, who described Ntsondwa-Ndlovu as both a close friend and fellow traditional healer, testified that the businesswoman was angry and believed the then-minister had failed to support her. According to Peter, Ntsondwa-Ndlovu said she would “not go down alone.”

Ntsondwa-Ndlovu has previously testified that her R104-million Defence Department logistics contract was cancelled before she was later awarded what she described as a replacement tender worth R79-million.

Although she has been granted indemnity from prosecution in this case in exchange for truthful testimony, the court also heard that Ntsondwa-Ndlovu is facing separate fraud charges in another court.

The trial resumes on Friday, when the state is expected to call a South African Reserve Bank official to testify about the movement of funds, even beyond South Africa’s borders.

World.title: Durban side rebrands to Sharks Rugby Club
World.content:
DURBAN - It's a new dawn in the Shark tank.

The Durban franchise will now be known as the Sharks Rugby Club.

They have also unveiled a new badge ahead of the new United Rugby Championship campaign.
