World.title: Los recelos sobre la moda ultrarrápida enfrían la salida a Bolsa de Shein
World.content:
La compañía busca una valoración de hasta 43.000 millones, muy lejos de los más de 85.000 millones que alcanzó en 2022, lastrada por la presión regulatoria y el deterioro de sus resultados

La salida a Bolsa de Shein entra en su fase decisiva. Cuatro años después de comenzar a estudiar un debut bursátil en Estados Unidos, y tras sortear una maraña de obstáculos regulatorios que frustraron sus planes en Nueva York y Londres, el gigante chino de la moda ultrarrápida se dispone a cotizar en Hong Kong. La compañía ya cuenta con el visto bueno para salir al mercado y ha comenzado a sondear a los inversores de cara a una operación que podría materializarse este mismo mes de agosto.

Muchas cosas han cambiado durante este proceso. La situación financiera de la empresa ya no es la misma; la presión regulatoria y fiscal se ha estrechado, la competencia ha aumentado y los hábitos de consumo han evolucionado. Todo ello ha terminado reflejándose en las expectativas del mercado. Shein aspira a una valoración de entre 40.000 y 50.000 millones de dólares (entre unos 34.600 y 43.300 millones de euros), aunque algunos inversores rebajan sus ambiciones y hablan de 30.000 millones de dólares (cerca de 26.000 millones de euros). Cifras, en cualquier caso, muy alejadas de los 66.000 millones de dólares de valoración que alcanzó en una ronda de financiación de 2023 y de los 100.000 millones de dólares que sonaban en 2022.

Cuando Shein empezó a preparar su salto al parqué, con la economía mundial saliendo aún de la pandemia, el auge del comercio electrónico impulsaba con fuerza su negocio. El confinamiento disparó las compras por internet y convirtió a la compañía en una de las grandes ganadoras de aquel bum. Una euforia que propició el estrellato de fenómenos como el de Peloton, un fabricante de bicicletas estáticas con planes de suscripción, que no logró superar el regreso de la vida al aire libre. Tampoco parece haberlo hecho Shein. El tráfico online en su plataforma pasó de registrar un crecimiento del 60% interanual en la segunda mitad de 2025, según la firma de análisis digital Similarweb. Los últimos datos, publicados en junio, indican avances de un solo dígito.

La pérdida de dinamismo coincide además con una creciente presión sobre el modelo de moda ultrarrápida. El mayor escrutinio regulatorio, las dudas sobre la sostenibilidad del sector y unos consumidores cada vez más sensibles al impacto ambiental de sus compras han contribuido a enfriar el entusiasmo que despertaba la compañía hace apenas unos años. El cambio de percepción también empieza a reflejarse en la evolución bursátil del sector. Mientras grupos como Inditex han reforzado el atractivo de sus marcas mediante colaboraciones con diseñadores y colecciones limitadas, las empresas más expuestas al segmento de bajo coste afrontan un entorno más complejo.

El propietario de Primark, Associated British Foods, también refleja las dificultades que afronta el segmento de la moda asequible. Afectado tanto por la debilidad de la demanda en su negocio de moda como por el deterioro de su división azucarera, el grupo británico cae un 0,7% en Bolsa en el año. En los últimos cuatro años su subida se limita al 17%, frente al 107% de Inditex. H&M, a su vez, avanza un 6% en ese periodo. La cadena sueca, uno de los principales exponentes mundiales del modelo de fast fashion, también afronta las crecientes dudas de los inversores sobre la capacidad del sector para mantener los niveles de crecimiento y rentabilidad de años anteriores.

Competencia y regulación

Las razones que explican el cambio de percepción sobre Shein son diversas. Sharon Iles, analista sénior de moda de GlobalData, considera que la salida a Bolsa en Hong Kong representa un hito para la compañía, pero no elimina los desafíos estructurales a los que se enfrenta. “La competencia se está intensificando a medida que Temu amplía su presencia internacional, mientras que Lefties, de Inditex, y Primark refuerzan sus propias propuestas centradas en la relación calidad-precio”, señala.

A esta creciente rivalidad se suma un entorno regulatorio cada vez más exigente para las plataformas de comercio electrónico de bajo coste. En paralelo al mayor escrutinio sobre el impacto ambiental de la moda ultrarrápida, los reguladores occidentales han comenzado a cerrar algunas de las ventajas de las que se beneficiaban compañías como Shein o Temu. Hace un año, Estados Unidos eliminó la exención para el envío de paquetes valorados en menos de 800 dólares, una medida que posteriormente ha replicado la Unión Europea. Un movimiento que ha supuesto un golpe en la línea de flotación de estas plataformas al restarles atractivo ante los consumidores.

La combinación de una competencia creciente y unas mayores exigencias regulatorias ayuda a explicar el deterioro de los resultados. El gigante de la moda ultrarrápida revela en su folleto de salida a Bolsa una ralentización tanto de sus beneficios como del crecimiento de sus ingresos, aumentando las dudas sobre su potencial valoración. En el primer trimestre de 2026 registró pérdidas de 99 millones de dólares (85,7 millones de euros), frente a las ganancias de 395 millones (341,87 millones de euros) obtenidas un año antes. Aunque la compañía ha tratado de quitar hierro a las cifras al señalar que las pérdidas responden en buena medida a un ajuste contable, la tendencia apunta a una pérdida de impulso que viene de lejos. En 2025, Shein obtuvo un beneficio neto de 2.060 millones de dólares (1.783 millones de euros), frente a los 3.370 millones (2.197 millones de euros) de un año antes.

Cambio de destino

En un entorno marcado por las tensiones comerciales entre China y Estados Unidos, Hong Kong se ha convertido en una alternativa más atractiva para las compañías chinas que buscan financiación en los mercados. Un entorno regulatorio más favorable ha permitido que su Bolsa vaya camino de su mejor año en captación de fondos desde 2020. A los entre 2.000 y 3.000 millones de dólares que aspira a levantar Shein se suman los hasta 8.000 millones que busca levantar Zhongji Innolight, un fabricante de componentes ópticos para centros de datos en su OPV. Unas cifras que le convertirán en la mayor salida a Bolsa en Hong Kong desde el Alibaba en 2019.

Para Shein, el auge del mercado hongkonés llega en un momento oportuno. Tras años de retrasos y obstáculos regulatorios en Occidente, la compañía afronta su debut bursátil en una plaza que vuelve a atraer a grandes emisores. La prueba definitiva, sin embargo, será comprobar si los inversores siguen dispuestos a apostar por un modelo de negocio que ya no genera el mismo entusiasmo que durante los años dorados del comercio electrónico.

World.title: Juan Antonio González Hernández, ‘Toño’, el cronista de los astros de La Palma nos da sus mejores pistas en la isla
World.content:
Guía Starlight y del Observatorio del Roque de Los Muchachos, su pasión por los cielos nocturnos nació hace tres décadas y la ha convertido en su profesión. Una vida dedicada a la divulgación astronómica en la isla canaria, de la que recomienda los mejores miradores

En la isla de La Palma, Juan Antonio González Hernández (La Palma, 1972) es conocido como Toño. Es uno de esos tipos que ha hecho de su afición su profesión. Además de astrónomo aficionado, es divulgador, guía Starlight —parte del primer grupo de profesionales de la isla homologados como tal por el Instituto de Astrofísica de Canarias— y del Observatorio del Roque de Los Muchachos (ORM). También es promotor de productos tematizados en astroturismo, astrofotógrafo, consultor, responsable de varios proyectos del Cabildo Insular de La Palma y exgerente de la empresa Cielos-LaPalma.

Una concatenación de hechos a mediados de los ochenta le hizo mirar al cielo y hasta hoy. Primero fue la inauguración, en 1985, del ORM (en el mundo solo hay otros dos observatorios de este tipo: uno en Chile y otro en Hawái) y, un año después, la noche del 12 de abril de 1986, el paso del cometa Halley. Ese fenómeno astronómico lo dibujó a lápiz, con paciencia y con ayuda de unos prismáticos desde el balcón de su casa, en la barriada de El Pilar, en Santa Cruz de La Palma. Su hambre de galaxias, planetas, estrellas y satélites la fue saciando registrando manchas solares durante los recreos del instituto, leyendo libros de astronomía, viendo Cosmos —serie de televisión escrita y presentada por Carl Sagan— y sumándose a la Agrupación Astronómica Palmera (AAP), que llegó a presidir durante 12 años. De la mano de alguno de los miembros de dicha agrupación tuvo la oportunidad de subir al ORM y disfrutar de las vistas del cielo sobre un mar de nubes a casi 2.400 metros de altitud. Son tantas las estrellas que se pueden contemplar a simple vista desde este punto que no es fácil distinguir las constelaciones.

Cielo estrellado sobre el el Observatorio del Roque de Los Muchachos, en la isla de La Palma. Luis Davilla (GETTY IMAGES)

En 1991, con conocimiento y ya equipado con instrumentos de observación, se decantó por la carrera de Astrofísica, “pero no para viajar y hacer investigación. Yo quería enseñar, soñaba con divulgar astronomía, como Sagan”, cuenta a El Viajero de camino a un punto de observación de La Palma. En la Universidad de La Laguna en Tenerife estudió dos años; una etapa personal complicada hizo que abandonase la carrera y regresase a La Palma. De vuelta a su isla natal estudió una FP de Técnico Administrativo y empezó a trabajar como consignatario de barcos en el puerto. Se casó, tiene dos hijos y nunca se cansó ni de contemplar el cielo ni de registrarlo —ha viajado a Novosibirsk (Siberia), donde vio un eclipse total de sol, y a Coquimbo (Chile), adonde fue para conocer cómo trabajaban allí el astroturismo—. Su familia un poco sí, ahora solo le acompañan a ver grandes acontecimientos, como el eclipse solar total del próximo 12 de agosto. Como en La Palma será parcial, lo verán en la provincia de Zaragoza.

Mientras trabajaba, como miembro de la AAP y emprendedor, intensificó su afición por la divulgación de la astronomía. Hasta que llegó un momento en el que su participación en el desarrollo de proyectos, como la Red de Miradores y Senderos Astronómicos, el Taller del Astrónom@ y muchos otros trabajos divulgativos, le demandaba una jornada laboral completa. Así que dio el paso y empezó a vivir profesionalmente de lo que siempre había sido su pasión —hoy trabaja en el departamento de promoción de astroturismo de la Sociedad de Promoción y Desarrollo Económico de La Palma (SODEPAL)—.

El punto de inflexión de ese cambio profesional fue durante la primera Conferencia Internacional Starlight celebrada en La Palma en 2007, donde se habló de la necesidad de desarrollar empresas vinculadas al astroturismo. Por aquel entonces existían algunas iniciativas aisladas en otras islas del archipiélago. Toño, junto a otros miembros de la Agrupación Astronómica de La Palma, presentó un proyecto llamado La Palma y 14 cielos, con la idea de resaltar la calidad excepcional de las noches en cada uno de los 14 municipios de la isla gracias a la aplicación de la Ley de Protección del Cielo. Una ley que él apunta que permite contemplar las estrellas desde cualquier punto oscuro de la isla, incluso a nivel del mar, desde la playa, y no solo desde la alta montaña, donde está instalado el ORM.

El Observatorio Astrofísico del Roque de Los Muchachos (ORM) se encuentra a 2.396 metros de altitud. Jose A. Bernat Bacete (GETTY IMAGES)

En ese contexto, junto con Carmelo González, fundó en 2009 una empresa especializada en astroturismo de la isla. No solo fue pionera en ese campo, “también empezamos a tematizar casas, senderos y experiencias gastronómicas con el cielo”, dice mientras estaciona su vehículo en el mirador de Llano del Jable, un clásico en sus excursiones nocturnas. Detrás de toda esa labor hay una estrategia de sensibilización. No se trata únicamente de pedir a la gente que apague la luz porque interfiere en la observación astronómica, se trata de explicar que cuidar y proteger el cielo beneficia a toda la isla porque la actividad económica que genera.

Atardecer en el mirador de Llano del Jable, en La Palma. Dominic Dähncke (GETTY IMAGES)

Alrededor de La Palma, en puntos estratégicos de su volcánica orografía, hay miradores en los que hasta hace no mucho tiempo la gente se paraba para contemplar las vistas panorámicas, el amanecer y el atardecer. Ahora también lo hacen por la noche para ver las estrellas. Desde que Toño participara en el desarrollo de estos allá por 2009, y gracias al apoyo del Cabildo Insular, los miradores se han convertido en balcones astronómicos equipados con dos módulos: uno compuesto por un panel grande con planisferios (mapas del cielo según las estaciones) con un contenido específico, en algunos casos, del municipio en el que se encuentra: flora, fauna, artesanía, etcétera. Existe un segundo módulo común a todos, el formado por un palo de sendero que señala hacia la Estrella Polar, con una rueda giratoria que ayuda a distinguir las constelaciones circumpolares, junto a un pequeño panel que explica su uso.

Mirador en el inicio del sendero al volcán de San Antonio, con el poste que señala la Estrella Polar y un panel informativo. Autumn Sky (Alamy/CORDON PRESS)

Hay tres tipos de miradores: de montaña, de medianías y urbanos, como el que hay en una plaza de Los Álamos, en Breña Alta. La idea de estos miradores urbanos, desde los que se puede ver la Estrella Polar, es acercar la astronomía al público general y, sobre todo, a los niños. Que los más pequeños vean cómo se monta un telescopio y cómo funciona es sinónimo de despertar su curiosidad y el interés por la astronomía. Si le preguntan a Toño por los miradores de su isla, recomienda el mencionado del Jable (en la parte alta de El Paso), el de Llano de Las Ventas (Breña Baja), El Infinito (San Andrés), el de Buracas (Garafía), el del Molino (Barlovento) y el de las Toscas (Mazo). Enclaves en los que los aficionados y los profesionales de la astronomía instalan sus equipos para ver todos los astros que pueden.

El mirador de Buracas, en el noroeste de la isla. blickwinkel (Alamy / CORDON PRESS)

Su principal motivación es compartir su pasión por la astronomía. También facilitársela. La accesibilidad para personas ciegas y un planetario son los proyectos en los que anda enfrascado. La Palma dispone de un planetario itinerante e hinchable, pero él quiere uno fijo y con instalaciones y accesos para personas con movilidad reducida. “Desde el Cabildo y SODEPAL estamos trabajando para que la astronomía sea cada vez más inclusiva”, dice orgulloso. Un buen altavoz para contar lo que hacen es Astrofest, donde hay programadas actividades divulgativas para el público general y otras para emprendimientos astronómicos.

El color azul en la red de miradores astronómicos de La Palma identifica los puntos o paneles vinculados a la interpretación del cielo y orientación estelar. Christina Bodendorfer (GETTY IMAGES)

La asignatura pendiente de Toño es ver auroras boreales. En Groenlandia o en el norte de Noruega dice que le gustaría verlas. Él, que ya ha disfrutado de cielos del hemisferio sur, eclipses totales, anulares y parciales, eclipses de Luna y lluvias de estrellas espectaculares, anima a ir a La Palma, isla desde la que quien quiera puede ver una galaxia con sus propios ojos.

World.title: No more “shame lips”: Dutch dictionary adds new word for labia
World.content:
Women’s rights groups are applauding the latest addition to the definitive Dutch dictionary Dikke Van Dale of the word labia: vulvalippen, added alongside the word schaamlippen.

While both words mean labia, the old schaamlippen translates as “shame lips”, which the organisations say is stigmatising as compared to the more neutral “vulva lips”.

“We should just mention these parts in our education with children and young people,” artist Esther van der Valk told broadcaster NOS. “People now know that this is a normal word, and with that we can break the taboo.”

Van der Valk is a member of Dolle Mina, the women’s rights group that was founded in the Netherlands in 1969 and has been advocating for the inclusion of vulvalippen in the Dutch dictionary to counter stigmatisation. They’re joined by Schaamteloos, a more recent campaign seeking to change language and attitudes regarding female anatomy.

Body positive

While schaamlippen will remain in the dictionary, the addition of vulvalippen means the word gets official Dutch language status – proof, say the activists, that the normalisation of sexuality via language can be achieved if enough people want it.

Schaamlippen is not the only word where shame is embedded in its name. There’s schaamhaar – “shame hair” – which is the name for pubic hair, schaambeen (shame bone) for pubic bone and even schaamstreek (shame area) for pubic area.

But Schaamteloos says it had to start somewhere, so it picked schaamlippen. “Everyone has pubic hair, a pubic bone, and a pubic area,” says the group, but “only half of us have labia – or ‘shame lips’ … which adds to a disproportionately large amount of trouble due to the taboo on talking about this.”

While some doctors and even the media have taken to using vulvalippen, it’s not yet part of the everyday Dutch vernacular.

That may change when the new anatomically correct word is included in the Dikke van Dale. That’s expected to happen during its next online update, likely this Autumn.

World.title: Four arrested for death threat against Breda mayor
World.content:
Police have arrested four men suspected of threatening to kill Breda mayor Paul Depla, after a photograph found on a football supporter’s phone revealed new evidence for a case that had stalled.

A banner bearing the words “Depla Dood” (Depla dead) was hung on the front of a café in the city’s Meidoornstraat on March 8, when NAC Breda played Feyenoord. Depla reported the threat to the police, but in May prosecutors said the case had halted because the suspects could not be linked to the banner.

A breakthrough came when several NAC supporters were arrested over rioting around the club’s match against Heerenveen on May 10 and their phones were seized, police said. On one of them, officers found a photograph of the banner in which four men could be identified.

The four – three from Breda, aged 16, 32 and 34, and a 24-year-old from Oosterhout – were arrested on Thursday and will be questioned. Threatening a public official carries a maximum prison sentence of four years.

It is unclear what prompted the threat, but broadcaster NOS reported it may have followed a warning from the city council to a different café, which had planned to host a pre-match party for the club’s hardcore supporters.

When the owners called the party off, the group gathered at the Meidoornstraat café instead, where the banner was hung.

Threats and intimidation against Dutch public officials are a growing concern. Some 45% of local and regional political office holders, including mayors, told a 2024 home affairs ministry survey they had faced aggression in the preceding year.

World.title: Warm, dry weekend ahead as drought shows no sign of ending
World.content:
The Netherlands is set for another warm and largely cloudless weekend, with barely a drop of rain likely for the coming week, according to forecasters.

Friday will be calm and dry with temperatures of 21 to 25°, with morning cloud in the north east giving way to sunshine. Saturday will be sunny and slightly warmer, at 25 to 28°, before temperatures climb to around 30° inland on Sunday.

A brief cooler spell will push maximums down to around 25° on Tuesday, but forecasters expect the warmth to return later in the week – without any significant rain.

The dry spell means no let-up for the ongoing drought, which has pushed the Rhine to record low levels and prompted water use restrictions in several regions.

World.title: Childcare benefits falling short for most parents: CBS
World.content:
Almost two-thirds of parents who claim childcare benefits pay more than the government’s maximum hourly rate, leaving them with hundreds of euros in costs the benefit does not cover, according to national statistics agency CBS.

Parents claiming the benefit spent an average of €10,510 on childcare in 2025, of which 68% was covered, up from 65% in 2024. The benefit was raised in both years as a step towards the government plan for near-free childcare.

But childcare providers are free to set their own fees, and the benefit only applies to costs up to a ceiling fixed by the government each year. In 2025, 63% of parents paid more than the maximum rate for at least one child.

On average, parents paid €3,340 towards childcare themselves last year – €2,860 in regular contributions, plus an extra €480 to cover fees above the official maximum.

The share of parents paying over the ceiling varies widely. In Nunspeet, Bloemendaal, Houten and Midden-Delfland, almost 90% pay more than the maximum rate, compared with just 8% on the island of Ameland. The proportion is highest in the provinces of Utrecht and Noord-Holland and lowest in Friesland and Groningen.

Households in the lowest income group paid an average of €1,190 towards childcare, or 11% of the total cost, while the highest earners paid €5,950, just over half the bill.

In total, 719,000 parents claimed the benefit last year for nearly 1.1 million children. More children attended nurseries and after-school clubs, while the number looked after by registered childminders (gastouders) fell by 10,000 to around 95,000.

The cabinet plans to make childcare almost free for working parents from 2029, covering 96% of costs regardless of income – a scheme that has been repeatedly delayed.

World.title: Kodai Sano joins PSV in biggest Eredivisie move of the summer
World.content:
PSV Eindhoven are in a race against the clock to complete the signing of NEC Nijmegen midfielder Kodai Sano before the first match of the Dutch league season after the clubs agreed a fee of €14.5 million.

The deal, a record sale for the Nijmegen club, left a bitter aftertaste after Sano pulled out of the squad for the midweek Champions League match against Olympiakos despite travelling to Greece.

Director of football Carlos Aalbers said the 22-year-old, who was instrumental in the club’s third-place finish last year, was sent home from the team hotel because “agreements were breached”.

“Sano didn’t want to play and we didn’t want a player in the team who didn’t want to play,” he said.

The champions could be set to offload striker Couhaib Driouech to Rangers before the end of the transfer window. Dutch media report that the two clubs have agreed a price of around €8 million for the 24-year-old Morocco international, but no formal bid has been tabled.

PSV are also believed to be close to completing the signing of Serbian international Filip Kostic, who spent two seasons at Groningen earlier in his career. The arrival of the 33-year-old has fuelled speculation that Croatian veteran Ivan Perisic is on his way out of Eindhoven, most likely to join Inter Milan.

Reserve goalkeeper Joël Drommel is leaving PSV after five years, returning to Twente, the club where he made his professional debut in 2015. “It feels like coming home,” said Drommel, who spent last season on loan at Sparta.

Tadic returns

Another Serbian veteran, former Ajax striker Dusan Tadic, is back in the Netherlands after joining NEC on a three-year contract. “The Netherlands is my second home,” said the 37-year-old, who has also played for Groningen and Twente.

Feyenoord look set to hang on to 20-year-old defender Givairo Read after turning down bids from AS Roma and Nottingham Forest.

Neither club was prepared to match the asking price of €25 million plus €4 million in bonuses for Read, whose current contract runs to 2029.

The Rotterdammers and PSV both want to sign former Feyenoord defender Lutsharel Geertruida from RB Leipzig, but neither club is willing to match the Bundesliga club’s €20 million asking price. Leipzig also say they are not interested in a loan deal.

Ajax loan signings

The biggest name to join Ajax so far under new head coach Míchel is goalkeeper Marc-André ter Stegen, who is moving from Barcelona on a season-long loan.

The 34-year-old, who won the Champions League and seven La Liga titles with the Catalan side, spent part of last season on loan at Girona, Míchel’s previous club. “When I first spoke with [Ajax’s director of football] Jordi Cruyff, I immediately felt it was the right option,” he said.

Another experienced German moving to Amsterdam is 30-year-old midfielder Julian Brandt, who arrives on a free transfer from Borussia Dortmund.

The Amsterdammers are believed to be in contact with Napoli about bringing Noa Lang back to the club if, as expected, Belgian striker Mika Godts leaves for Paris Saint-Germain before the end of the month. The clubs are understood to be negotiating a five-year deal, but PSG are haggling over Ajax’s €60 million price tag.

Torrents as cover

Ajax have also signed 19-year-old midfielder Jofre Torrents on loan from Barcelona as possible cover for Owen Wijndal, who is rumoured to be seeking a move out of Amsterdam. If Wijndal stays, Torrents is likely to turn out for the youth team in the Keuken Kampioen Divisie.

Midfielder Kian Fitz-Jim is definitely leaving after Ajax agreed to sell the 23-year-old, who spent part of last season on loan at Excelsior, to Torino.

Calvin Stengs is back at AZ Alkmaar after four years, after being released from his contract at Feyenoord, while Republic of Ireland striker Troy Parrott is said to be considering a move from Alkmaar to English Championship with West Ham United.

Elsewhere in the Eredivisie, Excelsior have signed 20-year-old striker Aymen Sliti on loan from city neighbours Feyenoord.

Swedes at Groningen

Groningen have signed 18-year-old Swedish midfielder Alvin Nordin from Helsingborgs on a four-year deal. Nordin played 28 first-teammatches for the Swedish club after making his debut at 16. Another Swede, defender Malcolm Jeng, is moving to the Euroborg on loan from Stade de Reims.

The northerners have also turned down a bid from AZ for striker Thom van Bergen. “We’ve made it clear Thom is not for sale,” managing director Frank van Mosselveld told RTV Noord.

Newly promoted Willem II have acquired 29-year-old midfielder Hidde ter Avest from English third-tier side Oxford United.

Telstar have strengthened their midfield with the signing of 20-year-old Harrie Kuster from Twente, 20-year-old Isiah Ahmed from Heerenveen and 23-year-old Gabi Caschili, who was released by Cambuur Leeuwarden a year ago after he was involved in a brawl during an amateur match.

World.title: Dutch rights group COC wins Pride Award for 80 years of work
World.content:
Dutch campaign group COC Nederland, the oldest surviving LGBTQI+ rights organisation in the world, has won the International Pride Award at the WorldPride Human Rights Conference in Amsterdam.

The awards, a joint initiative of the United Nations Development Programme and ILGA World, were presented to five “equality champions” at a ceremony in the Beurs van Berlage on Wednesday. Amsterdam is hosting WorldPride, the global LGBTQI+ event, for the first time this year.

The COC, founded in 1946, was recognised in particular for its support for people in countries where homosexuality is banned or even punishable by death, director Marie Ricardo, who accepted the prize, told broadcaster NOS.

“We support them with coaching, we help them think about how to bring about change in their own surroundings, and we support them with money,” she said.

Ricardo called the award “a recognition of the work we have been doing for 80 years, and the 40 years we have been supporting movements internationally”.

Other winners include South African deputy minister Mmapaseka Steve Letsike and Ugandan transgender pastor Aggie Dennett Harmon.

World.title: Dutch state close to breaking even on ABN Amro bailout
World.content:
The Dutch state is close to recouping the full cost of the 2008 nationalisation of ABN Amro, after a share price rally took the bank’s stock above €40 this week, according to calculations by the Financieele Dagblad.

The finance ministry had long assumed the rescue would be a loss-making operation. In late 2023 it told MPs it was “not realistic” that the state would break even in the short term, projecting a shortfall of almost €7 billion.

Since then the shares have tripled in value, from €13.20 at the time to just over €40 on Thursday. The state, which still owns 20.5% of the bank has now recouped €14.2 billion through staged sell-offs, and its remaining stake is worth some €6.7 billion, the FD said.

That brings the total close to the €21.7 billion the ministry says has been pumped into the bank since 2008.

Slow sell-off

The state bought ABN Amro, Fortis Bank Nederland and the insurer now known as ASR in October 2008 for €16.8 billion to stop parent company Fortis collapsing in the credit crisis, and injected roughly €8 billion more into the banks in the years that followed.

ABN Amro returned to the stock market in 2015, but the share price languished for years and the sell-off repeatedly stalled. Former D66 finance minister Sigrid Kaag restarted the sales in 2023, and every tranche since has fetched a higher price.

Interest paid on the money borrowed for the rescue has been roughly cancelled out by dividend income over the years, the FD said.

Cost cutting

Morningstar analyst Johann Scholtz told the FD the share price rise is partly due to the state selling its stakes and the bank therefore having more freedom to cut costs, along with investors speculating about takeovers in the European banking sector.

The windfall will not plug the cabinet’s budget gaps, however, as one-off share sales cannot be counted towards the deficit under EU rules.

World.title: Jetten thanks firefighters on visit to site of Limburg wildfire
World.content:
Prime minister Rob Jetten has visited the site of a wildfire that has been raging in Limburg for four days, destroying around a square kilometre of woodland.

Jetten thanked emergency workers for their efforts to contain the blaze in the Boshuizerbergen, in a social media video showing “the huge damage to nature and to the animals and people who have had to be evacuated”.

An emergency order banning people from the area remains in force, but limited train services resumed between Venray and Boxmeer on Thursday morning. Arriva had to lay on buses for commuters after the line through the fire zone was closed.

Firefighters said on Wednesday they had brought the blaze under control, only for it to flare up again twice during the night.

Chinook helicopters dropped 900,000 litres of water on the fire in the first two days, drawing it from the Maas in giant buckets containing 7,600 litres.

Efforts to contain the fire have been complicated by the fact that the area contains unexploded Second World War munitions, which bomb disposal specialists have had to make safe.

“In the next few days the fire service and [nature management service] Limburgs Landschap will focus on completely putting out the last sources of the fire. After that we can make a plan to restore this area,” Jetten said.

“I want to thank in particular everyone who has worked so hard in the last few days to deal with this crisis.”

Poland’s largest opposition party, the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), has called for Ukrainian men of conscription age who are not legally working to be deported to Ukraine. The policy, which continues a recent hardening of PiS’s position towards Ukraine and Ukrainians as it competes with the far right for support, was condemned by government figures, who called it “absurd” and “disgusting”. 🇵🇱 Bezpieczeństwo obywateli powinno być priorytetem każdego rządu. Potrzebne są zdecydowane działania wobec osób przebywających w Polsce niezgodnie z prawem. 👉 Udostępnij! 🔥 Ku nowemu rządowi! pic.twitter.com/m8MctmmPXd — Prawo i Sprawiedliwość (@pisorgpl) August 6, 2026 On Thursday, PiS, which has recently been hit by falling support in the polls and the defection of a large breakaway group of more moderate MPs, held a policy convention at which it presented ideas it wants to implement if it returns to power after next year’s parliamentary elections. “One of [our] government’s first, most significant decisions will be to deport men, Ukrainians of military age, who are not legally working in Poland,” announced Tobiasz Bocheński, a deputy leader of the party. “They will have the opportunity to fight for their homeland, so that the horrors of this war can quickly end,” he continued. “Because for Central and Eastern Europe to be secure and free, Ukraine must win.” Bocheński denied that the policy was inhumane, noting that, in 2022, when PiS was in government, “Poles, like no other nation in Europe, opened their hearts, their homes and their wallets to women, children, the elderly and disabled people fleeing Putin’s bombs”. Poland was the primary destination for refugees fleeing Ukraine in 2022. Almost one million of them remain in the country, alongside hundreds of thousands of other Ukrainian immigrants, many of whom arrived before 2022. They are by far Poland’s largest foreign national group. In their announcement of the proposed policy, PiS gave no details of how it would work in practice, nor on what legal basis Ukrainians who are legally resident in Poland and have not violated any laws would be deported. News website Interia, which had reported on PiS’s plans shortly before they were officially announced, notes that data from Poland’s labour ministry show that only around 11,000 Ukrainians are registered as unemployed in Poland. The figures are not broken down by gender, but most are believed to be women. However, PiS’s policy would also apply to Ukrainians in the so-called grey economy, where people work informally without registering or paying taxes, reports Interia. Military-age Ukrainian men in other European countries should not receive social benefits, says Poland's foreign minister, @sikorskiradek. "There should be no financial incentives for avoiding the draft" https://t.co/5TcTqyDa6X — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 16, 2024 PiS’s plan was immediately criticised by government figures, with interior ministry spokeswoman Karolina Gałecka calling it “an absurd idea” and “pure demagoguery”. She noted that over 95% of Ukrainian men of conscription age in Poland are working legally and paying taxes. “Without these people, many key sectors of the Polish economy would simply grind to a halt,” wrote Gałecka. “Stop the incitement.” Deputy interior minister Maciej Duszczyk, meanwhile, told broadcaster TVN that, among the Ukrainian men not working, many are wounded soldiers in Poland for treatment and rehabilitation or fathers caring for disabled children. Deportations are a “purely political, disgusting idea”, he added. Interior minister Marcin Kierwiński wrote that, “when [PiS] was in power, they couldn’t even deport those who were breaking the law, and now they’re supposedly going to deport everyone without rhyme or reason”. Since taking power, the current government has increased deportations of foreigners who are in Poland illegally or broke the law while in the country. In every year between 2017 and 2022, Poland was the EU member state that issued the highest number of first residence permits to immigrants from outside the bloc. There are now over two million foreigners registered as living in Poland, making up just 5% of the population. Around three quarters are Ukrainians (1.55 million), with the next largest groups being Belarusians (139,300), Indians (26,100), Georgians (22,200), Russians (19,500), Vietnamese (15,100) and Turks (14,500). Poland’s power grid operator, PSE, has, for the second time in three days and third time this summer, invoked emergency measures to ensure supply amid an ongoing heatwave. Before this summer, it had only done so twice in the eight years since such powers were introduced. However, following a meeting with PSE and other state energy officials, Prime Minister Donald Tusk has assured Poles that, despite “a very difficult period”, the “situation is under control” and power supplies are secure, thanks in part to the growth of renewables in recent years. ❗️PSE ponownie ogłaszają okresy przywołania na rynku mocy❗️ To już 3. raz w tym roku, kiedy operator sięga po to narzędzie. W historii zdarzyło się to tylko 5 razy, wliczywszy 3 przypadki tegoroczne, co pokazuje wyjątkowość roku 2026 dla energetyki. pic.twitter.com/DbCPnpyae4 — Jakub Wiech (@jakubwiech) August 6, 2026 PSE has called on contracted electricity generators to increase output and large consumers to cut use to help balance the grid on Thursday between 5:00 p.m. and 10:00 p.m., as temperatures have this week approached 40°C (104°F) in many parts of the country. The same measures were introduced on Tuesday, as the heatwave pushed up electricity consumption, partly due to increased use of air conditioning and refrigeration. Participants in Poland’s capacity market are paid for maintaining standby capacity and fulfilling their obligations when called upon by the operator. According to PSE, the mechanism is “a remedial measure” used when the generation capacity available to the operator falls significantly below the required safety level. Previously, the measures were invoked in June this year, amid another heatwave that saw Poland hit its highest-ever recorded temperature of 40.5°C. But before that, they had only been used twice since being introduced in 2018. Temperatures in Poland have reached the highest level on record, with a figure of 40.3°C (104.5°F) recorded this afternoon, as the heatwave that has hit Europe this week moves eastwards https://t.co/eRhRxiuCGq — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 28, 2026 Poland’s weather institute IMGW issued heat warnings on Thursday for 13 of the country’s 16 provinces, with daytime temperatures forecast to reach between 33C and 38C. High temperatures and prolonged drought conditions have also pushed water levels in many rivers to extremely low levels, with the Vistula, Poland’s longest river, only 5 centimetres above the historic low of 4 centimetres it fell to in Warsaw last year. Some other parts of the river have hit all-time record lows, reports Polsat News. One result has been a disruption of cooling supplies to Poland’s power sector. State energy firm Enea this week announced reduced operations at two of its coal-fired plants that are cooled by water from the Vistula. Around 1.1 gigawatts (GW) of capacity (just over 1% of Poland’s total) has gone offline. On Wednesday, Prime Minister Donald Tusk convened a meeting of a government crisis team, including PSE’s deputy president, to discuss the current heatwave and its potential impact on the power sector. However, afterwards he assured that “the situation is under control” and that the fact that Poland now has “a lot of energy from solar panels and wind turbines makes our system relatively secure”, reports the Polish Press Agency (PAP). Poland’s renewable sector has expanded rapidly over the last decade. Last year, it provided just over 29% of the country’s power, with onshore wind supplying 14% of the energy mix and solar 12%. Renewables generated 29.4% of Poland's electricity in 2025, almost exactly the same figure as in 2024, ending a period of strong growth since 2021. Coal (52.2%) remained the dominant source, though its share declined. Poland’s top administrative court has upheld a decision by the finance ministry to withhold state subsidies from the national-conservative opposition Law and Justice (PiS) party due to campaign finance irregularities. The decision was welcomed by the government, with Prime Minister Donald Tusk saying that there will be “no money for grifters”. PiS, however, argues that the money is being withheld for political reasons and accuses the authorities of “Russian standards”. Naczelny Sąd Administracyjny oddalił w środę kasacje ws. dotacji i subwencji dla PiS. – Miażdżący dla PiS wyrok podtrzymany! – stwierdził szef MF Andrzej Domański https://t.co/bcL18WbiYf — OKO.press (@oko_press) August 6, 2026 The dispute dates back to August 2024, when the National Electoral Commission (PKW) rejected PiS’s financial report for the previous year’s parliamentary election campaign after identifying around 3.6 million zloty (€838,000) in unauthorised expenditure. As a result, the PKW ordered that PiS should lose 10.8 million zloty from the state subsidies that political parties in Poland receive based on their level of electoral support. The party would normally have received 25.9 million zloty based on its 2023 election result. The decision triggered months of legal wrangling, with PiS arguing that the funding should be restored after the Supreme Court upheld its complaint against the PKW’s decision. However, finance minister Andrzej Domański refused to release the money, saying there were unresolved legal doubts over the ruling. The finance minister has refused to comply with the electoral commission's decision to pay out subsidies to the opposition PiS party He says there are "legal doubts" over the issue. But PiS says he is obliged to pay and will be held criminally responsible https://t.co/ZwIZRqn5tp — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) January 9, 2025 Those doubts stem from a broader dispute over the controversial and contested judicial reforms implemented by PiS when it ruled Poland from 2015 to 2023. The chamber of the Supreme Court that ruled in PiS’s favour was created as part of those reforms. It has previously been found to not be a legitimate body by both the European Court of Justice and European Court of Human Rights because it contains improperly appointed judges. After the Supreme Court chamber’s ruling, the PKW initially said it would not recognise the decision until the chamber’s legal status was clarified. Two weeks later, however, it reversed that decision and approved PiS’s financial report. Domański still declined to restore the subsidy, arguing that the PKW’s resolution was internally contradictory. While it approved the payments, it also stated that the chamber’s ruling should come from a body recognised as a court and that it was not determining whether the chamber met that standard. PiS challenged Domański’s decision. However, its case was initially rejected by a lower court in June last year, and that decision has now been upheld by the Supreme Administrative Court (NSA), which is the final court of appeal for administrative issues. The NSA found the minister had acted lawfully in withholding the funding. It also said the Supreme Court chamber’s ruling had no legal effect because it had been issued by a body that was not a properly constituted court, reports news website OKO.press. The ruling was welcomed by Domański, who called it a “crushing blow to PiS” and said that “yet another PiS lie has been exposed”. Prime Minister Donald Tusk, meanwhile, wrote on social media: “Just as we said, there is and will be no money for grifters.” Tak jak mówiliśmy, dla przekręciarzy pieniędzy nie ma i nie będzie. https://t.co/4Kqexj6NoC — Donald Tusk (@donaldtusk) August 5, 2026 The PKW’s decision to cut PiS’s funds was made after it found that government resources – including from the justice ministry, Government Legislation Centre (RCL) and Research and Academic Computer Network (NASK) – had been used to support the party’s election campaign. However, PiS has always argued that the decision was a political one, implemented at the behest of the new Tusk government in order to undermine the main opposition party. Radosław Fogiel, a senior PiS lawmaker and former party spokesman, said that the new NSA ruling “does not change the essence of the matter: it unlawfully deprives the main opposition party of the subsidy to which it is entitled. After a ten-year-long investigation, prosecutors have concluded that Poland’s government in 2010 – which was led by current Prime Minister Donald Tusk – was not guilty of “diplomatic treason” in its response to the plane crash in Russia that killed President Lech Kaczyński. The national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) party – which ruled Poland from 2015 to 2023 and is led by Lech’s twin brother, Jarosław – has always rejected the findings of official Polish and Russian investigations into the crash, which found it to have been an accident. Instead, PiS claims that the disaster, which claimed the lives of 96 people, many of them senior Polish state officials, was caused deliberately by Russia and then covered up with the help of Tusk’s government. However, while PiS launched various investigations during its time in power, it has never substantiated its claims. And prosecutors now say that there is no evidence that diplomatic treason, a crime that carries a potential prison sentence of up to ten years, took place. Teraz potwierdzenie @PK_GOV_PL: nie było żadnej zdrady dyplomatycznej ani żadnej intencji jej popełnienia. Oczywiście żaden z kłamców… https://t.co/VKZHlF5xkX — Radosław Sikorski 🇵🇱🇪🇺 (@sikorskiradek) August 5, 2026 Wednesday’s announcement by the National Prosecutor’s Office was welcomed by Radosław Sikorski, the current foreign minister, who held the same role in 2010. He condemned the “Smolensk liars”, such as Jarosław Kaczyński, who he suggested had exploited the tragedy for their own benefit. “They brainwashed millions of people, divided families, stirred up hatred within the nation,” he wrote. “They’ll burn in hell for it. But the power, money and satisfaction they gained from spitting on their rivals – that’s theirs.” The idea that Smolensk was an assassination of Lech Kaczyński has been a core part of PiS rhetoric. In 2022, for example, Jarosław Kaczyński said that the decision was made “at the highest level of the Kremlin” and Tusk’s government then “covered up” the incident as part of a “macabre reconciliation with Russia”. Smolensk was an “attack decided at the highest level of the Kremlin”, says Jarosław Kaczyński ahead of the 12th anniversary of the crash. Donald Tusk's government then “covered up” the incident as part of a “macabre reconciliation with Russia”, he adds https://t.co/5ae0gHJj3B — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) April 4, 2022 The investigation into diplomatic treason – a crime consisting of acting to the detriment of Poland while authorised to represent the country in relations with foreign states or organisations – was launched in August 2016, less than a year after PiS had come to power. Among the individuals who had formally notified prosecutors of a potential crime was PiS deputy leader Antoni Macierewicz, who from 2015 to 2018 served as defence minister. He has been the foremost proponent of conspiracy theories around the Smolensk air disaster. In their notifications to prosecutors, Macierewicz and the others accused Tusk and other officials of, in their relations with Russia, deliberately choosing a legal basis for an investigation into the crash that was unfavourable to Poland by giving it no real influence over how it was run. However, prosecutors now say that, after ten years in which they questioned 488 witnesses, gathered extensive documentation and requested legal assistance from several countries, they have “concluded that no crime of diplomatic treason was committed”. In a statement explaining the decision, the National Prosecutor’s Office said that the legal basis chosen for cooperating with Russia on an investigation – Annex 13 of the Convention on International Civil Aviation – was, in fact, “the most advantageous solution” for Poland. It ensured the participation of Polish representatives in the Russian-led investigation, including access to the wreckage and crash site. Other legal options would have offered no greater benefits and involved significant risks, concluded the Polish prosecutors. They acknowledged that Russia “subsequently failed to fulfil some of its obligations arising from the adopted procedure”, but said this should have no bearing on assessing the decisions that were previously made on setting up the investigation. The defence ministry will notify prosecutors of 41 suspected crimes linked to a commission established by the former PiS government to investigate the 2010 plane crash in Russia that killed President Lech Kaczyński https://t.co/aEAlmk9lDM — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 24, 2024 The prosecutors also found that, not only did Polish officials choose the best legal solution, but there was also “no evidence indicating that individuals authorised to act on behalf of Poland, including the prime minister and members of the Council of Ministers, acted with the intent to harm Poland”. Given that the crime of diplomatic treason requires intent, this finding further reinforced the decision to drop the investigation. However, the prosecutors note that their decision can still be appealed. At the time of writing, neither Kaczyński, Macierewicz, nor other senior PiS figures had commented on the prosecutors’ announcement. However, it is likely they will point to the fact that the current national prosecutor was appointed by Tusk’s government after it had removed the previous PiS-era incumbent in a legally questionable move. The Supreme Court has issued a ruling that effectively found that the government unlawfully replaced a senior prosecutor earlier this year However, the justice minister says the ruling has no legal force as it was issued by illegitimately appointed judges https://t.co/9fCE6d18uy — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 27, 2024 In 2020, in a separate civil case, a court ordered Jarosław Kaczyński to apologise for accusing Sikorski of “diplomatic treason” in relation to the Smolensk crash. Two years later, after Kaczyński had refused to comply with the ruling and Sikorski published the apology himself, Kaczyński was ordered to pay the costs. In 2024, an investigation by Tusk’s government found that the PiS administration had wasted tens of millions of zloty on a commission, headed by Macierewicz, that was tasked with re-investigating the Smolensk disaster. It notified prosecutors of dozens of suspected crimes relating to the functioning of the commission. Macierewicz, however, accused the government of spreading “lies and disinformation” designed to “protect Putin”. Poland has urged the European Union to adopt tougher measures in response to the recent migration crisis in Spain’s African exclave of Ceuta, including making migrants who enter the bloc illegally ineligible for obtaining residence rights. During a special meeting of EU interior ministers on Tuesday, Poland shared its own experience of dealing with “weaponised” migration from Belarus, which prompted the Polish government last year to restrict the right to asylum for people who cross irregularly. 🔵 KOMUNIKAT | Polska przedstawiła swoje stanowisko ws. migracji na nadzwyczajnym posiedzeniu Rady JHA w sprawie ostatnich wydarzeń w Ceucie 🇵🇱🇪🇺 Wiceminister spraw wewnętrznych i administracji @MaciekDuszczyk wziął udział w odbywającym się we wtorek (4 sierpnia br.)… pic.twitter.com/glfyiu5ZW3 — MSWiA 🇵🇱 (@MSWiA_GOV_PL) August 4, 2026 Last week, tens of thousands of migrants entered Ceuta, most of them by swimming there from neighbouring Morocco. Dozens died while trying to cross. Among those who managed to enter Ceuta, Spain says that the vast majority have been returned to Morocco. The incident prompted expressions of concern from many European leaders, including calls to restrict Spain’s participation in the Schengen free movement zone (despite the fact that anyone leaving Ceuta for the European mainland is subject to identity checks). Among those to speak out was Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk, who on Friday called on Spain to “follow our example if Schengen is to survive”. Poland has tightened asylum laws, border procedures, and has built effective barriers on its border with Belarus, which is the eastern border of the EU. We have invested billions of euros and engaged thousands of soldiers, police officers and border guards. Spain must follow our… — Donald Tusk (@donaldtusk) July 31, 2026 That was a reference to Poland’s response to a crisis on its eastern border, where since 2021 Belarus has encouraged and assisted tens of thousands of migrants – mainly from Asia and Africa – to try to cross irregularly into the EU. Both Poland and the EU have accused Belarus and its ally Russia of deliberately “weaponising” migration in an attempt to destabilise European societies as part of Moscow and Minsk’s broader “hybrid threats” against the EU. Tusk noted that, in response, Poland has restricted the right to asylum, invested billions in strengthening physical and electronic barriers along the border, and has deployed thousands of soldiers, police officers and border guards there (who have also been given expanded rights to use firearms). A court has ruled that Poland's recently introduced partial suspension of the right to asylum is justified and lawful. It rejected a complaint by a Sudanese man who had been denied the right to claim asylum after crossing irregularly from Belarus https://t.co/jx3s1AxRgG — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 10, 2025 On Saturday, Tusk and 21 other EU leaders jointly signed a letter expressing “serious concern” at the situation in Ceuta and warning that the EU “cannot allow uncontrolled mass border crossings, the instrumentalisation of migration, or other hybrid threats to create the impression that illegal entry…is possible”. While they welcomed Spain’s cooperation with Morocco to send most of the migrants back, they also called for an extraordinary meeting of EU interior ministers to “agree on a coordinated European response, including the rapid mobilisation of available EU instruments and the necessary support to Spain”. At that meeting, which took place on Tuesday, Poland’s interior ministry said that it had expressed the view that “illegal entry into the European Union should automatically exclude the possibility of obtaining residence permits, and therefore the possibility of permanent stay in the future”. While Poland’s statement did not mention it directly, earlier this year Spain’s government launched an amnesty that allowed undocumented migrants to apply to legalise their stay in the country. Over one million people had signed up for the scheme by the time it closed at the end of June. In its statement, Poland’s interior ministry warned that “migration must be fully controlled”, as otherwise it can “be used against the values that guide the EU”. It also called for the “official recognition of migration as a challenge directly linked to security”. It added that during Tuesday’s meeting it had “presented its own experiences with border protection in the context of the instrumentalisation and weaponisation of migration and adapting law to migration challenges”, including restrictions on asylum claims. “The example of Ceuta clearly demonstrates that absolute access to asylum is impossible to maintain in the face of such real threats,” wrote the interior ministry, which said that it “welcomed the shared perspective on migration among a growing number of member states”. In a statement of its own, the European Council noted that there had been a “common understanding of the need to continue relentlessly fighting migrant smuggling networks, to reinforce returns, to strengthen EU borders, to build deep partnerships with third countries, and to improve foresight.” It added that member states “were united in expressing strong solidarity with Spain”, appreciated its “swift and effective efforts” to deal with the crisis, and had also expressed their condolences for the people who died while attempting to cross from Morocco to Ceuta. World.title: Unexploded WWII ordnance discovered under busy Warsaw street
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Part of central Warsaw was shut down today after unexploded ordnance from World War Two was found buried under a major road during construction work. The discovery, which came just days after the city commemorated the anniversary of its wartime uprising against Nazi-German occupation, led to traffic being diverted and residents being warned to stay away from their windows and avoid going outside while bomb disposal experts worked to safely remove the item. W Al. Solidarności znaleziono niewybuch, najprawdopodobniej z czasów II wojny światowej. ℹ️ Czytaj więcej: https://t.co/Fv6oe84XiM pic.twitter.com/BfjQPZveYZ — tvp.info 🇵🇱 (@tvp_info) August 4, 2026 The object, reportedly around 70 centimetres long, was found early on Tuesday morning on Solidarity Avenue, a major thoroughfare, during modernisation work on tram lines. “We were digging a trench and I literally just touched it with the tip [of my digger],” the operator of the excavator who found it told broadcaster TVN. Staff working at the site were immediately evacuated to a safe distance. Police later confirmed that the item is unexploded ordnance, and that initial findings indicate it dates from World War Two. Bomb disposal experts arrived at the scene in the afternoon. However, they have not confirmed precisely what type of ordnance was discovered or its origin, reports Polsat News. Warsaw was the site of major fighting during World War Two, beginning in 1939, when Nazi Germany invaded and occupied Poland. In 1943, the Warsaw Ghetto Uprising, the largest single act of Jewish resistance during the war, took place. On 1 August 1944, the Polish underground Home Army launched the Warsaw Uprising, which was the largest single act of armed resistance anywhere in German-occupied Europe during the war. In response, the Germans destroyed much of the city, around 85% of which lay in ruins by 1945. Warsaw’s historic Old Town was meticulously rebuilt after the war. But many other parts of the city were redeveloped by the newly installed communist authorities, including Solidarity Avenue (which during the communist era was named after Polish-Soviet Red Army General Karol Świerczewski). Thousands of vehicles drove over the unexploded ordnance every day for decades. “Warsaw is marked by history, and there are many such surprises,” Witold Urbanowicz, spokesman for the city’s tram operator, told news website Interia. After the fall of the Warsaw Uprising – which began 80 years ago today – the German occupiers expelled the city's entire population. However, some survivors decided to remain among the ruins. They became known as "Robinson Crusoes" and this is their story https://t.co/UuVbfbcpQ4 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 1, 2024 Unexploded ordnance is regularly found in Poland. In May this year, around 200 anti-personnel mines dating from World War Two were discovered at the construction site of a student dormitory at Kraków’s Jagiellonian University. In October last year, two men were hospitalised after an artillery shell that one of them had brought home from a forest exploded in his apartment while the pair were under the influence of alcohol. Earlier that year, wild boars unearthed 21 mortar shells buried in a forest since the war. In 2023, 72 unexploded artillery shells were discovered during renovation work at a primary school and four pieces of World War Two ordnance were found in the walls of a church undergoing renovation. Wild boars dug up 21 mortar shells from World War Two that had been buried in a Polish forest. The unexploded ordnance has now been safely removed without harm to either the animals or humans https://t.co/W9kaPr1BNw — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 17, 2025 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Russia condemns Poland’s “sacrilegious” demolition of Soviet monument
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! We cannot do what we do without your support. Russia has criticised the demolition of a Soviet-era monument in Poland, calling the decision “sacrilegious” and a “flagrant violation” of an agreement between the two countries on respecting places of remembrance. However, Poland’s state Institute of National Remembrance (IPN), which financed the demolition, says that the monument was a “Soviet propaganda object” that was removed under a law requiring the “decommunisation” of public spaces. On Friday, around 150 residents in Pyrzyce, a town of 12,000 in northwestern Poland, gathered to watch the demolition of a monument to the Red Army that had stood there for decades. Initially, a memorial had been established in the town alongside a cemetery for Red Army soldiers in the immediate aftermath of World War Two, when the Soviets had driven the Nazi German occupiers out of Poland but then introduced a new communist government of their own. However, the soldiers’ remains were later moved to a military cemetery elsewhere in the region and the monument itself was redesigned and moved to another location within Pyrzyce. Its final form, created in 1984, was a huge rectangular concrete structure weighing several hundred tons and featuring a relief depicting the head of a Soviet soldier. A plaque said “Eternal glory to the fallen heroes 1941-1945” (a timeline that ignores the Soviet invasion and occupation of parts of Poland in 1939). Such Soviet monuments remained in many Polish towns and cities long after the fall of communism in 1989. In 2016, the then-ruling national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government introduced a law requiring local authorities to “decommunise” public spaces by removing objects and names that “propagate communism”. However, only in 2022, after Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, did the removal of Soviet-era monuments gather pace, with dozens demolished since then. Those efforts were led by the IPN, in particular during the time that the institute was headed by Karol Nawrocki between 2021 and last year, when he was elected president of Poland. Another Soviet memorial has been demolished in Poland – the 43rd since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. "We say ‘no’ to Russians who believe these lands somehow belong to their sphere of influence,” declared the Institute of National Remembrance https://t.co/aG9VQVlUQI — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) December 12, 2025 At the start of this year, the local authorities in Pyrzyce began public consultations on removing their Soviet memorial, finding that a majority were in favour of the move, according to the IPN. In February, the town council voted to remove the monument. It will now be replaced with a new one commemorating Polish independence. “We are aware that this change evokes various, often very strong, emotions among residents,” wrote the local authorities on social media. “We respect both the voices of those supporting the actions taken and those who differ in their assessment of the current monument and its place in the history of Pyrzyce.” “We hope that independence – as a paramount value for all Poles – will unite residents beyond differences of opinion and assessment of the past. We want the emerging space to be a space of shared remembrance, reflection, and a dignified celebration of the most important national ceremonies.” The removal of the monument drew condemnation from the Russian embassy in Warsaw, which announced on Monday that it had lodged a formal protest. It called the decision the “latest sacrilegious step by the Polish authorities” and said that it “constitutes a direct and flagrant violation” of a 1994 agreement between Poland and Russia on respect for graves and other places of memory. “The illegal dismantling of monuments is an overt attempt to falsify history, to erase from the consciousness of the Polish nation the memory of the heroism of Soviet soldiers,” added the embassy. ⚡️Komentarz Ambasady Rosji w Polsce 31 lipca 2026 r. w Pyrzycach (województwo zachodniopomorskie) na podstawie decyzji władz polskich został przeprowadzony demontaż pomnika ku czci poległych w latach 1941–1945 bohaterów – żołnierzy radzieckich. ❗️Ten kolejny świętokradczy krok… pic.twitter.com/cKhfFxIL9s — Russian Embassy, PL (@rusemb_pl) August 3, 2026 In response to such complaints from Russia, Poland has regularly pointed out that the 1994 agreement relates to graves and war cemeteries, not separate monuments and symbols, which can be legally removed. The IPN notes that such monuments were “Soviet propaganda objects”, designed to support the Moscow-backed communist regime, rather than genuine places of commemoration. Attending the demolition ceremony in Pyrzyce on Friday, IPN deputy president Karol Polejowski pointed out that the final version of the monument had been established in 1984 shortly after the period of martial law in Poland, when the authorities brutally clamped down on the democratic opposition. “Local communist activists, eager to curry favour with their Soviet masters, erected a monument honouring the Soviet army. This is not a symbol of liberation – it is a symbol of enslavement!” he declared, as the monument was torn down. 💪 Sowiecki obiekt propagandowy zostanie zastąpiony przez Pomnik Niepodległości, a przestrzeń wokół nowego monumentu stanie się godną sceną dla uroczystości patriotycznych. pic.twitter.com/5x4KEzG3Vb — Instytut Pamięci Narodowej (@ipngovpl) July 31, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Poland’s WIG20 stock market index hits record high
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s blue-chip WIG20 stock market index hit its highest ever level on Monday, surpassing a record that had stood for almost 19 years. The WIG20 has been Europe’s best-performing major blue-chip index so far this year. According to market monitoring website MarketScreener, the index has gained just under 25% since the start of 2026, ahead of the Dutch AEX (16.9%) and Sweden’s OMX Stockholm (14.9%). The WIG20, which tracks the 20 largest and most liquid companies on the Warsaw Stock Exchange (GPW), climbed to 3,963.21 points on Monday, breaking its previous record of 3,940.53 points set in October 2007. It continues a rally that began in October 2022, since when the index has almost tripled in value. “The market continues to be supported by solid economic growth, rising consumer spending, and the prospect of further EU investment,” commented analysts from BNP Paribas, a bank, quoted by business daily Parkiet. “However, after such strong gains, we do not expect the pace of appreciation to remain as high as in recent years,” they added. On Monday, the biggest boosts to the WIG20 index were provided by PGE, Poland’s biggest power producer, and KGHM, a Polish multinational mining company, with their shares rising 3.3% and 1.6%, respectively. The surge was also supported by improving risk appetite across global markets following signs of a de-escalation in tensions in the Middle East. This has pushed WIG20 above the levels last seen 19 years ago, just before the index plunged almost 70% during the 2008 global financial crisis, and then suffered another sell-off during the euro zone debt crisis in 2011. Reform of one of the pillars of Poland’s pension system in 2014, which reduced the role of open pension funds, ushered in years of market stagnation and left the index struggling to meaningfully rebound in the following years. Another decline came during the COVID-19 pandemic and then in the aftermath of Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. In October 2022, however, the WIG20 started its rebound, rising by 195% since then. More than 30 Polish-listed companies have doubled in value over the past three years, including large-cap stocks such as Orlen, PKO BP, Bank Pekao, KGHM and Tauron, according to an analysis by economic journalist Rafał Hirsch published by news service WNP. Polish state energy firm Orlen has seen its market valuation rise to its highest ever level, and surpass Russia’s Gazprom for the first time https://t.co/w3po4izshJ — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 12, 2026 BNP Paribas’s analysts, however, note that, “despite a long-term upward trend and reaching record highs”, the Polish stock market “is still valued below many other European markets”. “Our stock market…remains significantly cheaper than the US market and most European markets, but at the same time, when viewed against its own historical performance, it is now relatively highly valued,” they said. Poland’s main stock index, the broader WIG, also closed on Monday at a record high of 148,428 points, having hit several records in recent months. Poland’s benchmark WIG stock index has passed the 100,000-point mark for the first time. Meanwhile, the Warsaw Stock Exchange has been the world’s best performing so far this year "It is a clear signal of the strength of our economy," says the PM's office https://t.co/fIgGWOLLn8 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) April 25, 2025 Analysts warn, however, that unlike in the case of WIG, the WIG20’s record may prove short-lived because the benchmark is a price index, which excludes dividends. When companies in the index pay dividends, their share prices usually fall by about the same amount, which automatically pulls the index down even if nothing has changed in the companies themselves. Monday was the last day investors could buy shares in PKO BP and qualify for this year’s dividend. From Tuesday, the bank’s shares will trade ex-dividend, a move expected to reduce the WIG20 by about 0.8% because of PKO BP’s large weighting in the index.
