World.title: US dollar exchange rate continues to rise in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar compared to the Iraqi dinar rose on Thursday in the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, and the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq, Erbil.

The US dollar exchange rate slightly rose in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,523.5 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,520.5 Iraqi dinars on Thursday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,530 Iraqi dinars and 1,520 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate also rose, fluctuating between 1,525.5 and 1,525 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation indicated a difference of over 10 percent in the exchange rates.

World.title: Iraq to increase production from Kirkuk oil fields
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair announced on Thursday plans to increase oil production from the Kirkuk oilfields.

The decision intends to capitalize on a recent agreement with Turkey for exporting oil to the port of Ceyhan.

This move also aims to circumvent the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and increase Iraq’s oil exports via ports on the Mediterranean.

The instruction utilizes the recently expanded Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline deal, with the goal of increasing exports from 180,000 barrels per day to approximately 750,000 barrels per day.

Khudair stated that increasing production lays the groundwork for boosting export volumes through Turkey to 1.5 million barrels per day.

Turkish Petroleum Corporation (TPAO) has officially partnered with British Petroleum (BP) to bolster cooperation in oil and natural gas projects in Kirkuk oilfields.

In 2025, BP reached a deal with Iraq’s North Oil Company (NOC) to develop oil fields in the northern Iraqi province of Kirkuk, with investments projected to reach $25 billion.

The step is part of the Iraqi government’s attempts to optimize energy sector investments, increase oil output, and minimize gas flaring.

The enhanced output directly addresses the Iraqi government’s growing deficit as a result of continued maritime restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz.

By producing more petroleum from Kirkuk, Baghdad reduces internal shipping expenses from southern fields while increasing supplies to global markets via outlets on the Mediterranean.

World.title: Iraqi Prime Minister orders higher military readiness as security tensions rise
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces Ali Al-Zaidi has directed all security and military formations to raise their operational readiness and combat preparedness, according to the Security Media Cell.

The directive aims to maintain a high state of preparedness across Iraq’s security forces through intensified training exercises and operational movements designed to strengthen national security and protect public interests.

In a statement, the Security Media Cell said the Commander-in-Chief instructed security and military forces to increase their level of readiness while conducting training exercises and field movements.

The measures are intended to ensure that all security formations remain fully prepared to carry out their assigned duties and respond to potential security developments.

According to the statement, the directive is part of ongoing efforts to maintain continuous operational readiness across Iraq’s armed forces.

The Security Media Cell said the enhanced readiness program is designed to reinforce Iraq’s security framework and improve the capabilities of military and security units.

Officials stated that maintaining high readiness contributes to:

Strengthening national security.

Preserving public stability.

Protecting Iraqi citizens.

Safeguarding public institutions and national interests.

The government has increasingly emphasized preparedness amid evolving regional security challenges.

The announcement comes during a period of elevated security concerns in Iraq following recent regional developments and heightened tensions involving armed groups.

The official statement, however, does not specify any particular threat or military operation linked to the readiness order.

Some media reports and political analysts have suggested the move may be connected to broader security developments or precautionary planning ahead of upcoming government deadlines. These assessments are analytical interpretations and were not included in the official Security Media Cell statement.

The latest directive reflects Baghdad’s continued focus on ensuring the operational effectiveness of Iraq’s security institutions.

By ordering additional training activities and maintaining high alert levels, the government aims to preserve stability while ensuring security forces remain prepared to respond to any developments affecting the country’s security environment.

World.title: Iraqi Drilling Company completes well rehabilitation at West Qurna 1 oil field
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Drilling Company (IDC) has successfully completed the rehabilitation of oil well WQ1-132 at the West Qurna 1 oil field, marking another step in Iraq’s efforts to enhance oil production efficiency and support the long-term development of its energy sector.

The project was carried out as part of the company’s operational program to improve well performance and maintain sustainable crude oil production.

According to a statement issued by the Iraqi Drilling Company, the rehabilitation work was completed in line with directives from Oil Minister Bassem Mohammed Khudair Al-Abadi and under the supervision of the company’s Director General, Mohammed Hantoosh Asad Al-Azirjawi.

Technical and engineering teams carried out the operation using the company’s specialized expertise and equipment.

The company said the rehabilitation project forms part of its broader strategy to improve the efficiency of existing oil wells while supporting sustainable production across Iraq’s major oil fields.

Restoration work on producing wells helps maximize output, extend operational life, and improve field performance without the need for entirely new drilling operations.

The Iraqi Drilling Company emphasized that the successful completion of the project reflects the capabilities of its engineering and technical staff, who continue to execute specialized rehabilitation operations according to approved operational plans.

The company noted that relying on local expertise strengthens operational efficiency while supporting the continued development of Iraq’s oil infrastructure.

West Qurna 1 is one of Iraq’s largest producing oil fields and plays a significant role in the country’s crude oil output.

Ongoing rehabilitation and maintenance projects are designed to ensure production stability, improve operational reliability, and meet the technical requirements of field development programs.

The completion of well WQ1-132 is expected to contribute to maintaining efficient production operations within the field as Iraq continues investing in the modernization of its energy sector.

World.title: Iraqi PM, Kurdistan president discuss Erbil-Baghdad cooperation
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and the president of the Kurdistan region of Iraq, Nechirvan Barzani, discussed on Wednesday the country’s political, economic, and security situation.

During their meeting in Baghdad, the two leaders indicated that it is important to boost cooperation between the federal government and the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) to enhance stability, address challenges, and serve the interests of the Iraqi people, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

Al-Zaidi affirmed the government’s commitment to resolving outstanding issues in line with the constitution, preserving Iraq’s unity, and strengthening national partnership.

Barzani stated that it is important to continue dialogue between national parties. He added that the KRG supports the federal government’s efforts to enhance stability and promote national development.

The discussions focused on approaches to secure the success of the government’s national agenda.

This high-level meeting comes after al-Zaidi’s trips to Turkey and Iran, where he met top officials, and Barzani’s visit to Damascus, where he met with Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa.

World.title: Iraq wins legal case in Jordan for Samarra Pharmaceutical Company
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Ministry of Justice has announced a legal victory before the Jordanian judiciary after securing a final court ruling in favor of the State Company for Drug Industries and Medical Appliances in Samarra, a subsidiary of the Ministry of Industry and Minerals.

The ruling requires a Jordanian company to pay financial compensation following a dispute over the supply of medical materials that failed to meet agreed specifications.

According to a statement from the Ministry of Justice, the ministry’s Legal Department successfully represented the Iraqi pharmaceutical company throughout all stages of the legal proceedings before Jordanian courts.

The case involved a supply contract under which the Jordanian company was expected to provide metal covers for medical supplies. However, the supplier allegedly delivered products that did not comply with the contractual specifications.

Director of the Legal Department, Haitham Mohi Radi, said the final judgment issued by the Jordanian Court of Cassation, and upheld by both the Court of Appeal and the Court of First Instance, ordered the Jordanian company to pay financial amounts to the Samarra-based pharmaceutical company.

The ruling concludes a lengthy legal process aimed at protecting the contractual rights of the Iraqi state-owned enterprise.

The Ministry of Justice described the outcome as an important achievement in safeguarding Iraq’s financial interests abroad.

Officials said the successful litigation reflects the ministry’s continued efforts to defend state institutions before international courts and judicial authorities while protecting public funds from contractual violations.

The ministry added that the case demonstrates the expertise and professionalism of Iraq’s legal teams in handling international commercial disputes.

By successfully pursuing the claim through multiple judicial levels in Jordan, the Legal Department reinforced Iraq’s commitment to enforcing contractual rights and ensuring accountability in cross-border commercial agreements.

The decision is expected to strengthen confidence in the government’s ability to defend the interests of Iraqi public institutions through legal channels.

World.title: Ammar Al-Hakim and Iranian Science Minister discuss academic cooperation
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The head of Iraq’s National State Forces Alliance, Ammar Al-Hakim, met with Iranian Minister of Science, Research and Technology Hossein Simaei Sarraf in Baghdad to discuss expanding academic cooperation between Iraq and Iran through university partnerships, knowledge exchange, and joint educational initiatives.

The meeting focused on strengthening higher education ties while emphasizing the role of universities in addressing labor market needs and societal challenges.

According to a statement released by Al-Hakim’s office, the two sides reviewed opportunities to deepen cooperation between Iraqi and Iranian universities by promoting twinning agreements, expanding academic collaboration, and exchanging expertise.

The discussions highlighted the importance of strengthening institutional relationships to support scientific research and educational development in both countries.

During the meeting, Al-Hakim stressed that university graduates should possess skills that match the demands of today’s job market.

He also urged academic institutions to prioritize scientific research that offers practical solutions to national challenges and contributes to sustainable development.

Al-Hakim emphasized the importance of equipping university students with strong scientific knowledge to prepare them for future professional opportunities.

The Iraqi political leader underscored the role of research institutions in supporting innovation and policymaking.

He noted that universities should focus on producing research capable of addressing economic, social, and developmental issues while enhancing academic excellence.

The discussion reflected a shared interest in strengthening educational cooperation as part of broader bilateral relations.

The meeting also touched on the annual Arbaeen pilgrimage, with Al-Hakim praising the hospitality shown by Iraqis toward visitors traveling to commemorate Imam Hussein.

He said the event demonstrates positive values of solidarity and cooperation, while calling for stronger ties between societies based on shared humanitarian and religious principles.

The visit concluded with discussions on enhancing educational cooperation alongside broader people-to-people engagement between Iraq and Iran.

World.title: Iraq’s State Administration Coalition warns armed groups after September 30
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s State Administration Coalition has reaffirmed its support for restricting all weapons to state control, warning that any armed activity outside the authority of the government after September 30, 2026, will be treated under the country’s Anti-Terrorism Law.

The position was announced following the coalition’s 37th regular meeting, hosted by Prime Minister Ali Falih Al-Zaidi, with the participation of Iraq’s senior political and constitutional leaders.

According to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office, the meeting brought together the President of the Republic, the Speaker of Parliament, the President of the Supreme Judicial Council, the President of the Kurdistan Region, and leaders of the State Administration Coalition.

Participants reviewed Iraq’s political, security, economic, and public service developments, as well as regional events and their impact on the country.

The coalition reiterated its backing for the government’s efforts to ensure that all weapons remain under state authority, in line with the government program approved by the Iraqi Parliament.

The coalition stressed that Iraqi territory must not be used as a launchpad for attacks against neighboring countries or for actions that could draw Iraq into regional conflicts.

It warned that individuals or groups engaging in such activities would be committing crimes that threaten national security.

According to the statement, after September 30, 2026, any armed activity conducted outside the state’s legal framework will be dealt with under Iraq’s Anti-Terrorism Law.

Officials also cited constitutional provisions prohibiting the formation of armed organizations outside the official security forces.

Prime Minister Al-Zaidi briefed coalition members on government efforts to strengthen security, improve public services, implement the ministerial program, and address Iraq’s financial and economic challenges.

The coalition emphasized the need to:

Maintain national security and stability.

Protect essential public services.

Diversify Iraq’s oil export routes.

Increase non-oil revenues.

Combat corruption, smuggling, and financial waste.

The meeting highlighted the government’s commitment to protecting citizens’ interests while strengthening economic resilience.

On regional affairs, coalition leaders expressed support for diplomatic efforts aimed at reducing tensions across the Middle East.

The meeting reaffirmed Iraq’s rejection of resolving disputes through military force and emphasized Baghdad’s willingness to play a constructive role in promoting dialogue between regional parties.

Participants also discussed border security, counterterrorism cooperation, combating drug trafficking and organized crime, and strengthening relations with neighboring and international partners based on mutual respect and national sovereignty.

At the conclusion of the meeting, the State Administration Coalition called for accelerating the completion of the government formation process and submitting the government’s official program to the Council of Representatives for discussion and approval.

The coalition said completing these constitutional steps remains essential for advancing Iraq’s political stability and governance agenda.

World.title: Karnataka legislative council chairman Basavaraj Horatti resigns
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

leader Basavaraj Horatti on Friday tendered his resignation as Chairman of the

Legislative Council.

Asked about the reason behind his decision, Horatti said, "I was asked to resign, so I tendered my resignation."

"I don't know why they (the Congress government) asked me to resign," he added.

Horatti also admitted that he was under pressure to resign.

Horatti, who was previously with the Janata Dal (Secular), joined the BJP on May 18, 2022, a year before the Congress came to power in Karnataka.

He said the Congress government, led by D K Shivakumar, mounted pressure on him ahead of the Legislative Council session beginning on August 13.

went from Parliament to Gotham, at least on Instagram, when a playful Batman question landed in his Gen Z-focused âAsk Me Anythingâ session on Thursday. Gandhi launched the AMA session on Instagram, inviting young people to question him on subjects ranging from student protests and education to politics and philosophy. Gandhi's Gen Z outreach comes as political leaders increasingly turn to social media to connect with younger audiences.

World.title: Govt bars firms filing fake drug data from seeking fresh approvals
World.content:
Govt bars firms filing fake drug data from seeking fresh approvals. (Photo: IANS)

NEW DELHI:

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

In a major crackdown on regulatory fraud in the pharmaceutical sector, the Centre has amended the Drugs Rules, 1945 to empower drug regulators to temporarily debar companies that submit fake or fabricated data while seeking approvals for drugs and related licences.Under the amended rules notified by the Union health ministry on Thursday, applicants found submitting fabricated data will not only face rejection of their applications or cancellation of existing licences, but can also be barred from filing fresh applications before the concerned licensing authority, whether at the Centre or in the states, for a specified period. The action will be taken only after issuing a show-cause notice, and affected applicants will have the right to appeal.The new provision will apply to all applications filed under the Drugs Rules, 1945, and is aimed at deterring companies from submitting false scientific data to secure regulatory approvals.The ministry said regulatory decisions on the quality, safety and efficacy of medicines are based on scientific data submitted by applicants. Fabricated data undermines the integrity of the approval process, raises questions about the quality of medicines and can pose serious risks to public health.The amendment is intended to strengthen accountability and ensure that drug approvals are backed by reliable scientific evidence.Officials said the amendment is part of the government's broader effort to align India's drug regulatory framework with global best practices by promoting ethical compliance while taking stricter action against companies that indulge in malpractice.

World.title: BJP MLAs storm well, disrupt Jharkhand assembly over exam irregularities
World.content:
Jharkhand assembly adjourned amid BJP uproar over job exam irregularities

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Opposition BJP MLAs disrupted proceedings of the Jharkhand Assembly over alleged irregularities in a job examination, with several legislators entering the well of the House in protest.Proceedings of the Jharkhand Assembly were adjourned till 12.30 pm amid an uproar by the BJP MLAs.During the proceedings, BJP leader Babulal Marandi demanded a CBI probe into the alleged irregularities under a court-monitored panel.Opposition MLAs raised placards and shouted slogans, including "stop selling students' future" and "recommend a CBI probe into irregularities in JPSC examination", targeting the JMM-led government.BJP chief whip Naveen Jaiswal alleged that the CID probe into the suspected job exam scam had been initiated to "cover up the issues"."It is an eyewash. The youth doesn't have faith in the CID probe. The protesters will get justice only when a CBI team probes into the irregularities raised by the protesters," Jaiswal said, as cited by PTI.The protest over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations in Jharkhand entered its 14th day on Friday, with six demonstrators continuing their hunger strike.Meanwhile, two student unions announced plans to march to the state Assembly, which is currently in session, during the day.The demonstrators have been demanding the cancellation of the 14th Jharkhand PSC Civil Services Examination and an independent probe into the alleged irregularities in the recruitment test, either by the CBI or by a panel of retired High Court judges from outside the state.They have also called for comprehensive reforms in the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and the Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC).The protest began on July 25 at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium under the banner of the JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch and has since emerged as one of the biggest student-led movements in the state in recent years.The CID has so far arrested 19 people in connection with the alleged irregularities in the job examination.

World.title: India, China agree to use diplomatic, military channels to avoid LAC misunderstandings: MEA
World.content:
NEW DELHI: India and China reviewed the overall situation along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) and held detailed discussions on boundary delimitation, border management and trans-border cooperation during the 36th meeting of the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination (WMCC) on India-China Border Affairs in New Delhi.

"The two sides engaged in frank discussions and reviewed the situation along the LAC," the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said on Friday, a day after the meeting.

The MEA said both sides underlined that maintaining peace and tranquillity in the border areas is essential for the overall development of bilateral relations.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

"Both sides agreed to continue to use existing diplomatic and military channels, including the WMCC, local commander-level meetings and other agreed mechanisms, to resolve outstanding issues and avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation along the LAC," the ministry said.

The discussions followed up on the outcomes of the 24th Special Representatives' talks, with both sides holding detailed exchanges on issues related to boundary delimitation, border management, mechanism-building and trans-border cooperation.

The Indian side also reiterated the need for an early meeting of the Expert Level Mechanism on trans-border rivers and stressed the importance of sharing technical details on upstream projects, the MEA said.

World.title: 'Power Banks' for satellites? Bengaluru Company builds tech to keep ageing spacecraft alive
World.content:
BENGALURU: What if satellites could simply plug into a power bank instead of drifting away when they run out of fuel? Thatâs the idea driving a Bengaluru startup building âjetpackâ satellites designed to latch onto ageing spacecraft, take over their propulsion duties and keep billion-dollar assets working years longer.

After recently validating a key part of its technology at an Isro facility used for Indiaâs SpaDeX docking mission, Aule Space is now preparing for what could become one of the worldâs most ambitious private satellite docking demonstrations.

Aule 2: Dark room hardware test setup where the team recreated on-orbit lighting conditions with a sun simulator and a target mounted on a robotic arm to simulate the targetâs motion.

For satellite operators, running out of fuel doesnât necessarily mean spacecraft have reached the end of life. In many cases, expensive communication satellites remain fully functional, but can no longer maintain their assigned orbital positions because they have exhausted the propellant needed for station-keeping.

Once that happens, operators are forced to retire assets worth hundreds of millions of dollars.

Aule has found another way. âWeâre trying to build satellites which can go and dock to existing satellites in space which donât have any installed ports... and extend their life so that they can keep generating revenue,â CEO Jay Panchal, told TOI. âItâs like a power bank,â he added.

Instead of attempting the far more complicated task of refuelling satellites in orbit, Auleâs approach is to send a smaller âjetpackâ spacecraft that docks with an existing communications satellite and assumes responsibility for station-keeping using its own propulsion system.





The company plans to target geostationary communication satellites, many of which cost more than $300 million to build and generate significant annual revenues.

The challenge lies in docking with satellites that were never designed to be serviced. Rather than relying on dedicated docking ports, Aule will attach its spacecraft to the liquid apogee motor (LAM) nozzle, a standard external feature found on most geostationary satellites.

If successful, the technology could help operators extract years of additional service from satellites that would otherwise become orbital relics. Panchal said each docked âjetpackâ could extend a satelliteâs operational life by up to 5 years.

*Key Test Done*

The startup recently completed a major milestone by testing its camera-based guidance, navigation and control system at the Rendezvous Simulation Laboratory (RSL) at Isroâs ISITE â the same lab where critical elements of the SpaDeX were validated.

âWe were the first non-govt entity to access RSL. This is the best kind of on-ground testing we can do for these capabilities,â Panchal said.

One of Auleâs differentiators is its reliance on computer vision instead of multiple specialised sensors. Current docking systems typically use LiDAR, infrared cameras and other sensors. Aule says its spacecraft will perform the critical final approach using a single optical camera powered by onboard AI.

The visual navigation models are trained using data generated in its own facilities and validated at Isroâs testbed before being deployed in orbit.

The company is targeting an in-orbit demonstration next year, when it plans to launch two satellites that will autonomously dock in low-Earth orbit. Panchal claims it could be the worldâs first private mission to perform non-cooperative docking in LEO using camera-only navigation. The mission will validate technologies that Aule ultimately intends to deploy around geostationary communication satellites.

World.content:
Students protest in Ranchi's Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium.

BJP MLAs protest outside Assembly

Rahul Gandhi speaks to aspirants

11-member delegation finalised

Officials reach protest site

'Assembly gherao' on Monday

Minister claims 19 arrested

NEW DELHI: The protest by JPSC and JSSC aspirants in Jharkhand entered its 14th day on Thursday, with students demanding action over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations, while political pressure on the Hemant Soren government intensified.The protest, launched on July 25 under the JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch at Ranchi's Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium, has grown into one of Jharkhandâs largest student-led movements in recent years. Protesters are seeking cancellation of the 14th JPSC Civil Services Preliminary Examination, an independent probe into alleged irregularities, and comprehensive reforms in the JPSC and JSSC. Here are the top developments:BJP MLAs on Thursday staged a protest outside the Jharkhand Assembly, on the first day of the Monsoon Session, over alleged irregularities in the state competitive examinations.Speaking to ANI, BJP MLA Alok Chaurasia said, "The Bharatiya Janata Party stands firmly and vocally with the students regarding the functioning of Jharkhand government agencies such as JPSC, JSSC, and CJL, as well as the widespread corruption across the state, particularly the fraud committed against students..."The legislators raised slogans against the government, with chief whip Naveen Jaiswal alleging it was "selling" Jharkhand's youths' future and demanding a CBI probe, saying, "nobody trusts your CID and committee."Congress leader Rahul Gandhi spoke to JPSC-JSSC aspirants over the phone on Thursday. Student leader Piyush Kumar said the students raised their demand for cancellation of the examination, an investigation and reforms."We told him of our demands, that exam should be cancelled, regarding investigation and reforms. He said that he stands with our demands, and that they will take it up with the Govt. He said that he stands with and supports students...We are yet to get any official information regarding the date and time of meeting (with the government)," Kumar said.Student leader Ravindra Paswan said Gandhi enquired about the situation at the protest site."He asked us about the situation here. We told him about the irregularities in exams here. We told him that Congress is in the government in Jharkhand and they should help us. He told us that he stands with students," Paswan said.According to JPSC JSSC Reform Manch, protesting students have finalised an 11-member delegation for talks with the state government. The group comprises eight student representatives, one lawyer and two technical experts.The eight student representatives are Piyush Kumar Singh, Ravindra Paswan, Rajesh Prasad, Neetu Kujur, Kartik Soren, Ravindra, Ankit Kumar and Shalu Singh.Students have also demanded that any dialogue with the government be held in the presence of the media.Ranchi Sadar SDO Rajat Kumar and ADM Dhananjay Kumar reached Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium to hear the grievances of the protesting aspirants."We came to speak with our younger brothers about how we can assist them in their preparations for the future," Rajat Kumar said.A protester said there had been a suggestion that a four- or five-member delegation should participate in talks, but students insisted on a transparent process.Amid the continuing agitation, students announced a "Vidhan Sabha Gherao" on August 10 if their demands are not met. Protester Radhe Kumar said the decision was taken after the government initiated contact with the students.JMM MLA Jairam Kumar Mahato urged the government to immediately open talks, warning that "something untoward will happen" if the situation remains unresolved.Activist Sonam Wangchuk rejected reports that student leader Devendra Nath Mahato had ended his hunger strike after speaking with him. A total of six demonstrators are presently on a hunger strike.In a video message on X, Wangchuk said, "He consumed water, not food; I want to clarify this."He added, "He was fasting without water and without food, which is, in a way, like suicide. So, I only urged him to consume water and salt now and continue his fast."Mahato began his indefinite hunger strike on August 2 at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium. He is now continuing the fast on water and salt.Jharkhand minister Shilpi Neha Tirkey said on Thursday that the government was investigating the allegations and that 19 people had been arrested.

World.title: Rahul Gandhi flags Ken-Betwa tribal displacement; Centre forwards complaints to MP govt
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Union ministry of tribal affairs on Thursday told the Lok Sabha that it has received several representations raising concerns over the displacement of people due to the Ken-Betwa river-link project in Madhya Pradesh.

The ministry said it has forwarded the representations to the state government and the concerned district administrations for examination and appropriate action.

In a written reply to questions from Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi and Samajwadi Party MP Ajendra Singh Lodhi on the rehabilitation of tribal families affected by the project, compliance with the Forest Rights Act (FRA), and alleged evictions, the ministry said it had not received any complaints specifically claiming that compensation disbursed under the project had failed to reach beneficiaries.

The ministry, however, said it had received representations "raising issues of displacement" due to the project.

It added that the representations had been forwarded to the Madhya Pradesh government and the concerned district administrations for examination and appropriate action, while noting that the implementation of the Forest Rights Act (FRA) rests with state governments and Union Territory administrations.





Minister of state for tribal affairs Durgadas Uikey, in his written reply, said the representations had been referred to the state authorities. "These have been forwarded to the State Government of Madhya Pradesh and respective District Administrations for examination and necessary action," the reply said.

In its response, the ministry said the rehabilitation plan for Scheduled Tribe families affected by the Ken-Betwa river-link project was based on a proposal submitted by the National Water Development Agency in 2016.

Citing the 2016 proposal, the ministry said the project's first phase is expected to displace 1,913 families comprising 8,339 people, including 648 Scheduled Tribe families.

Responding to questions on gram sabha meetings under the Forest Rights Act (FRA), the ministry said it does not maintain centralised records of meeting dates, attendance, signatures, grievances related to consent, compensation and displacement, or the status of their disposal, as implementation of the law falls under the jurisdiction of state governments and Union Territory administrations.

The ministry added that it has repeatedly urged states and UTs to ensure that no eligible beneficiary is denied forest rights and to strictly comply with Section 4(5) of the FRA, which prohibits the eviction or removal of claimants from forest land under their occupation until the process of recognition and verification of their rights has been completed.

World.title: Basavaraj Horatti resigns as Karnataka Legislative Council Chairperson
World.content:
Karnataka Legislative Council Chairperson Basavaraj Horatti submitted his resignation from the post on August 7, making way for the Congress to have one of its own members to preside over the Upper House.

Congress has named its senior leader Saleem Ahmed as the candidate for the position. He is expected to be officially anointed Chairperson on August 14. Till such time, Mr. Horatti would continue as pro-tem Speaker.

There had been several rounds of talks with Mr. Horatti on the issue, with Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar taking the lead in an effort to persuade him to resign of his own volition to avoid the embarrassment of a no-confidence motion. Congress now enjoys a majority in the 75-member Legislative Council.

While the monsoon session of the Karnataka legislature starts on August 13, Mr. Horatti had on August 6 told mediapersons that he would address the Council about the circumstances of his resignation before stepping down. However, after another round of talks with Mr. Shivakumar and other legislators, he submitted his resignation on August 7.

Speaking after a meeting with Mr. Horatti, the Chief Minister said that he would be designated pro-tem Speaker as per procedure and would preside over the session on August 13, and officially resign thereafter on August 14.

Mr. Horatti said he would appoint the Deputy Chairperson and submit his resignation to him. Currently, the post of Deputy Chairperson is vacant after M.K. Pranesh lost his position following a legal battle, over counting of votes, to A.V. Gayatri Shante Gowda of the Congress. The resignation submitted by Mr. Horatti has been accepted by the Council Secretary, in the absence of the Deputy Speaker. Incidentally, Ms. Shante Gowda was sworn in by Mr. Horatti on August 7.

The opposition BJP has taken exception to the manner in which Mr. Horatti is being ‘forced’ to step down. It has also taken exception to Mr. Horatti going to the Chief Minister’s residence for a meeting.

Mr. Horatti brushed aside the criticism and said, “I met the Chief Minister to thank him for co-operating for this long. I will conduct the House on August 13, appoint a Deputy Speaker and tender my resignation formally.”

Former minister Umashree is the Congress’ nominee for the post of Deputy Chairperson.

An eight-time MLC, Mr. Horatti has been a member of the Legislative Council for 46 years. He has two years remaining in his current term.

World.title: CM N. Rangasamy to present Puducherry Budget on August 24
World.content:
Puducherry Chief Minister N. Rangasamy, who holds the Finance portfolio, will present the Union Territory’s annual Budget for 2026-27 on August 24, 2026, Pro-tem Speaker A. Anbalagan said on Friday (August 7, 2026).

Addressing a press conference in the UT to announce the convening of the second session of the 16th Puducherry Legislative Assembly, the Pro-tem Speaker said the proceedings of the House will commence with the customary address of the Lieutenant Governor on August 24.

The Lt. Governor will deliver his address at around 9. 30 a.m. and on the same day, at around 3 p.m., the Budget will be presented by the Chief Minister, he said. The Business Advisory Committee will decide on the number of days the Assembly will be in session, as well as on the other proceedings in the House, he said.

When asked about the Speaker’s election, Mr. Anbalagan said the government will announce the date for the same. Asked whether he was in contention for the Speaker’s post, as his party, the All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK), is a constituent of the ruling National Democratic Alliance in the UT, Mr. Anbalagan said he had expressed his interest in occupying the Speaker’s post.

To a query on whether he would contest in the event of an election, he said, “I will contest only if the Chief Minister desires so. I will not contest if the Chief Minister does not want me for the post.”

On his meeting with Union Home Minister and BJP leader Amit Shah in New Delhi last month, the Pro-tem Speaker said the meeting was purely a courtesy call.

World.title: Supreme Court seeks Centre's response on pleas challenging data protection law
World.content:
The Supreme Court on Friday (August 7, 2026) sought the Centre's response on a batch of pleas challenging amendments made to the Right to Information (RTI) Act through the Digital Personal Data Protection Act.

A Bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana heard submissions from senior advocate Vrinda Grover and advocate Prashant Bhushan before asking Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Centre, to file the government's response.

The pleas said the changes dilute transparency by removing the public interest safeguard for disclosure of personal information.

The petitions challenge the amendment to Section 8(1)(j) of the RTI Act, which deals with exemptions from disclosure of personal information.

World.title: Supreme Court dismisses plea for SIT probe in Justice Varma case
World.content:
The Supreme Court on Friday rejected a petition filed by a lawyer seeking Special Investigation Team (SIT) probe into the alleged discovery of burnt currency at the official residence of former Delhi High Court judge, Yashwant Varma, after a blaze in March last year.

Justice P.S. Narasimha observed orally that the petition filed by Ghanshyam Upadhyay was a shot at “cheap publicity”.

Mr. Upadhayay said the criminal liability related to the allegations surrounding the discovery of the burnt currency would survive the resignation of Justice Varma in April 2026. The lawyer contended that the resignation has deprived the former judge of any immunity from prosecution.

A three-member in-house committee of Punjab and Haryana High Court Chief Justice Sheel Nagu, Himachal High Court Chief Justice GS Sandhawalia and Karnataka High Court Justice Anu Sivaraman had submitted a fact-finding report to Chief Justice of India (now retired) Sanjiv Khanna on the incident in May 2025.

The CJI had asked Justice Varma to resign or face impeachment proceedings. The report was subsequently referred to the President of India and the Prime Minister by the CJI.

In August 2025, Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla constituted a committee to investigate the allegations. Justice Varma resigned from office before the committee gave its report.

World.title: How ‘AI sentries’ are bringing new hope to Kerala’s human-wildlife conflict zones
World.content:
Marking a major leap in human-wildlife conflict management, an AI-driven digital sentry system deployed across six high-risk forest zones in Kerala has achieved a near-100% success rate in repelling wild animals.

First piloted at Mankala coming under Paruthippally range of Thiruvananthapuram, the ‘Farmguard’ units were later expanded to five critical forest fringes in Kollam, Thrissur and Palakkad during the last couple of months. Early reports from field officials indicate an unprecedented success rate in deterring wild animal intrusions, prompting Forest authorities to consider rolling out the technology to more hotspots.

Acting as autonomous digital sentries, these units harness advanced machine learning, night-vision capabilities, and high-resolution cameras to distinguish between living creatures and inanimate objects.

“Positioned along perimeter lines, multi-directional camera setups continuously scan a radius of up to around 200 meters. The moment a target animal such as an elephant, wild boar, leopard, tiger, bear, or gaur steps into the monitored perimeter, the system’s integrated algorithms identify the specific species. It instantly triggers real-time alerts via SMS, WhatsApp, and Telegram to forest officials and Rapid Response Teams (RRTs),” says Thiruvananthapuram Divisional Forest Officer A. Shanavas.

Simulated threats

To safely drive animals back into the forest, the device uses a multi-frequency acoustic defence system loaded with over 100 audio patterns and specialised frequency profiles. Since animals can become accustomed to the warnings, the device cycles through simulated threats such machine gun fire, grenade blasts, and loud crowd noises along with low-frequency infrasound designed to mirror natural wildlife communication.

The villagers of Chippanchira in the Kulathupuzha range say the past two months have brought a long-awaited sense of calm as the newly installed system could effectively block elephant incursions.

“Earlier, the elephants would wander onto our main roads, knock down boundary walls, and destroy our crops. Since the system went live, those incursions have stopped,” says ward member Sheeba Sreekumar.

At present, forest authorities are strategically deploying the technology to reinforce vulnerable gap areas rather than attempting continuous, end-to-end boundary coverage. In Palakkad, field officers have utilised the units to bolster frequently broken entry and exit paths used by wild elephant herds.

“Since wild animals quickly grow accustomed to repetitive noises, it automatically alters the sound output, timing, and frequency during every encounter. This dynamic variation prevents target species from becoming familiarised with the device, effectively scaring them back,” says Subair N., Range Forest Officer, Alathur.

Practical challenges

Meanwhile, forest officials also point out some practical and logistical challenges along with the need for substantial budget allocations. The system operates most efficiently on flat terrains and clear sightlines, which are not consistent across Kerala’s undulating forest topography. While dense canopy cover can affect solar power generation, remote field conditions pose another issue.

Officials also point out that dust accumulation and regular wear on sensors require prompt technical servicing. While the short-term performance is proven, its long-term durability, maintenance requirements, and overall scalability across rugged forest terrains remain under evaluation.

The Jharkhand government on Friday (August 7, 2026) tabled a supplementary budget of ₹8,399 crore in the Assembly for the current 2026-27 fiscal, amid the Opposition’s protest over alleged irregularities in recruitment exams in the State.
